Capacity requirement in megawatts (MW) that must be met by resources located within a specific local reliability area or load pocket, due to transmission constraints.
reference: CAISO Local Capacity Technical Study, RTO/ISO Local Reliability Rules

description: Target loss of load probability expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.1 represents one day in ten years). NERC reliability standard threshold for acceptable risk of load shedding.
Net qualifying capacity in megawatts (MW) representing the effective capacity contribution of resources after applying derating factors for availability, intermittency, and transmission constraints.
reference: CAISO Tariff, CPUC Resource Adequacy Rules

description: Free-text notes providing additional context, assumptions, or special considerations for this capacity requirement (e.g., policy drivers, market conditions, planning assumptions).
Forecasted peak demand in megawatts (MW) for the planning period, representing the maximum expected load that must be served.
Planning reserve margin expressed as a percentage above peak demand, representing the target capacity cushion to ensure reliability (e.g., 15.0% means capacity must be 115% of peak demand).
Capacity requirement allocated to renewable energy resources (wind, solar, hydro, biomass) in megawatts (MW). Driven by Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) mandates and clean energy targets.

Capacity requirement allocated to thermal generation resources (coal, natural gas, nuclear) in megawatts (MW). Used for resource mix planning and diversification analysis.
Capacity adjustment in megawatts (MW) to account for transmission system constraints that limit the deliverability of generation capacity to load centers.
Unforced capacity requirement in megawatts (MW), representing capacity adjusted for expected forced outage rates. Used in PJM and other markets to account for resource reliability.

description: Reference to the newer forecast that supersedes this one. Nullable if this is the current active forecast. Supports forecast version lineage.
Forecasted price for ancillary services (regulation, spinning reserves, non-spinning reserves) in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Supports grid stability and frequency control cost modeling.
Timestamp when this forecast was approved by an authorized user. Distinct lifecycle event from creation and modification.
Forecasted capacity price in US dollars per megawatt-day. Represents the cost of ensuring resource adequacy and grid reliability through capacity markets.
Forecasted carbon price or carbon tax in US dollars per ton of CO2 equivalent. Used for environmental compliance cost modeling and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) analysis.
reference: EPA Clean Air Act - Emissions Trading

description: Forecasted coal price in US dollars per ton. Used for modeling generation costs for coal-fired power plants.
Timestamp when this forecast record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary values in this forecast (e.g., USD, CAD, EUR). Supports multi-currency operations for international utilities.
Statistical confidence level of the forecast expressed as a percentage (e.g., 80%, 90%, 95%). Indicates the probability that actual prices will fall within the forecasted range.
The last date for which this forecast is applicable. Defines the end of the forecast validity period. Nullable for open-ended forecasts.
The first date for which this forecast is applicable. Defines the beginning of the forecast validity period.
Business-readable identifier or code for this forecast run, used for tracking and referencing in reports and analysis.
The precise end timestamp of the interval for which this price forecast applies. Defines the interval boundary for time-series price data.
The precise start timestamp of the interval for which this price forecast applies. Used for interval-level LMP forecasting at hourly or sub-hourly resolution.

The methodology used to generate this forecast: fundamental (supply-demand modeling), statistical (time-series analysis), machine learning (AI/ML models), hybrid (combination), or expert judgment (analyst-driven).
Free-text notes or commentary from analysts regarding assumptions, limitations, or special considerations for this forecast. Supports transparency and decision-making context.
Name or identifier of the source system that generated this forecast (e.g., OpenLink Endur, proprietary forecasting tool, third-party vendor). Supports data lineage and audit.

Current lifecycle status of the forecast: draft (under development), approved (validated by analysts), published (released for operational use), superseded (replaced by newer forecast), or archived (historical record).
Classification of the forecast horizon: short-term (hours to days), mid-term (weeks to months), long-term (years), day-ahead market (DAM), real-time market (RTM), or seasonal planning.
reference: NAESB WEQ Standards - Wholesale Electric Quadrant

description: Indicates whether this forecast is used for developing hedging strategies and risk management in energy trading. True if used for hedging, False otherwise.
The duration of the forecast interval in minutes (e.g., 5, 15, 60). Supports configurable resolution for different market and planning needs.

business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Code
description: Code identifying the ISO or RTO market region for this forecast (e.g., CAISO, PJM, ERCOT, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP). Critical for market-specific price modeling.
Timestamp when this forecast record was last updated or modified. Supports change tracking and audit requirements.

business_glossary_term: Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) Calculation Flag
description: Indicates whether this forecast is used for LCOE calculations and generation asset economic analysis. True if used for LCOE, False otherwise.

business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Congestion Component (USD per MWh)
description: Forecasted congestion component of the LMP in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Reflects transmission constraints and grid congestion costs at this pricing node.

business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Energy Component (USD per MWh)
description: Forecasted energy component of the Locational Marginal Price in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Represents the marginal cost of serving the next increment of load at this location.

business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Loss Component (USD per MWh)
description: Forecasted loss component of the LMP in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Accounts for electrical losses in transmission from generation to load.

business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Total (USD per MWh)
description: Total forecasted Locational Marginal Price in US dollars per megawatt-hour. Sum of energy, congestion, and loss components. Primary price metric for market operations and economic dispatch.
Forecasted system load in megawatts for the interval or period. Key input assumption for price forecasting and economic dispatch modeling.
The type of energy market this forecast applies to: day-ahead market (DAM), real-time market (RTM), bilateral contract, or forward market.
Forecasted forward natural gas price in US dollars per million British thermal units. Critical input for generation cost modeling and LCOE calculations for gas-fired plants.
reference: NAESB WGQ Standards - Wholesale Gas Quadrant

description: Indicates whether this forecast is specifically used for PPA economic valuation and contract negotiation. True if used for PPA analysis, False otherwise.
Timestamp when this forecast was published and made available for operational decision-making, trading strategy, and planning activities.
Forecasted price for Renewable Energy Certificates in US dollars per certificate. Used for RPS compliance cost modeling and renewable energy valuation.
Forecasted renewable generation (wind, solar, hydro) in megawatts. Accounts for renewable intermittency and its impact on market prices.
Indicates whether transmission constraints are expected to be binding during this forecast interval. True if constraints are active, False otherwise. Impacts congestion component of LMP.
The weather scenario assumption underlying this price forecast: normal (historical average), hot, cold, extreme heat, extreme cold, or mild. Weather is a key driver of load and renewable generation.
Unique identifier for the energy price forecast interval record. Primary key for this table.
Reference to the parent energy price forecast run that generated this interval-level forecast. Links this interval to the overall forecast execution context.
Forecasted price for ancillary services in $/MWh. Includes regulation, spinning reserves, non-spinning reserves, and other grid reliability services.
Forecasted capacity price in dollars per megawatt-day ($/MW-day). Represents the cost of ensuring sufficient generation capacity is available to meet peak demand.
reference: ISO/RTO Capacity Market Rules, FERC Order 719

description: Timestamp when this forecast interval record was first created in the system. Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.
Source system or vendor that provided input data for this forecast interval. May reference ISO/RTO market data feeds, weather services, or internal systems.

business_glossary_term: Forecast Accuracy Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE)
description: Historical mean absolute percentage error for this model and interval type. Provides a measure of expected forecast accuracy based on past performance.
Statistical confidence level of the price forecast expressed as a percentage (0-100). Indicates the probability that actual prices will fall within the forecasted range.
Lower bound of the forecasted LMP price range in $/MWh. Represents the low end of the confidence interval for this forecast.
Upper bound of the forecasted LMP price range in $/MWh. Represents the high end of the confidence interval for this forecast.
Duration of the forecast interval in minutes. Common values include 5, 15, 30, or 60 minutes depending on market resolution.
The ending timestamp of the forecast interval. Represents the end of the time period for which this price forecast applies.
Sequential ordering of this interval within the parent forecast run. Used to maintain chronological order of forecast intervals.
The beginning timestamp of the forecast interval. Represents the start of the time period for which this price forecast applies.

business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Congestion Component Forecast
description: Forecasted congestion component of LMP in $/MWh. Represents the cost premium due to transmission constraints limiting power flow to this location.

business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Energy Component Forecast
description: Forecasted energy component of LMP in $/MWh. Represents the marginal cost of generating one additional MWh of electricity, excluding transmission congestion and losses.

business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Loss Component Forecast
description: Forecasted loss component of LMP in $/MWh. Represents the marginal cost of electrical losses in transmitting power to this location.
Forecasted total Locational Marginal Price in dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh). Represents the complete cost of energy at this location and time, including energy, congestion, and loss components.
Forecasted electrical load demand in megawatts for this interval and location. Load is a primary driver of energy prices.

The type of energy market for which this price forecast applies. Day-ahead market (DAM) forecasts next-day prices, real-time market (RTM) forecasts immediate dispatch prices, hour-ahead provides short-term forecasts, and forward represents longer-term contract prices.
The market zone or load zone in which this PNode is located. Used for aggregating prices across geographic regions.

Type of forecasting model used. Statistical models use time-series analysis, machine learning models use AI/ML algorithms, fundamental models use supply-demand economics, and hybrid models combine approaches.
Version identifier of the forecasting model used to generate this interval forecast. Enables tracking of model changes and performance over time.
Timestamp when this forecast interval record was last modified. Supports change tracking and audit requirements.
Forecasted natural gas price in dollars per million British thermal units ($/MMBtu). Natural gas prices are a key driver of electricity prices due to gas-fired generation.

Boolean flag indicating whether planned or forced generation or transmission outages are expected to impact prices during this interval.
Identifier for the pricing node (PNode) at which this energy price forecast applies. PNodes represent specific locations in the transmission grid where prices are calculated.
Human-readable name of the pricing node. Provides business-friendly identification of the location.

Timestamp when this forecast interval was published and made available to business users. Critical for audit trails and understanding forecast timing.
Forecasted price for Renewable Energy Credits in dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh). RECs represent the environmental attributes of renewable generation and are traded separately from energy.

Forecasted ambient temperature in degrees Fahrenheit for this interval. Temperature is a key driver of electricity demand and therefore prices.
Status of transmission constraints affecting this PNode during the forecast interval. Constraints drive congestion pricing.
Weather scenario classification used in this forecast. Different weather scenarios drive different load and price patterns.
Unique identifier for the fuel price assumption record. Primary key for the fuel price assumption entity.
Identifier of the baseline fuel price assumption against which this assumption is compared in sensitivity or scenario analysis. Supports variance analysis and risk quantification.

Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this fuel price assumption within planning systems and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) filings.

Source of the fuel price assumption data. Identifies whether the assumption is derived from EIA Annual Energy Outlook (AEO), internal forecasting models, third-party consultants, market forward curves, historical averages, or regulatory guidance.
Additional detail about the assumption source, such as specific EIA AEO edition, consultant name, or market data provider. Supports audit trail and assumption validation.
Current lifecycle status of the fuel price assumption. Tracks progression from draft through approval and eventual supersession by updated assumptions.

business_glossary_term: Carbon Intensity Kilograms Carbon Dioxide (CO2) per Million British Thermal Units (MMBtu)
description: Carbon dioxide emissions intensity of the fuel in kilograms CO2 per MMBtu. Used in emissions modeling, carbon cost calculations, and environmental compliance analysis.

business_glossary_term: Carbon Price per Ton Carbon Dioxide (CO2)

Statistical confidence level associated with the fuel price assumption, expressed as a percentage. Indicates the degree of certainty in the forecast based on historical volatility and market analysis.
Date and time when this fuel price assumption record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all fuel price values in this assumption record. Supports multi-currency planning for utilities operating across jurisdictions.

Specific delivery point or pricing node for the fuel assumption (e.g., pipeline interconnection, coal rail terminal, uranium enrichment facility). Used for transportation cost modeling and delivered fuel price calculation.
Assumed price of diesel fuel in US dollars per gallon. Used for backup generation, emergency peaking units, and distributed generation cost modeling.
Date from which this fuel price assumption becomes effective for use in generation dispatch modeling, procurement decisions, and infrastructure investment analysis.
Annual escalation rate applied to the fuel price assumption over the planning horizon, expressed as a percentage. Used to project future fuel costs in multi-year IRP and LCOE analysis.
Date after which this fuel price assumption is no longer valid for planning purposes. Supports assumption lifecycle management and prevents use of outdated data.
Assumed price of fuel oil in US dollars per gallon. Supports cost modeling for oil-fired peaking units and backup generation assets.
Type of fuel for which the price assumption applies. Supports generation dispatch cost modeling and Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) calculations.

Geographic region or market area to which this fuel price assumption applies (e.g., Henry Hub for natural gas, Powder River Basin for coal, regional ISO/RTO market). Supports location-specific cost modeling.

business_glossary_term: Heat Content Million British Thermal Units (MMBtu) per Unit
description: Average heat content of the fuel in MMBtu per physical unit (e.g., MMBtu per ton of coal, MMBtu per gallon of diesel). Used to convert physical fuel quantities to energy equivalents for dispatch modeling.
Reference identifier linking this fuel price assumption to a specific IRP filing or docket number. Supports regulatory compliance and assumption traceability in rate cases.
Version identifier of the forecasting model or methodology used to generate this fuel price assumption. Supports model governance and reproducibility.
Date and time when this fuel price assumption record was last modified. Tracks changes and updates to assumption data over time.

business_glossary_term: Natural Gas Price per Million British Thermal Units (MMBtu)
description: Assumed price of natural gas in US dollars per MMBtu. Used in generation dispatch cost modeling, combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) economics, and peaking unit cost analysis.
Free-text field for additional context, assumptions, caveats, or special considerations related to this fuel price assumption. Supports documentation and knowledge transfer.
End date of the planning period for which this fuel price assumption is applicable. Defines the temporal boundary for economic analysis and dispatch modeling.
Start date of the planning period for which this fuel price assumption is applicable. Supports long-term capacity planning and resource adequacy analysis.
Assumed fuel cost equivalent for renewable generation in US dollars per MWh. Typically zero for wind and solar; may reflect biomass or biogas fuel costs for renewable thermal generation.

Name of the planning scenario to which this fuel price assumption belongs (e.g., Base Case, High Gas Price, Low Gas Price, Renewable Acceleration). Used in IRP scenario modeling and sensitivity analysis.
Upper bound fuel price for sensitivity analysis and risk assessment. Represents optimistic or high-price scenario for stress testing generation economics and resource selection.
Lower bound fuel price for sensitivity analysis and risk assessment. Represents pessimistic or low-price scenario for stress testing generation economics and resource selection.
Assumed transportation cost per unit of fuel (e.g., dollars per MMBtu for gas pipeline, dollars per ton for coal rail). Added to base fuel price to calculate delivered cost at generation facility.

description: Assumed price of uranium in US dollars per pound of U3O8. Used in nuclear generation cost modeling and fuel cycle economic analysis.
Measure of historical price volatility for the fuel type, used in risk assessment and stochastic modeling. Higher values indicate greater price uncertainty and risk exposure.

FK to forecast.load_growth_assumption.load_growth_assumption_id — IRP scenarios are built on specific planning assumptions (load growth, fuel price). Must link for scenario reproducibility.
Name or identifier of the executive or committee that approved this scenario for inclusion in the IRP filing. Provides accountability and governance trail.
Timestamp when this scenario was formally approved for inclusion in the IRP filing. Marks transition from draft to official status.
Total planned battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity additions over the planning horizon for this scenario, measured in megawatts (MW). Critical for renewable integration and grid flexibility.

description: Assumed market structure for capacity procurement. None means vertically integrated utility; energy_only means no separate capacity payments; capacity_market means RTO/ISO capacity auction; hybrid means mixed approach.

None means no carbon constraint; state_target follows state renewable portfolio standard (RPS) or clean energy goals; federal_mandate assumes national policy; carbon_tax models explicit carbon pricing; cap_and_trade models emissions trading system.
reference: State RPS Legislation, EPA Clean Power Plan

description: Timestamp when this scenario record was first created in the system. Audit trail for scenario development lifecycle.
Assumed demand response (DR) program capacity credit in megawatts (MW) that can be counted toward resource adequacy. Represents load reduction capability from DR programs during peak periods.

Weighted average cost of capital (WACC) or discount rate used for net present value (NPV) calculations in this scenario, expressed as a percentage. Reflects utility cost of capital for investment analysis.
reference: Utility Financial Planning, State PUC Rate Case Orders

description: Assumed penetration of distributed energy resources (rooftop solar, battery storage, microgrids) as a percentage of total capacity by end of planning horizon. Impacts load forecast and grid planning.
reference: State Net Energy Metering (NEM) Policies, DERMS Planning

description: Assumed economic growth trajectory for the service territory. Low assumes slow GDP growth; reference uses consensus forecasts; high assumes robust expansion; recession models economic downturn impacts on load.

Assumed rate of transportation and building electrification (electric vehicles, heat pumps) over the planning horizon. Low assumes slow adoption; reference uses market forecasts; high assumes policy-driven acceleration.
reference: EIA Annual Energy Outlook, State Climate Action Plans

description: Cumulative annual energy savings from energy efficiency programs by the end of the planning horizon, measured in gigawatt-hours (GWh). Reduces forecasted energy requirements.
Timestamp when the IRP containing this scenario was filed with the state Public Utility Commission (PUC). Establishes regulatory record date.

Total planned fossil fuel generation capacity retirements (coal, natural gas, oil) over the planning horizon for this scenario, measured in megawatts (MW). Reflects decarbonization strategy and asset lifecycle management.
reference: Asset Management Lifecycle Plans, EPA Emissions Standards

description: FK to forecast.peak_demand_forecast.peak_demand_forecast_id — IRP scenarios reference peak demand forecasts for capacity planning. Critical for resource adequacy analysis.
Average annual load growth rate assumption for this scenario expressed as a percentage (e.g., 1.50 for 1.5% annual growth). Key driver for capacity planning and resource adequacy analysis.

Name and version of the capacity expansion or production cost modeling software used to develop this scenario (e.g., PLEXOS, Aurora, PROMOD, Encompass). Important for model transparency and reproducibility.
Timestamp when this scenario record was last modified. Tracks iterative refinement during IRP development process.

Assumed natural gas price path over the planning horizon. Low assumes sustained low prices; reference uses EIA or market consensus; high assumes supply constraints or carbon pricing; volatile models price uncertainty.

Average annual peak demand (MW) growth rate assumption for this scenario expressed as a percentage. May differ from energy growth due to load shape changes, electrification, or demand response programs.
Final year of the planning horizon covered by this scenario (typically 10-20 years from start). Four-digit year (e.g., 2043).
First year of the planning horizon covered by this scenario (typically current year or next year). Four-digit year (e.g., 2024).
State PUC docket or case number assigned to the IRP filing containing this scenario. Links scenario to regulatory proceeding for tracking and reference.

business_glossary_term: Loss of Load Expectation (LOLE) Reliability Metric
description: Loss of Load Expectation (LOLE) reliability metric for this scenario, typically measured in days per year. Industry standard is 0.1 days/year (one day in ten years). Demonstrates resource adequacy.

Total planned renewable generation capacity additions (solar, wind, hydro, biomass) over the planning horizon for this scenario, measured in megawatts (MW). Key metric for tracking renewable energy integration.
Target renewable energy percentage of total generation by the end of the planning horizon. Reflects state RPS requirements or utility commitments (e.g., 50.00 for 50% renewable by 2030).

Planning reserve margin target for resource adequacy expressed as a percentage above forecasted peak demand (e.g., 15.00 for 15% reserve margin). Ensures sufficient capacity to meet reliability standards.

Business identifier code for the scenario (e.g., BASE_2024, HIGH_GROWTH_2024, LOW_CARBON_2024). Used in regulatory filings and internal planning documents.

Detailed narrative description of the scenario including key assumptions, strategic rationale, and how it differs from other scenarios in the IRP. Used in regulatory filings and stakeholder presentations.
Descriptive name of the IRP scenario (e.g., Base Case, High Load Growth, Accelerated Decarbonization, Low Gas Price). Human-readable label for reports and presentations.
Additional notes, caveats, or technical details about the scenario that do not fit in other structured fields. Used for model documentation and knowledge transfer.

Current lifecycle status of the scenario. Draft indicates work in progress; under_review means internal stakeholder review; approved means executive sign-off; filed means submitted to PUC; archived means superseded by newer IRP.

Classification of the scenario within the IRP framework. Base represents the most likely case; sensitivity tests single variable changes; alternative explores different strategic paths; stress_test examines extreme conditions; bookend defines planning boundaries.
For sensitivity scenarios, identifies the specific variable being tested (e.g., natural gas price, load growth, carbon price, technology cost). Null for base case scenarios.
Summary of stakeholder comments and feedback received on this scenario during public comment periods or technical conferences. Documents stakeholder engagement process required by many state PUCs.

Assumed capital cost trajectory for new generation technologies (solar, wind, battery storage, gas turbines). Low assumes rapid cost declines; reference uses industry consensus; high assumes slower learning curves.
reference: NREL Annual Technology Baseline, Lazard LCOE

business_glossary_term: Total Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Emissions Million Tons

FK to generation.generating_unit.generating_unit_id — CEMS data is monitored per generating unit (each unit has its own CEMS stack). generating_unit_id is required for EPA Part 75 compliance reporting which is unit-level.

Boolean flag indicating whether emissions allowances must be surrendered for this reading under cap-and-trade compliance programs. True if allowance deduction is required, False if not required or if the unit is exempt.
The quantity of emissions allowances (in tons) deducted from the facility's allowance account to cover the emissions recorded in this reading. Only populated for cap-and-trade compliance programs.

The vintage year of the emissions allowances used to cover this reading. Allowances are typically issued for specific compliance years and may be banked or borrowed across years subject to program rules.
The ambient air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for temperature correction factors in emissions calculations.
The barometric pressure in inches of mercury (inHg) at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for pressure correction factors in emissions calculations.
The calculated carbon cost in US dollars associated with this emissions reading, based on allowance market prices or internal carbon pricing. Used for carbon cost accounting and financial planning.

business_glossary_term: CEMS (Continuous Emissions Monitoring System) Monitor ID
description: The unique identifier for the specific CEMS monitor that recorded this reading. Links to the physical monitoring equipment installed on the generating unit.

The environmental compliance program under which this emissions reading is reported. EPA_ARP (Acid Rain Program), RGGI (Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative), California_Cap_and_Trade, CSAPR (Cross-State Air Pollution Rule), MATS (Mercury and Air Toxics Standards), State_SIP (State Implementation Plan).

Overall data quality indicator for this emissions reading based on QA/QC test results and validation rules. Passed indicates the reading meets all quality standards, failed indicates quality issues, not_available indicates quality assessment is incomplete, conditionally_valid indicates the reading is usable subject to documented conditions.
The name of the source system that provided this emissions reading data. Typically ABB Ability Symphony Plus DCS, OSIsoft PI Historian, or direct CEMS data acquisition system.
The measured emission rate for the pollutant. Units depend on pollutant type and are specified in emission_rate_unit field.

The unit of measure for the emission rate. Common units include lbs/MMBtu (pounds per million British thermal units), lbs/hr (pounds per hour), tons/hr, kg/MWh (kilograms per megawatt-hour), g/kWh (grams per kilowatt-hour).
The date when this emissions reading was submitted to the EPA through ECMPS. Only populated when submitted_to_epa_flag is True.

business_glossary_term: Flow Rate (SCFH - Standard Cubic Feet per Hour)
description: The volumetric flow rate of exhaust gas in standard cubic feet per hour (SCFH) at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for total mass emissions calculations.

The primary fuel type being consumed by the generating unit during this emissions measurement. Used for emissions factor calculations and compliance program categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: coal|natural_gas|oil|biomass|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The gross electrical load output of the generating unit in megawatts (MW) at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for emissions rate calculations and compliance verification.
The total heat input to the generating unit in millions of British thermal units (MMBtu) during the measurement period. Used for emissions rate calculations and fuel consumption analysis.
The precise date and time when the emissions measurement was recorded by the CEMS (Continuous Emissions Monitoring System). This is the principal business event timestamp for the reading.
The moisture content percentage in the exhaust gas stream at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for dry-basis emissions rate calculations.

The operational status of the CEMS monitor at the time of the reading. Operational indicates normal functioning, calibration indicates the monitor was being calibrated, maintenance indicates scheduled maintenance, failed indicates equipment failure, out_of_service indicates the monitor was not in service.
Boolean flag indicating whether the generating unit was in operation during this measurement hour. True if operating, False if not operating. Used for compliance hour calculations.

The operating mode of the generating unit at the time of the emissions measurement. Baseload indicates continuous operation, cycling indicates variable operation, peaking indicates high-demand operation, startup/shutdown indicate transitional states, standby indicates ready but not generating.

business_glossary_term: ORISPL (Office of Regulatory Information Systems Plant Location) Code
description: The unique EPA-assigned ORISPL code identifying the power plant facility. This is the standard identifier used in all EPA emissions reporting systems.
The oxygen concentration percentage in the exhaust gas stream at the time of the emissions measurement. Used for combustion efficiency calculations and emissions rate corrections.
The type of pollutant measured in this reading. SO2 (Sulfur Dioxide), NOx (Nitrogen Oxides), CO2 (Carbon Dioxide), Hg (Mercury), PM (Particulate Matter), CO (Carbon Monoxide).

The quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) certification status of this emissions reading. Certified indicates the reading passed all QA/QC tests, provisional indicates temporary certification pending full testing, conditionally_valid indicates the reading is valid subject to conditions, invalid indicates the reading failed QA/QC, pending_certification indicates certification testing is in progress.
The date when the most recent QA/QC certification test was performed on the CEMS monitor that recorded this reading. Used to verify data quality and compliance with EPA testing requirements.
The timestamp when this emissions reading record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.
The timestamp when this emissions reading record was last updated in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.
The time period granularity for which this emissions reading is aggregated and reported to regulatory agencies. Hourly is the most granular level required by EPA Part 75.
The calendar quarter (1-4) in which this emissions reading occurred. Used for quarterly compliance reporting aggregation.
The calendar year in which this emissions reading occurred. Used for annual compliance reporting and allowance reconciliation.
The unique identifier for the exhaust stack or flue where the CEMS monitor is installed and from which emissions are measured. A single stack may serve multiple generating units.

Boolean flag indicating whether this emissions reading has been submitted to the EPA through the Emissions Collection and Monitoring Plan System (ECMPS). True if submitted, False if not yet submitted.

Boolean flag indicating whether this reading is substitute data rather than actual measured data. True if substitute data was used due to monitor downtime or failure, False if actual measured data. Substitute data is calculated using EPA-approved methodologies.
The EPA-approved methodology used to calculate substitute data when actual CEMS measurements are unavailable. Only populated when substitute_data_flag is True.

The total mass of pollutant emitted during the measurement period, calculated from emission rate and operating time. Units are typically pounds (lbs) or tons depending on pollutant type and reporting requirements.

business_glossary_term: Total Mass Emissions Unit of Measure (UOM)
description: The unit of measure for total mass emissions. Common units include lbs (pounds), tons (short tons), kg (kilograms), metric_tons.
The type of generating unit technology that produced this emissions reading. Used for emissions factor selection and compliance program applicability determination.

Indicator of data quality status for this fuel inventory record. Verified indicates quality-assured data, estimated for calculated or interpolated values, pending verification for preliminary data awaiting confirmation, failed validation for records with quality issues requiring correction.

Calculated number of days the current fuel inventory can support generation operations at average burn rate. Critical metric for fuel supply planning, generation availability forecasting, and risk management during supply disruptions.

Federal Energy Information Administration (EIA) unique plant identifier. Required for EIA Form 923 monthly fuel receipt and cost reporting. Links internal fuel inventory data to federal regulatory reporting requirements.

description: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Uniform System of Accounts code for fuel inventory accounting. Typically account 151 for fuel stock. Required for FERC Form 1 financial reporting and rate case filings.

Fixed carbon content of coal as a percentage by weight. Represents the solid combustible residue after volatile matter is driven off. Higher fixed carbon indicates higher energy content and coal rank. Critical for coal quality classification and heat rate calculations.
Date of the inventory position snapshot or receipt transaction. For positions, represents the as-of date for stock levels. For receipts, represents the date fuel was received at the facility.

Current status of the fuel inventory. Available for generation use, reserved for specific unit commitment, in transit from supplier, quarantined pending quality verification, or consumed (historical record). Supports inventory allocation and generation scheduling.

Supplier invoice number for the fuel receipt transaction. Links fuel deliveries to accounts payable, supports invoice reconciliation, and provides audit trail for financial controls per Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) requirements.

Timestamp when this fuel inventory record was last modified. Tracks data changes for audit purposes, supports change data capture for downstream analytics, and provides data freshness indicator for operational dashboards.

Nitrogen content of the fuel as a percentage by weight. Affects nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions formation during combustion. Critical for EPA air quality compliance, NOx emissions calculations, and selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system design.

description: Geographic origin or source location of the fuel. Examples include coal mine name and state, natural gas production basin, nuclear fuel fabrication facility, or biomass harvest region. Supports supply chain tracking and sourcing analysis.

Certificate or lab analysis number documenting fuel quality test results. Links to third-party laboratory reports for heat content, sulfur, moisture, and ash analysis. Provides audit trail for fuel quality assurance and contract compliance.

Quantity of fuel in inventory or received. Measured in tons for coal and biomass, Million British Thermal Units (MMBtu) for natural gas and oil, or fuel assemblies for nuclear fuel. Precision supports accurate fuel accounting and EIA reporting.

Precise date and time when fuel was received at the generation facility. Captured from weigh station, pipeline meter, or receiving dock systems. Supports just-in-time inventory management and delivery performance tracking.

Identifier of the operational system that originated this fuel inventory record. Examples include SAP Materials Management (MM), OSIsoft PI historian, plant fuel management system, or manual entry. Supports data lineage and system-of-record tracking.

Name of the fuel supplier or vendor for receipt transactions. Tracks fuel procurement sources for contract management, supplier performance evaluation, and supply chain risk assessment. Business-confidential supplier relationship data.

Total cost of the fuel inventory position or receipt transaction in US dollars. Calculated as quantity multiplied by unit cost, adjusted for energy content. Used for financial reporting, Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) and Operational Expenditure (OPEX) tracking, and regulatory rate case filings.

Type of fuel inventory transaction. Position represents current stock level, receipt captures incoming fuel deliveries, consumption tracks fuel burned for generation, adjustment handles inventory corrections, and transfer records inter-facility movements.

Method of fuel transportation for receipt transactions. Rail for coal unit trains, truck for short-haul deliveries, pipeline for natural gas, barge for waterway transport, or ship for international coal imports. Affects delivery costs and supply chain logistics.

Cost per unit of fuel expressed in dollars per Million British Thermal Units ($/MMBtu). Supports Operations and Maintenance (O&M) cost tracking, Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) analysis, and generation dispatch economics. Business-confidential pricing data.

Volatile matter content of coal as a percentage by weight. Indicates the portion of coal that vaporizes when heated. Affects ignition characteristics, flame stability, and combustion efficiency. Higher volatile matter improves combustion but may increase emissions.

Reference to a WAMS disturbance or oscillation event that this measurement is associated with. Null for routine measurements outside of event windows.
Real power flow in megawatts calculated from voltage and current phasors. Positive values indicate power flowing in the defined direction.
Apparent power in megavolt-amperes, the vector sum of active and reactive power. Represents total power flow magnitude.
NERC-registered balancing authority code for the control area where this PMU is located. Used for jurisdictional reporting and inter-BA coordination.
Phase angle of the current phasor in degrees relative to the system reference. Used to calculate power flow and detect phase imbalances.
Magnitude of the current phasor measured in amperes. Represents the RMS current flowing through the monitored circuit element.
Quality indicator for the PMU measurement data. Good indicates valid GPS-synchronized data; questionable indicates potential issues; invalid indicates data should not be used for analysis.
Name of the source system that provided this PMU measurement data. Typically the PDC system name or OSIsoft PI interface identifier.
Type of electrical equipment being monitored by this PMU measurement. Determines the interpretation and application of the phasor data.
Measured system frequency in Hertz at the PMU location. Nominal frequency is 60 Hz in North America or 50 Hz in other regions. Frequency deviations indicate generation-load imbalances.
Timestamp when this PMU measurement record was ingested into the Silver layer lakehouse. Used for data lineage and latency monitoring.
North American interconnection where this PMU is located. The four major interconnections operate asynchronously from each other.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the PMU device location in decimal degrees. Used for geospatial visualization and propagation analysis.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the PMU device location in decimal degrees. Used for geospatial visualization and propagation analysis.
Precise UTC timestamp of the synchrophasor measurement with microsecond resolution. GPS-synchronized time reference for wide-area situational awareness and event correlation.
Negative sequence component of the three-phase voltage in kilovolts. Indicates voltage imbalance and potential phase faults.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Protection and Control (PRC) 002 Registered
description: Indicates whether this PMU measurement point is registered for NERC PRC-002 disturbance monitoring compliance. Registered points must retain data for reportable disturbances.
Free-text field for operational notes, data quality annotations, or event context related to this PMU measurement record.
Damping ratio of the detected oscillation mode. Values below 0.03 indicate poorly damped oscillations requiring operator attention. Null if no oscillation detected.
Indicates whether an inter-area or local oscillation was detected in this measurement window by the WAMS analytics engine. Used for modal analysis and stability assessment.
Dominant oscillation frequency detected in Hertz. Typical inter-area oscillations range from 0.1 to 1.0 Hz. Null if no oscillation detected.
Reference to the PDC that aggregated and forwarded this PMU measurement. PDCs collect synchrophasor data from multiple PMUs for wide-area monitoring.
Indicates whether this PMU measurement stream is actively archived in the OSIsoft PI historian for long-term storage and analysis.
OSIsoft PI historian tag name where this PMU measurement stream is archived. Enables correlation with other SCADA and operational data in the PI system.
Version identifier of the PMU configuration frame active when this measurement was captured. Used to track configuration changes over time.
Overall synchronization status of the PMU device. Synchronized indicates the PMU is GPS-locked and producing valid time-aligned measurements.
Positive sequence component of the three-phase voltage in kilovolts. Represents the balanced component of the voltage phasor.
Ratio of active power to apparent power, ranging from -1.0 to 1.0. Indicates the efficiency of power transmission and the phase relationship between voltage and current.
Reactive power flow in megavolt-amperes reactive calculated from voltage and current phasors. Used for voltage control and power factor management.
Version number of this measurement record. Incremented if the record is corrected or reprocessed. Initial version is 1.
PMU reporting rate in frames per second. Common rates are 30, 60, or 120 FPS. Higher rates provide better temporal resolution for transient event analysis.

business_glossary_term: Rate of Change of Frequency (ROCOF) Hertz per Second (Hz/s)
description: Rate of change of frequency measured in Hz per second. High ROCOF values indicate rapid frequency excursions and potential grid instability events requiring immediate response.
Name of the substation where the PMU device is installed. Provides geographic and operational context for the measurement.
GPS time synchronization status. Locked indicates accurate GPS time; unlocked indicates loss of GPS signal; holdover indicates operating on internal clock.
Total harmonic distortion of the current waveform expressed as a percentage. Indicates non-linear load effects and power quality issues.
Total harmonic distortion of the voltage waveform expressed as a percentage. Measures power quality and the presence of harmonic frequencies.
Phase angle of the voltage phasor in degrees relative to the system reference. Critical for detecting angular separation and stability issues across the wide-area grid.
Nominal voltage level of the bus or circuit where the PMU is measuring. Common transmission levels include 115, 230, 345, 500, and 765 kV.
Magnitude of the voltage phasor measured in kilovolts. Represents the RMS voltage at the PMU measurement point.
Zero sequence component of the three-phase voltage in kilovolts. Indicates ground faults and neutral voltage displacement.
Unique identifier for each real-time rating record. Primary key for the real_time_rating product.
Identifier of the balancing authority responsible for this transmission element. Links rating to operational control area.
Identifier of the substation where this transmission element originates or terminates. Links rating to physical grid location.
User identifier of the system operator who reviewed or overrode this rating. Supports accountability and audit requirements.

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point Identifier (ID)
description: Identifier of the SCADA measurement point providing real-time loading or temperature data for this element.
Measured or forecasted ambient air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the element location. Primary environmental input for thermal rating calculations.
Circuit identifier distinguishing parallel transmission paths between the same bus pair. Used in switching orders and outage coordination.
Measured or calculated conductor surface temperature in degrees Celsius. Must not exceed maximum design temperature to prevent annealing and sag violations.
Indicates whether this rating is actively used in real-time contingency analysis. True for critical elements monitored for N-1 and N-2 contingencies.
Timestamp when this rating record was first inserted into the data platform. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.
Name of the source system or application that generated this rating record (e.g., DLR system, EMS rating module, weather integration service).
Human-readable name or designation of the transmission element as known in operational systems and switching orders.
Unique identifier of the transmission element (line, transformer, cable) being rated. References the asset or network element in the EMS model.
Type of transmission equipment being rated. Determines applicable rating methodology and thermal limits.
reference: IEEE Std 738 Standard for Calculating Current-Temperature Relationship of Bare Overhead Conductors

description: Real-time emergency thermal rating in megavolt-amperes. Maximum load the element can carry for a limited duration (typically 15 minutes to 4 hours) during contingency conditions.
Name of the EMS or SCADA system that received and is using this real-time rating for state estimation and contingency analysis.
Name of the originating bus or node in the EMS network model. Defines one end of a transmission line or branch element.
Timestamp when this rating record was last modified. Tracks changes to ratings due to recalculation or operator override.
Short-term emergency rating used during system restoration or load shedding events. Highest permissible loading for very brief durations to prevent cascading outages.
Maximum allowable conductor temperature in degrees Celsius per design specifications. Exceeding this limit risks permanent conductor damage and clearance violations.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region
description: NERC regional entity with jurisdiction over this transmission element. Determines applicable reliability standards and reporting requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WECC|ERCOT|MRO|NPCC|RF|SERC|TRE|SPP — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Real-time normal (continuous) thermal rating in megavolt-amperes. Maximum load the element can carry indefinitely under current ambient conditions without exceeding design limits.
Free-text field for additional context, special conditions, or operational notes related to this rating. Used for documentation and knowledge transfer.
Current operational status of the transmission element. Out-of-service elements do not require active rating updates.
Indicates whether a system operator manually overrode the calculated rating. True when operator judgment supersedes automated calculation.
Free-text explanation provided by the operator for manually overriding the calculated rating. Required for audit trail and compliance documentation.
PI historian tag name where this rating value is archived for historical analysis, trending, and post-event review.
Timestamp when the rating calculation algorithm executed. May differ from rating_timestamp if calculation is performed ahead of validity period.
Overall confidence in the calculated rating based on data quality, sensor availability, and model accuracy. Low confidence may trigger operator alerts.
Methodology used to calculate the real-time rating. Static uses fixed seasonal values; ambient-adjusted incorporates weather; dynamic line rating (DLR) uses real-time sensor data.
reference: IEEE Std 738 and CIGRE Technical Brochure 299

description: Date and time when this real-time rating was calculated and became effective. Represents the moment the rating applies to grid operations.
Timestamp when this rating expires and must be replaced by a new rating calculation. Ensures stale ratings are not used in operations.
Timestamp when this rating becomes valid and can be used by EMS for operational decisions and contingency analysis.

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
description: Code identifying the RTO or ISO market operator if this element participates in organized wholesale markets.
Calculated vertical clearance in feet between conductor at current temperature and ground or obstacles. Must maintain minimum clearances per NESC standards.

business_glossary_term: Solar Irradiance (Watts per Square Meter - W/m²)
description: Solar radiation intensity in watts per square meter. Solar heating reduces available thermal capacity, especially for overhead conductors.
Name of the terminating bus or node in the EMS network model. Defines the other end of a transmission line or branch element.
Nominal operating voltage level of the transmission element in kilovolts. Critical for determining thermal and electrical limits.
Quality indicator for weather inputs used in rating calculation. Poor quality data may require conservative rating adjustments or operator review.
Source of weather data used in rating calculation. Real-time sensors provide highest accuracy; forecasts or seasonal defaults are fallback options.
Wind direction in degrees (0-360) relative to true north. Wind angle relative to conductor affects cooling efficiency.
Measured or forecasted wind speed in miles per hour at conductor height. Wind cooling significantly increases thermal capacity of overhead lines.
Unique identifier for the voltage control action record.
Reference to the contingency analysis scenario that recommended or triggered this control action. Null for non-contingency-driven actions.
Reference to the control area where the voltage control action was executed.
Identifier of the system operator who initiated or approved the control action. Null for fully automatic actions. Used for audit trail and accountability.
Identifier of the distribution feeder affected by the voltage control action. Applicable for distribution-level voltage control actions.
FK to grid.ems_node.ems_node_id — Voltage control actions target a specific EMS bus (node) to maintain voltage within limits. The FK to ems_node identifies the target bus for the action.

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
description: Reference to the SCADA telemetry point associated with the controlled device.
Reference to the EMS node (bus) where the voltage control action was targeted.
Time in seconds from action initiation to completion or stabilization. Includes device response time and system settling time.

Outcome status of the voltage control action. Successful indicates action completed and achieved desired voltage change, failed indicates action did not execute or had no effect, partial indicates action executed but did not fully achieve target, aborted indicates action was cancelled mid-execution, pending verification indicates action executed but effectiveness not yet confirmed.
Date and time when the voltage control action was executed in the field. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the physical control action occurred.
Indicates whether a voltage alarm was triggered that led to this control action. True if an alarm condition existed, False if action was preventive or scheduled.

Indicates whether this voltage control action was taken to maintain compliance with NERC FAC-001 voltage profile requirements or other regulatory standards. True if compliance-driven, False otherwise.

Type of voltage control action executed. Capacitor bank switching adds reactive power, reactor switching removes reactive power, transformer tap change adjusts voltage ratio, generator VAR dispatch adjusts generator reactive output, static VAR compensator provides dynamic reactive support, synchronous condenser provides rotating reactive reserve.

Operating mode under which the control action was executed. Automatic indicates system-initiated without operator intervention, manual indicates direct operator command, supervisory indicates operator-approved automatic action, emergency indicates action taken during system emergency, test indicates action performed during commissioning or testing.
Name or identifier of the physical device that was controlled (e.g., capacitor bank CB-123, transformer T-456, generator G-789).

Classification of the controlled device. Capacitor bank provides capacitive reactive power, shunt reactor provides inductive reactive power, load tap changer adjusts transformer voltage, generator provides dynamic VAR support, SVC and STATCOM provide fast dynamic reactive compensation, synchronous condenser provides rotating inertia and reactive support. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: capacitor_bank|shunt_reactor|load_tap_changer|generator|svc|statcom|synchronous_condenser — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Timestamp when this voltage control action record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
Name of the source system that originated this voltage control action record (e.g., GE ADMS, OSIsoft PI, SCADA RTU).
Name or identifier of the EMS system that executed or recorded the voltage control action (e.g., GE ADMS, ABB Symphony Plus, Siemens Spectrum).
reference: IEC 61970 Energy Management System Application Program Interface

description: Source or trigger that initiated the voltage control action. Automatic Volt-VAR optimization indicates EMS algorithm-driven action, automatic voltage regulator indicates local device control, operator manual indicates human-initiated action, state estimator recommendation indicates action based on network state analysis, contingency analysis recommendation indicates preventive action, scheduled maintenance indicates planned operational adjustment.
Timestamp when this voltage control action record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

Change in reactive power in megavolt-amperes reactive resulting from the control action. Positive values indicate capacitive reactive power injection (voltage support), negative values indicate inductive reactive power absorption (voltage reduction).

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region
description: NERC regional entity jurisdiction where the voltage control action occurred. WECC=Western Electricity Coordinating Council, ERCOT=Electric Reliability Council of Texas, MRO=Midwest Reliability Organization, NPCC=Northeast Power Coordinating Council, RF=ReliabilityFirst, SERC=SERC Reliability Corporation, SPP=Southwest Power Pool, TRE=Texas Reliability Entity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WECC|ERCOT|MRO|NPCC|RF|SERC|SPP|TRE — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Free-text field for operator comments, special conditions, or additional context about the voltage control action.
OSIsoft PI historian tag name associated with this voltage control action for time-series data archival and retrieval.
Measured voltage in kilovolts at the target bus after the control action was executed and the system stabilized. Used to assess the effectiveness of the control action.
Power factor measured at the target bus after the control action and system stabilization. Used to assess improvement in reactive power balance.

Power factor measured at the target bus before the control action. Range -1.0 to 1.0, where values closer to 1.0 indicate better reactive power balance. Negative values indicate leading power factor (capacitive), positive values indicate lagging power factor (inductive).
Measured voltage in kilovolts at the target bus immediately before the control action was executed. Used to assess the voltage deviation that triggered the action.

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
description: Code identifying the RTO or ISO market operator responsible for the transmission system where the action occurred (e.g., CAISO, PJM, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP).
Name of the substation where the controlled device is located.
Number of tap positions changed for transformer tap control actions. Positive values indicate raise operations, negative values indicate lower operations. Null for non-tap control actions.
Name of the electrical bus where voltage control was targeted. This is the point in the network where voltage was being regulated.
Nominal voltage level in kilovolts of the target bus where control action was applied.

Percentage deviation of pre-action voltage from the nominal voltage setpoint. Calculated as ((pre_action_voltage - nominal_voltage) / nominal_voltage) * 100. Positive values indicate overvoltage, negative values indicate undervoltage.
Upper voltage limit in kilovolts for the target bus as defined by operating procedures or NERC standards. Actions are triggered when voltage approaches or exceeds this limit.
Lower voltage limit in kilovolts for the target bus as defined by operating procedures or NERC standards. Actions are triggered when voltage approaches or falls below this limit.
Target voltage setpoint in kilovolts that the control action was attempting to achieve or maintain at the target bus.
Unique identifier for the ACE record. Primary key for the time-series ACE dataset.
Foreign key reference to the balancing authority control area for which this ACE value was computed.

Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: ACE measurements are the foundation of NERC BAL-001 compliance for balancing authorities. Every ACE record serves as evidence for CPS1/CPS2 compliance calculations. This link enables automated complia

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
description: SCADA system point identifier for the ACE calculation output. Links this record to the underlying SCADA telemetry infrastructure.
Rolling 10-minute average of ACE values in megawatts. Critical metric for NERC CPS2 compliance evaluation, which requires the 10-minute average ACE to remain within L10 limits.
Filtered Area Control Error value in megawatts after applying smoothing algorithms to remove noise and transient spikes. Used for AGC control actions.
Raw unfiltered Area Control Error value in megawatts as computed by the EMS. Represents the instantaneous imbalance between scheduled and actual interchange plus frequency bias contribution.

Actual measured interconnection frequency in hertz at the time of this ACE calculation. Nominal frequency is 60.000 Hz for North American interconnections (Eastern, Western, Texas) and 50.000 Hz for other regions.
Boolean flag indicating whether AGC was enabled and actively issuing control signals to generating units at the time of this ACE measurement.

Operating mode of the AGC system at the time of this ACE measurement. Automatic mode indicates AGC is actively controlling generation; manual mode indicates operators are manually balancing; off indicates AGC is disabled; test indicates AGC is in test/simulation mode.

Method used to compute this ACE value. Standard indicates normal EMS calculation; backup indicates calculation by backup system; manual indicates operator calculation; estimated indicates interpolated or reconstructed value.

Boolean indicator of whether this ACE measurement contributes positively to CPS1 compliance. CPS1 measures the balancing authority's contribution to interconnection frequency error over a rolling 12-month period.

Boolean indicator of whether the 10-minute average ACE is within the L10 limit for this measurement period. CPS2 requires the balancing authority to maintain its 10-minute average ACE within specific bounds at least 90% of clock-10-minute periods.

Quality indicator for this ACE measurement. Good indicates validated real-time data; suspect indicates potential data quality issues; bad indicates known invalid data; estimated indicates calculated/interpolated value; manual indicates operator-entered value.
Name or identifier of the source system that provided this ACE record (e.g., EMS vendor name, PI historian instance, SCADA system identifier).
Boolean flag indicating whether a reportable disturbance event was occurring during this ACE measurement period. Disturbances may trigger special ACE evaluation rules under NERC standards.
Name or identifier of the EMS system that computed this ACE value. Supports environments with multiple EMS instances or backup systems.

The frequency bias setting in megawatts per 0.1 Hz used in the ACE calculation for this measurement period. Represents the balancing authority's obligation to respond to frequency deviations. Negative value indicates the BA will increase generation when frequency drops.
Difference between actual and scheduled frequency in hertz (actual minus scheduled). Positive values indicate over-frequency; negative values indicate under-frequency.
Interchange meter error correction term in megawatts applied to the ACE calculation to account for known metering inaccuracies on tie lines.

Name of the North American interconnection to which this balancing authority belongs. Eastern, Western, and Texas (ERCOT) are the three major asynchronous interconnections in North America; Quebec operates as a separate interconnection.

The L10 limit in megawatts for CPS2 compliance evaluation. Represents the maximum allowable 10-minute average ACE magnitude. Calculated as 1.65 times epsilon10 (the root-mean-square of the balancing authority's 10-minute average ACE over 12 months).
UTC timestamp when the ACE measurement was captured by the EMS. Represents the real-world event time for this ACE calculation cycle, typically at 4-6 second intervals per NERC requirements.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region
description: NERC regional entity code for the balancing authority. WECC=Western Electricity Coordinating Council, TRE=Texas Reliability Entity, MRO=Midwest Reliability Organization, NPCC=Northeast Power Coordinating Council, RF=ReliabilityFirst, SERC=SERC Reliability Corporation, SPP=Southwest Power Pool, FRCC=Florida Reliability Coordinating Council. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WECC|TRE|MRO|NPCC|RF|SERC|SPP|FRCC — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Net actual interchange power flow in megawatts across all tie lines connecting this balancing authority to neighboring control areas. Positive values indicate net export; negative values indicate net import.
Difference between net actual interchange and net scheduled interchange in megawatts (actual minus scheduled). A key component of the ACE calculation formula.
Net scheduled interchange power flow in megawatts for this measurement period, including all confirmed interchange transactions and dynamic schedules.
Free-text field for operational notes, annotations, or explanations related to this ACE measurement. May include operator comments about unusual conditions, data quality issues, or special events.
OSIsoft PI historian tag name for this ACE measurement point. Enables traceability to the real-time data historian for post-event analysis and compliance reporting.
Adjustment term in megawatts applied to ACE during primary frequency response events to account for the balancing authority's contribution to arresting frequency decline or rise.
Timestamp when this ACE record was first inserted into the data historian or lakehouse. Distinct from measurement_timestamp_utc, which represents the real-world event time.
Scheduled interconnection frequency in hertz for this measurement period. Typically 60.000 Hz for North American grids, but may vary during time error correction periods.
Boolean flag indicating whether the EMS state estimator had a valid converged solution at the time of this ACE calculation. Invalid state estimator solutions may affect ACE accuracy.
Number of tie line meters contributing to the net actual interchange calculation for this ACE measurement. Used for data quality assessment.
Number of tie line meters that were unavailable or failed at the time of this ACE calculation. Non-zero values may indicate degraded ACE accuracy.

Boolean flag indicating whether the interconnection was in time error correction mode during this measurement period. Time error correction adjusts scheduled frequency to correct accumulated time error.
Unique identifier for the AGC signal record. Primary key for the agc_signal product.
Reference to the balancing authority control area issuing this AGC signal.
Reference to the generating unit receiving this AGC regulation signal.

description: The SCADA system point identifier associated with this AGC signal measurement.

Foreign key linking to trading.trade. Business justification: AGC regulation deployment often fulfills ancillary service trades or regulation market awards. Linking enables real-time trade performance tracking, settlement quantity validation, and compliance veri
The actual measured system frequency in hertz (Hz) at the time of this AGC signal. Nominal frequency is 60.000 Hz in North America.

The operational mode of the Automatic Generation Control system at the time of this signal. Automatic mode means AGC is actively controlling generation; manual mode means operators are controlling generation manually.
The type of ancillary service being provided by this AGC signal. Regulation services provide continuous balancing, while reserve services provide contingency response.
The base generation setpoint in megawatts (MW) for the generating unit before AGC regulation adjustment.
Boolean indicator of whether this AGC signal interval meets NERC CPS1 compliance criteria. CPS1 measures the balancing authority's ability to follow its own generation schedule on a one-minute basis.

Boolean indicator of whether this AGC signal interval meets NERC CPS2 compliance criteria. CPS2 measures the balancing authority's ability to limit unscheduled power flows on a 10-minute average basis.
The name of the operational system from which this AGC signal record was sourced (e.g., OSIsoft PI, EMS, SCADA).
The name of the Energy Management System that generated this AGC signal.
The filtered Area Control Error in megawatts (MW) after applying smoothing algorithms to remove noise and transient spikes.
The frequency bias setting in megawatts per 0.1 hertz (MW/0.1 Hz) used in the ACE calculation. Represents the balancing authority's expected MW response to a 0.1 Hz frequency deviation.
The name of the North American electric interconnection to which this control area belongs. The four major interconnections are Eastern, Western, Texas (ERCOT), and Quebec.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Region
description: The NERC regional entity code responsible for reliability oversight of this control area (e.g., WECC, SERC, MRO, NPCC, RF, TRE).
The actual net interchange power flow in megawatts (MW) across all tie lines for the control area at this timestamp.
The deviation between actual and scheduled net interchange in megawatts (MW). Calculated as (Actual Net Interchange - Scheduled Net Interchange).
The scheduled net interchange power flow in megawatts (MW) across all tie lines for the control area at this timestamp.
Free-text field for additional comments, annotations, or operational notes related to this AGC signal event.
The OSIsoft PI historian tag name from which this AGC signal data was sourced. Used for traceability back to the SCADA system.

The unfiltered Area Control Error in megawatts (MW) computed at the same time grain as the AGC signal. Raw ACE = (Actual Net Interchange - Scheduled Net Interchange) - (Frequency Bias Setting) × (Actual Frequency - Scheduled Frequency).
The timestamp when this AGC signal record was first created in the data platform.
The timestamp when this AGC signal record was last updated in the data platform.
The direction of the regulation signal. Raise indicates the unit should increase generation, lower indicates decrease, neutral indicates no change.
The amount of regulation reserve capacity deployed in megawatts (MW) in response to the AGC signal.
The AGC regulation signal in megawatts (MW) sent to the generating unit. Positive values indicate raise signal, negative values indicate lower signal.
The rate at which the generating unit responds to the AGC signal, measured in megawatts per minute (MW/min).

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
description: The code identifying the RTO or ISO responsible for coordinating this control area's operations (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP).
The scheduled target system frequency in hertz (Hz). Typically 60.000 Hz for North American interconnections.
The settlement interval number within the operating day, used for ancillary services market settlement. Typically 5-minute or 15-minute intervals.
Quality indicator for the AGC signal data. Good indicates reliable data, uncertain indicates questionable data, bad indicates invalid data, substituted indicates estimated or replaced data.
The precise timestamp when this AGC signal and ACE computation were recorded. Primary event timestamp for this transactional record.
The rolling 10-minute average of Area Control Error in megawatts (MW), used for NERC CPS2 compliance calculations.
The status of the generating unit's response to the AGC signal. Indicates whether the unit is following the signal as expected.
Unique identifier for the balancing authority control area. Primary key for the control area master record.

Maximum allowable Area Control Error in megawatts before corrective action is required, used for automatic generation control and NERC BAL-001 compliance.
Current operating mode of the automatic generation control system for this control area.
Full legal name of the balancing authority organization operating this control area.
Indicates whether real-time contingency analysis is active for N-1 and N-2 security assessment.
Short alphanumeric code identifying the control area, typically 2-6 uppercase letters used in interchange scheduling and NERC reporting.
Target CPS1 compliance percentage (minimum 100%) measuring the control area's contribution to interconnection frequency error over a rolling 12-month period.
CPS2 compliance limit percentage (minimum 90%) measuring the control area's ACE performance within defined bounds during 10-minute periods.
Timestamp when this control area master record was first created in the system.
Name of the source system from which this control area record originated (e.g., EMS, SCADA, PI Historian, NERC Registry).
Most severe single contingency loss in megawatts that the control area must be prepared to recover from within 15 minutes, per NERC BAL-002 standard.
Date when this control area ceased operations or when the current configuration was superseded, null if currently active.
Date when this control area became operational or when the current configuration became effective.

Textual description of the geographic and electrical boundaries defining the control area's operational footprint.
Total installed generation capacity in megawatts available within the control area boundaries.

Standardized code returned by the AMI head-end system indicating the outcome of the remote service order execution (e.g., SUCCESS, METER_OFFLINE, COMMAND_REJECTED, TIMEOUT).
Detailed code explaining why the remote service order failed, populated only when order_status is failed; used for root cause analysis and retry logic.
Human-readable description of the failure reason, providing additional context for troubleshooting and customer communication.
Target meter firmware version to be installed by the over-the-air (OTA) update, verified upon successful completion.
Meter firmware version installed before the over-the-air (OTA) update, used for version control and rollback tracking.
Date and time when the remote service order record was last modified, supporting audit trail and change tracking requirements.
Power threshold in kilowatts (kW) set for load limiting activation orders, restricting customer consumption to prevent overload or support demand response programs.
Maximum number of retry attempts allowed for this remote service order before it is marked as permanently failed.
Date and time when the meter reading was captured at the meter during an on-demand read remote service order.
Unit of measure for the meter reading value captured during on-demand read (e.g., kWh for energy, kW for demand, kVAh for apparent energy).
Meter register reading value captured during an on-demand read remote service order, used for billing validation or dispute resolution.
Free-text notes or comments entered by users or systems regarding the remote service order, capturing additional context, special instructions, or resolution details.
Externally visible unique business identifier for the remote service order, used for tracking and customer communication.

Current lifecycle status of the remote service order: pending (queued), in progress (executing), success (completed successfully), failed (execution error), cancelled (user/system cancelled), or timeout (no response from meter).
Type of remote service action executed via AMI: remote connect, remote disconnect, on-demand meter read, load limiting activation/deactivation, or firmware over-the-air (OTA) update.

Priority level assigned to the remote service order, determining execution sequence in the AMI command queue (critical for safety/emergency, high for revenue protection, normal for routine, low for bulk operations).
Business reason for a remote reconnect order, typically following payment receipt or resolution of the disconnect condition.
Indicates whether the remote service order execution complies with applicable Public Utility Commission (PUC) regulations for disconnect/reconnect procedures and customer notification requirements.
Date and time when the remote service order was requested by the system or user, representing the business event initiation time.
Name or identifier of the source system that initiated the remote service order (e.g., CC&B, OMS, MDM, manual CSR entry).
Technical response payload returned by the meter to the AMI head-end system, stored for audit and troubleshooting purposes.
Number of times the remote service order has been retried after initial failure, used to track execution persistence and prevent infinite retry loops.
Date and time when the remote service order is scheduled to be executed on the meter, may differ from requested timestamp for planned actions.
Signal strength in decibels-milliwatts (dBm) measured at the time of remote service order execution, used to diagnose communication failures.
Unique identifier for the TOU or CPP rate program. Primary key.

FK to metering.meter_point.meter_point_id — After merging tou_enrollment into tou_rate_program, the enrollment records within tou_rate_program reference specific meter points. Required for billing to apply correct TOU rate periods.
