business_glossary_term: Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) Meter Required Flag
description: Indicates whether an AMI smart meter with interval data capability is required for enrollment in this program. True if AMI is mandatory; False if standard meters are acceptable.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Meter Configuration Requirements

description: Indicates whether enrollment effective dates must align with billing cycle boundaries. True if enrollment can only start at the beginning of a billing cycle.
reference: Oracle Utilities CC&B Billing Cycle Configuration

description: Email address for inquiries about the rate program. Used by customer service representatives and external stakeholders.
Phone number for inquiries about the rate program. Used by customer service representatives and external stakeholders.

business_glossary_term: Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) Event Trigger Criteria
description: Business rules or thresholds that trigger a CPP event (e.g., 'Forecasted system load >95% capacity', 'Day-ahead LMP >$150/MWh', 'Heat index >105F'). Nullable for non-CPP programs.
Maximum duration in hours for a single CPP event. Nullable for non-CPP programs.
Maximum number of CPP events that can be called in a calendar year, as defined in the tariff. Nullable for non-CPP programs.
Minimum advance notice in hours that must be provided to customers before a CPP event begins. Nullable for non-CPP programs.
Timestamp when this rate program record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record lifecycle.
Customer class or segment eligible for this rate program. Defines which customer types can enroll.
Date when the rate program expires or is superseded. Nullable for open-ended programs. After this date, no new enrollments are accepted.
reference: State PUC Rate Tariff Filing Requirements

description: Date when the rate program becomes effective and available for customer enrollment. Aligns with regulatory approval effective date.
reference: State PUC Rate Tariff Filing Requirements

description: Detailed criteria that customers must meet to be eligible for enrollment (e.g., 'Residential customers with annual usage >5000 kWh', 'Commercial customers with demand >50 kW').
reference: State PUC Rate Program Enrollment Rules

description: Defines how customers are enrolled in the program. OPT_IN: customer must actively enroll; OPT_OUT: customer is enrolled by default but can opt out; DEFAULT: automatic enrollment for new customers; MANDATORY: required for customer segment.
reference: State PUC Rate Program Enrollment Rules

description: Estimated average annual cost savings in US dollars for a typical customer enrolled in this program. Used for program marketing and benefit analysis.
Estimated average annual energy savings in kilowatt-hours (kWh) for a typical customer enrolled in this program. Used for program marketing and benefit analysis.
Code identifying the source system or integration point for this program record (e.g., 'MDM', 'CC&B', 'CIS'). Used for data lineage and system-of-record tracking.
Timestamp when this rate program record was last updated. Audit trail for record lifecycle and change tracking.
Reference code linking this rate program to marketing campaigns and customer acquisition initiatives. Nullable if no active marketing campaign.
Minimum number of months a customer must remain enrolled in the program before they can opt out or switch to another rate. Nullable if no minimum commitment.
reference: State PUC Rate Program Enrollment Rules

description: Minimum frequency in minutes at which interval data must be collected for this program (e.g., 15, 30, 60). Defines the granularity required for TOU period classification.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Interval Data Standards

description: User ID or system account that last modified this rate program record. Audit trail for accountability and compliance.
Textual or structured definition of off-peak period hours (e.g., 'All other hours', 'Weekdays 8pm-2pm, All day weekends'). Defines when off-peak TOU rates apply.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Rate Period Configuration

description: Indicates whether customers are allowed to opt out of the program after enrollment. False for mandatory programs; True for voluntary programs.
reference: State PUC Rate Program Enrollment Rules

description: Number of days advance notice required for a customer to opt out of the program. Nullable if opt-out is not allowed or has no notice requirement.
reference: State PUC Rate Program Enrollment Rules

description: Textual or structured definition of peak period hours (e.g., 'Weekdays 2pm-8pm', 'Mon-Fri 14:00-20:00'). Defines when peak TOU rates apply.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Rate Period Configuration

description: Business identifier for the rate program, used in billing systems and customer communications. Externally-known unique code for this TOU or CPP program.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Program Code Standard

description: Detailed business description of the rate program, including objectives, benefits, and customer value proposition. Used in customer communications and marketing materials.
reference: Oracle Utilities CC&B Program Documentation Standards

description: Human-readable name of the TOU or CPP rate program (e.g., 'Residential Time-of-Use Summer 2024', 'Commercial Critical Peak Pricing').
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Program Naming Convention

description: Business unit or department responsible for managing and administering this rate program (e.g., 'Metering Operations', 'Demand Response', 'Regulatory Affairs').

Current lifecycle status of the rate program. DRAFT: under development; PENDING_APPROVAL: submitted to PUC; ACTIVE: available for enrollment; SUSPENDED: temporarily inactive; RETIRED: no longer offered; CANCELLED: terminated before activation.
reference: State PUC Rate Program Lifecycle Standards

description: Classification of the rate program structure: TOU (Time-of-Use with fixed peak/off-peak periods), CPP (Critical Peak Pricing with event-driven pricing), TOU_CPP_HYBRID (combination), DYNAMIC_PRICING, or REAL_TIME_PRICING.
reference: NAESB Retail Electric Quadrant Business Practice Standards

description: Date when the regulatory body (PUC) approved this rate program. Critical for compliance and audit trails.
reference: State PUC Rate Tariff Filing Requirements

description: Reference number or docket ID of the PUC or regulatory body approval authorizing this rate program (e.g., 'PUC Docket 2024-E-001', 'Tariff Sheet 123-A').
reference: State PUC Rate Tariff Filing Requirements

description: Defines whether the program applies year-round or only during specific seasons. SEASONAL_VARIABLE indicates different rate periods apply in different seasons.
Textual or structured definition of shoulder (mid-peak) period hours, if applicable. Nullable if program has only peak/off-peak structure.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Rate Period Configuration

description: Month and day when summer season ends (MM-DD format, e.g., '09-30' for September 30th). Applicable when season_type includes summer periods.
Month and day when summer season begins (MM-DD format, e.g., '06-01' for June 1st). Applicable when season_type includes summer periods.
Reference to the official tariff sheet or rate schedule document that defines this program. Links to regulatory filing documentation.
reference: State PUC Rate Tariff Filing Requirements

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Rule Set
description: Reference to the VEE rule set applied to interval data for this program. Defines validation, estimation, and editing processes for data quality assurance.
Unique identifier for the interval reading record. Primary key for raw interval energy consumption and demand data collected from AMI smart meters.

Identifier of the billing cycle to which this interval reading contributes. Links interval data to the billing period for invoice generation and revenue recognition.
reference: Oracle Utilities CC&B - Billing Cycle Entity

Identifier of the smart meter device that generated this interval reading. Links to the physical AMI meter asset.

Identifier of the service point (delivery location) where energy consumption was measured. Represents the physical location of energy delivery.

description: FK to metering.meter.meter_id — Raw interval readings must reference the meter device that produced them. This is the fundamental data provenance link for all consumption data.
Channel identifier on the meter device. Multi-channel meters track multiple measurement types (kWh delivered, kWh received, kW demand, voltage, power factor). Typically 1-99.

Method by which the interval data was collected. AMI_PUSH = meter initiated transmission, AMI_POLL = head-end system requested, MANUAL = field reading, ESTIMATED = system generated, SCADA = real-time system, IMPORT = bulk file load.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Collection Method Taxonomy

description: Identifier of the batch collection run or polling cycle that retrieved this reading. Groups readings collected in the same operational batch for traceability and reprocessing.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Collection Run Entity

description: Code identifying the reason for manual correction or substitution of the original reading value. Examples: METER_ERROR, COMM_FAILURE, CUSTOMER_DISPUTE, DATA_QUALITY. Empty if no correction.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Correction Reason Taxonomy

description: Timestamp when this interval reading record was first inserted into the MDM system. Audit field for data lineage and record creation tracking.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

description: Percentage of expected interval data received for the associated collection period. 100.00 = complete, <100.00 = partial data. Used for data quality monitoring and VEE prioritization.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Data Quality Metrics

description: Name or identifier of the source system that provided this interval reading. Examples: AMI_HEAD_END, SCADA_HISTORIAN, MANUAL_ENTRY, BILLING_SYSTEM. Supports multi-source MDM environments.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Source System Registry

description: Indicates whether daylight saving time was in effect during this interval. True = DST active, False = standard time. Critical for accurate time-of-use rate application and demand response event timing.
Indicates whether a demand response event was active during this interval. True = DR event in progress, False = normal operation. Used for curtailment measurement and settlement.
Code identifying the estimation algorithm applied if the reading was estimated. Examples: LIKE_DAY, LINEAR_INTERPOLATION, AVERAGE_USAGE, ZERO_FILL. Empty for actual meter readings.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Estimation Algorithm Registry

description: Duration of the measurement interval in minutes. Common values: 15 (quarter-hourly), 30 (half-hourly), 60 (hourly). Supports variable interval lengths for different meter configurations.
Timestamp marking the end of the measurement interval. Defines the close of the accumulation period for this reading.

Timestamp marking the beginning of the measurement interval. Represents the real-world event time when the meter began accumulating energy for this interval. Typically aligned to 15-minute or 60-minute boundaries.
Timestamp of the most recent update to this interval reading record. Tracks modifications during VEE processing, manual corrections, or reprocessing events.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

description: Customer load profile classification segment for this service point. Used for load forecasting, rate design, and demand response targeting. Examples: RESIDENTIAL_STANDARD, COMMERCIAL_SMALL, INDUSTRIAL_LARGE.
Status of the meter read operation that produced this interval. SUCCESS = complete read, PARTIAL = incomplete data, FAILED = read failure, TIMEOUT = communication timeout, COMM_ERROR = network error.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Read Status Taxonomy

description: Indicates whether this service point is enrolled in net energy metering (solar or DER generation). True = NEM active, False = standard consumption-only metering. Affects billing credit calculations.
Original raw reading value before any estimation, substitution, or manual correction. Preserved for audit trail and comparison with corrected values. Null if no correction occurred.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

description: Indicates whether a power outage was detected during this interval based on meter status flags or zero-consumption patterns. True = outage detected, False = normal operation.

Data quality indicator for the raw interval reading. RAW = actual meter reading, ESTIMATED = calculated by estimation algorithm, SUBSTITUTED = replaced due to validation failure, EDITED = manually corrected, REJECTED = failed validation, MISSING = no data received.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Quality Codes

description: Rate schedule or tariff code in effect for this service point at the time of the interval. Used to determine applicable TOU (Time of Use) or CPP (Critical Peak Pricing) rates for billing.
reference: Oracle Utilities CC&B - Rate Schedule Entity

description: Raw numeric value of the interval measurement as collected from the meter. Represents energy consumption (kWh) or demand (kW) depending on channel configuration. Immutable raw value before VEE processing.
Timestamp when the interval reading was received by the head-end system or MDM platform. Used for latency analysis and data freshness monitoring. Distinct from the interval measurement time.
Indicates whether this interval reading has been reprocessed after initial load. True = reprocessed due to correction or VEE re-run, False = original processing. Supports data lineage tracking.

Indicates whether energy flowed in reverse direction (customer generation exported to grid) during this interval. True = export/generation, False = import/consumption. Critical for NEM and DER settlement.
Ambient temperature at the service point location during the interval, if available from weather data integration. Used for weather normalization and load forecasting. Null if not available.
UTC offset for the interval timestamps in ISO 8601 format (e.g., -05:00, +00:00). Ensures correct temporal alignment across service territories and daylight saving transitions.
Time-of-use pricing period classification for this interval based on rate schedule and timestamp. Determines the applicable energy rate tier for billing calculations.
reference: NAESB WEQ-019 - TOU Rate Structure Standards

description: Unit of measurement for the reading value. kWh (kilowatt-hour) for energy consumption, kW (kilowatt) for demand, kVArh for reactive energy, kVAr for reactive demand, kVAh for apparent energy, kVA for apparent demand.
User ID or system account that last modified this interval reading record. Supports audit trail and accountability for manual edits or system corrections.
reference: SOX - Internal Controls for Data Modification

description: Code identifying the specific validation rule or exception that flagged this reading during VEE processing. Examples: HIGH_USAGE, NEGATIVE_VALUE, MISSING_INTERVAL, SPIKE_DETECTED. Empty if no exceptions.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Exception Taxonomy

description: Status of VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) processing for this raw reading. PENDING = awaiting validation, VALIDATED = passed validation rules, FAILED = validation exceptions detected, BYPASSED = validation skipped.

Voltage classification of the service point where this interval was measured. LOW = residential/small commercial (<1kV), MEDIUM = commercial/industrial (1-35kV), HIGH = large industrial (35-230kV), TRANSMISSION = bulk power (>230kV).

business_glossary_term: Meter Data Management (MDM) Usage Transaction Identifier
description: Unique identifier for the MDM usage transaction record. Primary key for this billing-ready consumption record derived from validated interval data.

Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Usage transactions are the authoritative source data for billing calculations and must link directly to customer accounts for billing determinism, dispute resolution, and regulatory audit trails. Supp

Foreign key linking to renewable.der_registry. Business justification: MDM-calculated usage transactions for DER accounts include generation offsets, export credits, and net metering calculations. NEM billing calculation process requires usage transactions linked to DER

Foreign key linking to billing.invoice. Business justification: MDM usage transactions are the pre-billing usage records that feed invoice generation. This link traces billed charges back to source usage calculations, supports billing dispute investigation, revenu
Reference to the meter point (service point) for which this usage transaction was calculated. Links to the physical metering location.

FK to metering.validated_interval_reading.validated_interval_reading_id — Usage transactions are derived from validated interval data. This lineage link supports billing audit and consumption reconciliation.
Reference to the original usage transaction that this record reverses or replaces. Maintains audit trail for billing corrections.

FK to metering.meter_point.meter_point_id — MDM usage transactions (billing determinants) must reference the meter point for which consumption was calculated. This is the primary billing handoff link.

FK to metering.validated_interval_reading.validated_interval_reading_id — Usage transactions are derived from validated interval data. This FK enables billing reconciliation and audit — tracing a bill back to its source validated readings.
The amount of energy (in kWh) added or subtracted from the calculated usage due to manual adjustment. Positive for additions, negative for reductions.
Code indicating the reason for any manual adjustment applied to this usage transaction. Used for audit trail and dispute resolution.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; NAESB WEQ-015

description: Timestamp when this usage transaction was successfully handed off to the billing domain for invoice generation. Marks the completion of the meter-to-cash data flow from metering to billing.
The end date of the billing period for which this usage transaction was calculated. Defines the end of the consumption measurement window.
The start date of the billing period for which this usage transaction was calculated. Defines the beginning of the consumption measurement window.
Indicates whether this usage transaction has passed all validation checks and is ready to be handed off to the billing system for invoice generation.
Total energy consumption in kilowatt-hours (kWh) for this billing period and rate component. Primary billing determinant for energy charges.
Energy consumption during Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) events. Highest-priced energy period triggered during grid stress conditions for demand response.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; FERC Demand Response Standards

description: Timestamp when this usage transaction record was first created in the MDM system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Timestamp of the current meter read that marks the end of the consumption period for this usage transaction. Used for interval data boundary definition.
The source system or method from which the underlying interval or register data was obtained. Indicates data collection channel for quality assessment.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; NAESB WEQ-015

description: Number of interval data records that were manually or automatically edited during Validation, Estimation, and Editing (VEE) processing. Indicates data correction activity.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; NAESB WEQ-015

description: Number of interval data records that were estimated rather than measured during Validation, Estimation, and Editing (VEE) processing. Indicates data quality and estimation reliance.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; NAESB WEQ-015

description: Timestamp when this usage transaction record was last modified. Tracks updates during VEE processing, adjustments, or corrections.

business_glossary_term: Meter Data Management (MDM) Processing Run Identifier
description: Identifier of the MDM batch processing run that generated this usage transaction. Used for traceability, reprocessing, and audit purposes.
Multiplier applied to raw meter readings to account for Current Transformer (CT) and Potential Transformer (PT) ratios. Converts instrument readings to actual consumption values.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; IEEE C57.13 Instrument Transformer Standards

description: Energy exported back to the grid from customer-owned Distributed Energy Resources (DER) under Net Energy Metering (NEM) programs. Negative consumption for billing credit calculation.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; PURPA Net Metering Standards

description: Energy consumption during off-peak hours as defined by the Time of Use (TOU) rate schedule. Lower-priced energy period for demand management.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; FERC TOU Rate Standards

description: Energy consumption during on-peak hours as defined by the Time of Use (TOU) rate schedule. Higher-priced energy period for demand management.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; FERC TOU Rate Standards

description: Maximum demand in kilowatts (kW) recorded during the billing period for this rate component. Used for demand-based billing and capacity planning.
reference: IEEE 1459 Power Definitions; FERC Rate Design Standards

description: Timestamp of the previous meter read that marks the start of the consumption period for this usage transaction. Used for interval data boundary definition.
The rate component or tariff element for which this usage was calculated (e.g., on-peak energy, off-peak energy, demand charge, reactive power). Determines how the usage is priced in billing.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; FERC Rate Design Standards

description: Maximum reactive power demand in kilovolt-amperes reactive (kVAR) during the billing period. Used for power factor billing and grid stability management.
reference: IEEE 1459 Power Definitions; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Indicates whether this usage transaction is a reversal of a previously posted transaction. Used for billing corrections and reprocessing scenarios.
Energy consumption during shoulder (mid-peak) hours as defined by the Time of Use (TOU) rate schedule. Mid-tier pricing period between on-peak and off-peak.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; FERC TOU Rate Standards

description: Indicates whether this usage transaction has been adjusted for weather normalization to account for temperature variations. Used for load forecasting and customer comparisons.
Total number of interval data records aggregated to produce this usage transaction. Used for data quality assessment and completeness validation.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; NAESB WEQ-015

description: The unit of measure for the primary usage value in this transaction. Standardizes measurement units across different rate components and meter types.

The method used by MDM to calculate this usage transaction. Indicates whether the value was derived from interval data aggregation, register reads, estimation algorithms, proration, or manual adjustment.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; NAESB WEQ-015 Retail Market Business Practices

description: Data quality indicator code assigned by MDM to this usage transaction. Reflects confidence level in the calculated usage based on source data quality and VEE results.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; NAESB WEQ-015

description: Business identifier for the usage transaction. Human-readable reference number used in billing and customer service interactions.

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Completion Timestamp
description: Timestamp when the VEE processing was completed for this usage transaction. Marks when the data became billing-ready.
Overall status of the Validation, Estimation, and Editing (VEE) process for the interval data underlying this usage transaction. Indicates data quality and readiness for billing.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Data Model; NAESB WEQ-015

description: Unique identifier for the validated interval reading record. Primary key for this entity representing a single VEE-processed meter reading interval.

Foreign key linking to compliance.audit. Business justification: Interval data validation processes audited for VEE rule compliance, estimation methodology, data quality standards. Provides audit evidence for billing accuracy, regulatory data quality reviews, SOX t

Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: VEE-validated readings are the authoritative source for control area load profiles used in state estimation, load forecasting, and balancing authority financial settlement. Regulatory and operational
Reference to the billing cycle that this interval reading contributes to. Links interval data to the billing period for invoice generation.
reference: Oracle Utilities CC&B - Billing Cycle Entity

description: Foreign key linking to renewable.der_registry. Business justification: VEE-processed interval data from DER meters supports PPA settlement calculations, RPS compliance reporting, and curtailment event compensation. Monthly PPA settlements require validated generation dat
Reference to the demand response event that was active during this interval, if applicable. Null if no DR event was in effect.
Reference to the specific outage event record if this interval was affected by a service interruption. Null if no outage occurred.

description: Reference to the source raw interval reading record from which this validated reading was derived. Establishes lineage from raw to validated data.

Reference to the physical meter device that captured this interval reading. Links to the meter asset registry.

FK to metering.interval_reading.interval_reading_id — Each validated interval reading must trace back to its source raw interval reading for audit trail and VEE processing lineage. Regulatory requirement for billing data integrity.

FK to metering.meter_point.meter_point_id — Validated interval data is associated with the meter point (not just the meter device) because billing and downstream consumers need location-based consumption. This is the SSOT consumption record key
The identifier of the user or system process that performed manual editing on this reading. Null for automated VEE processing.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - User Audit Trail

description: FK to metering.vee_rule.vee_rule_id — Each validated reading should reference the VEE rule that was applied during validation/estimation. Required for regulatory audit of data quality processing.
Reference to the rate schedule (tariff) that was active for this service point during this interval. Used to determine applicable TOU or CPP pricing periods.
reference: Oracle Utilities CC&B - Rate Schedule Entity

description: Reference to the service delivery point (premise connection) where energy consumption was measured. The logical metering location.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Service Point Entity

description: FK to metering.vee_rule.vee_rule_id — Each validated interval reading references the VEE rule that was applied during validation/estimation. Critical for audit trail and understanding how data quality was assured.

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: VEE processing operations (meter data management, validation software, analyst labor) have associated costs allocated to cost centers. Required for MDM operational cost tracking, billing quality assur
The workflow approval state for this validated reading. Indicates whether the reading has been reviewed and approved for downstream consumption by billing and analytics systems.
The date and time when this validated reading was approved for billing and operational use. Null if not yet approved.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Approval Audit Trail

description: Boolean indicator of whether this reading meets the quality standards required for billing purposes. True indicates the reading is approved for billing calculations.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Billing Quality Criteria

description: The specific meter channel or register from which this reading was captured. Multi-channel meters track different measurement types on separate channels.
reference: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

description: The validated energy consumption for this interval measured in kilowatt-hours. This is the authoritative billing-quality consumption value after VEE processing.
Boolean indicator of whether this interval occurred during a declared Critical Peak Pricing event. True indicates CPP premium rates apply.
reference: FERC - Demand Response and Advanced Metering

description: The date and time when this validated interval reading record was first created in the MDM system.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

description: A composite quality score (0-100) calculated by the VEE engine based on validation rules, estimation confidence, and data completeness. Higher scores indicate higher quality.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Quality Scoring Framework

description: The originating system or channel from which the raw interval data was collected before VEE processing.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Source System Registry

description: The maximum instantaneous power demand recorded during this interval, measured in kilowatts. Used for demand-based billing and capacity planning.
Free-text notes provided by the editor explaining the context or justification for manual edits to this reading.
The business reason code explaining why this reading was manually edited. Examples include meter malfunction, data transmission error, or customer dispute resolution.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Edit Reason Reference

description: A numerical score (0-100) indicating the confidence level in the estimated value. Higher scores indicate greater confidence in the estimation accuracy.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Estimation Quality Metrics

description: The algorithm or technique used to estimate this reading if the original data was missing or invalid. Set to 'none' for non-estimated readings.
The specific exception rule code that was triggered during VEE processing. Examples include high-usage threshold breach, negative consumption, or data gap detection.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Exception Rule Reference

description: Boolean indicator of whether this reading triggered any VEE exception rules requiring manual review. True indicates the reading requires analyst attention.
The length of the measurement interval in minutes. Common values include 15, 30, or 60 minutes depending on meter configuration and rate program requirements.
The precise date and time when this measurement interval ended. Defines the end boundary of the consumption period.
The precise date and time when this measurement interval began. Defines the start boundary of the consumption period.
The date and time when this validated interval reading record was most recently updated or edited.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Audit Trail Standards

description: Classification of how the meter reading was obtained: automatically via AMI, manually by field personnel, estimated by system, or provided by customer.
The raw, unmodified consumption value before VEE processing. Preserved for audit trail and comparison purposes. Null if no original value existed.
Boolean indicator of whether a power outage was recorded at this service point during this interval. True indicates zero consumption due to service interruption.
The ratio of real power to apparent power, ranging from 0 to 1. Indicates the efficiency of power usage and may trigger power factor penalties or credits.
reference: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for Measurement of Electric Power

description: The reactive power component measured in kilovolt-amperes reactive. Used for power factor calculations and grid stability analysis.
reference: IEEE 1459 - Definitions for Measurement of Electric Power

description: The timestamp when the meter physically recorded this interval data. May differ from interval_end_timestamp in cases of delayed meter reads or backfill scenarios.

description: The ambient temperature in degrees Fahrenheit recorded at the associated weather station during this interval. Used for load forecasting and weather normalization.
The time-of-use pricing period classification for this interval (e.g., on-peak, off-peak, shoulder). Determines the rate tier applied for billing.
The measurement unit for the primary consumption value. Standardizes interpretation of numeric readings across different meter types and configurations.
The quality status assigned by the VEE process indicating whether the reading is original valid data, was estimated, edited, substituted, flagged as suspect, or missing.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Status Codes

business_glossary_term: VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) Processing Timestamp
description: The date and time when the VEE process completed validation and transformation of this reading into its final billing-quality state.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Processing Audit Trail

business_glossary_term: VEE (Validation, Estimation, and Editing) Run ID
description: Reference to the VEE processing batch run that produced this validated reading. Enables traceability of which VEE execution cycle processed this data.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - VEE Processing Framework

description: The average voltage level measured during this interval in volts. Used for power quality monitoring and voltage regulation analysis.
reference: ANSI C84.1 - Electric Power Systems and Equipment Voltage Ratings

description: Reference to the weather station used for temperature normalization and weather-adjusted load analysis for this service point location.

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Identifier
description: Unique identifier for the VEE exception record. Primary key for the VEE exception entity.
Reference to the customer account associated with the meter and service point for this VEE exception. Used for customer impact analysis and billing hold workflows.

Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: VEE exceptions identified as audit findings when indicating systematic data quality issues or control deficiencies. Supports audit evidence collection, corrective action tracking, regulatory reporting
Reference to the employee or system user who reviewed and resolved this VEE exception. Null if exception is still open or was auto-resolved without manual review.

Foreign key linking to outage.outage_event. Business justification: VEE analysts investigate whether missing/anomalous interval readings stem from power interruptions. Regulatory VEE reports require cross-referencing exceptions with outage events to justify estimation
Reference to the meter that generated the interval data which triggered this VEE exception.
Reference to the service point (delivery location) associated with the meter that generated the interval data for this exception. Used to link exceptions to customer accounts and premises.

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Rule Identifier
description: Reference to the VEE rule that was triggered and caused this exception to be raised.

Reference to the rate schedule (tariff) applicable to the service point at the time of the exception. Used to determine billing impact and priority for resolution, especially for Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) customers.

FK to metering.interval_reading.interval_reading_id — VEE exceptions must reference the interval reading(s) that failed validation. Without this link, operators cannot identify and resolve data quality issues.
FK to metering.vee_rule.vee_rule_id — Each VEE exception must reference the VEE rule that triggered it. This is essential for exception resolution workflows and rule tuning.
Reference to the specific interval data record that failed VEE validation and raised this exception.

Boolean flag indicating whether the VEE engine attempted automatic resolution of this exception through estimation algorithms. True if auto-resolution was attempted; False if exception was immediately flagged for manual review.

Boolean flag indicating whether automatic resolution by the VEE engine was successful. True if the engine successfully estimated a replacement value that passed validation; False if auto-resolution failed and manual intervention is required.

Boolean flag indicating whether this VEE exception affects customer billing. True if the affected interval data is used in billing determinants and the exception must be resolved before bill calculation; False if the exception is for non-billing data (e.g., operational monitoring, grid analytics).

Final corrected interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) after manual review and editing. This is the value that will be used for billing if the exception is resolved. Null if not yet corrected.
Timestamp when this VEE exception record was first created in the MDM system. Audit field for data lineage and record lifecycle tracking.

Numeric data quality score (0.00 to 100.00) assigned to the interval data by the VEE engine, indicating confidence in the data accuracy. Lower scores trigger exceptions. Used for trending meter health and VEE rule tuning.
Estimated interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) calculated by the VEE engine to replace the invalid or missing original value. Null if estimation was not performed or failed.

Method used by the VEE engine or analyst to estimate the corrected interval value. Linear interpolation: average of adjacent intervals. Historical average: average of same interval from prior days. Similar day: value from comparable day (same day-of-week, season). Regression: statistical model. Manual entry: analyst-provided value. None: no estimation performed.

Final disposition category of the VEE exception indicating how it was ultimately handled. Resolved: data corrected and validated. Escalated: sent to engineering or management for further investigation. Waived: accepted without correction per approved business rule or regulatory guidance.

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Number
description: Business-facing unique exception number assigned to this VEE exception for tracking and audit purposes. Format: VEE-xxxxxxxxxx.
Timestamp when the VEE exception was first raised by the MDM VEE engine during interval data validation processing. Represents the business event time of exception detection.

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Severity
description: Severity level of the VEE exception indicating business impact and urgency for resolution. Critical exceptions block billing; high exceptions require immediate review; medium and low exceptions are tracked for quality metrics; informational exceptions are logged for audit only.

Source system that originated the interval data which triggered this VEE exception. Typically MDM (Meter Data Management) for AMI data, AMI head-end for direct meter reads, SCADA for grid operations data, manual entry for field reads, or billing system for estimated reads.

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Status
description: Current lifecycle status of the VEE exception. Open: newly raised and awaiting review. In Review: assigned to analyst for investigation. Resolved: corrective action taken and data corrected. Escalated: requires supervisor or engineering review. Waived: exception accepted without correction per business rule. Closed: final disposition recorded and exception archived.

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Exception Type
description: Classification of the VEE exception indicating the nature of the data quality issue: validation failure (data failed validation rule), estimation failure (unable to estimate missing interval), editing failure (manual edit rejected), missing data (no interval data received), suspect data (data flagged as questionable), or out of range (value exceeds expected bounds).
Number of individual interval readings affected by this VEE exception. For 15-minute interval meters, a 1-hour exception would affect 4 intervals.
End timestamp of the interval data range affected by this VEE exception. Defines the end of the time window containing suspect or invalid data.
Start timestamp of the interval data range affected by this VEE exception. Defines the beginning of the time window containing suspect or invalid data.
Timestamp when this VEE exception record was last updated. Audit field for tracking changes to exception status, resolution actions, and data corrections.
Original raw interval data value (in kWh or other unit of measure) that triggered the VEE exception before any estimation or editing was applied.

Boolean flag indicating whether this VEE exception must be reported to regulatory authorities (e.g., state Public Utility Commission) as part of data quality and billing accuracy compliance reporting. True if reportable; False otherwise.

Action taken to resolve the VEE exception. Re-estimate: apply different estimation algorithm. Manual edit: analyst manually corrected the value. Accept original: original value accepted despite exception. Override: supervisor approved exception without correction. Escalate: sent to engineering for investigation. Waive: exception acknowledged but no correction required per business rule.
Free-text notes entered by the analyst or system documenting the resolution action, rationale for the decision, and any additional context for audit purposes.

Timestamp when the VEE exception was resolved (status changed to resolved, waived, or closed). Null if exception is still open or in review. Used to calculate exception aging and VEE team performance metrics.
Full name of the analyst or system user who reviewed and resolved this VEE exception. Captured for audit trail and operational reporting.

Numeric threshold value defined in the VEE rule that was exceeded or violated, triggering this exception. For example, maximum expected consumption in kWh, or maximum percent deviation from historical average.

Unit of measure for the interval data values associated with this exception. Typically kWh (kilowatt-hour) for electric energy consumption, kW for demand, or gas volume units. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kWh|MWh|kW|kVAR|kVA|CCF|MCF|therms — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Batch Identifier
description: Reference to the VEE processing batch run that raised this exception. Used to group exceptions by processing cycle for operational dashboards and batch-level quality metrics.

business_glossary_term: Validation Estimation and Editing (VEE) Rule Identifier

Comma-separated list of rate schedule codes to which this VEE rule applies. Enables rate-specific validation and estimation logic for TOU and CPP programs.
Type of utility service to which this VEE rule applies (electric, gas, water, steam). Ensures rules are applied to appropriate commodity data streams.
Indicates whether changes to this VEE rule require formal approval before activation. True for rules impacting billing or regulatory compliance.
User identifier of the person who approved this VEE rule for production use. Applicable when approval_required_flag is true.
Timestamp when this VEE rule was formally approved for production use. Supports governance and compliance documentation.

business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Audit Trail Enabled Flag
description: Indicates whether detailed audit logging is enabled for this rule, capturing every application of the rule and its outcomes for compliance and troubleshooting.
Indicates whether data passing this VEE rule is considered billing-quality and suitable for revenue calculation. True if the rule ensures billing-grade accuracy.
Minimum confidence level (as a percentage) required for estimated values to be accepted as billing-quality. Used in statistical estimation algorithms.
Timestamp when this VEE rule record was first created in the MDM system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.
Date after which the VEE rule is no longer active. Nullable for open-ended rules. Supports rule lifecycle management and historical analysis.
Date from which the VEE rule becomes active and is applied to meter data. Supports temporal rule management and regulatory compliance.

Specific estimation technique used when the rule type is estimation. Defines how missing or invalid interval data is calculated (e.g., linear interpolation, historical average, same-day-last-week). Action taken when the rule detects a data quality exception: flag for review, automatically estimate, reject the data, route to manual review, or substitute with a default value.
Frequency at which the VEE rule is executed against incoming or historical meter data (real-time, hourly, daily, weekly, on-demand).

business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Last Modified By User
description: User identifier of the person who last modified this VEE rule record. Supports change tracking and accountability.
Timestamp when this VEE rule record was last modified. Supports audit trail and change management.

business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Lookback Period in Days
description: Number of days of historical data the rule examines for validation or estimation purposes. Used by statistical and pattern-matching algorithms.
Minimum acceptable value for validation rules. Interval data below this limit triggers a validation exception or editing action.
Free-text field for additional notes, implementation guidance, or special considerations related to this VEE rule. Supports knowledge transfer and operational documentation.

description: Business unit or team responsible for maintaining and governing this VEE rule (e.g., Metering Operations, Revenue Assurance, Data Quality Team).
Execution sequence priority for the rule within the VEE processing engine. Lower numbers execute first. Determines the order in which multiple rules are applied to the same interval data.
Citation of the regulatory requirement, tariff provision, or PUC order that mandates or justifies this VEE rule. Supports compliance documentation and audit trails.

description: Functional category of the rule indicating the specific data quality issue it addresses (e.g., spike detection, zero consumption validation, missing data estimation).
Business identifier code for the VEE rule, used for external reference and system integration. Typically a short alphanumeric code following utility naming conventions.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Business Practice Standards

description: Detailed description of the VEE rule including its business logic, application context, and expected outcomes when applied to interval meter data.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Business Practice Standards

description: Human-readable name of the VEE rule describing its purpose and function within the meter data management process.
Current lifecycle status of the VEE rule indicating whether it is actively applied to meter data processing or in a non-operational state.
Classification of the rule within the VEE process: validation (checks data quality), estimation (fills missing data), or editing (corrects erroneous data).

business_glossary_term: VEE Rule Threshold Unit of Measure
description: Unit of measure for the threshold value (e.g., kWh, MWh, percentage, count, standard deviations) providing context for threshold interpretation.
Numeric threshold parameter used by the rule algorithm to determine data quality exceptions. For example, spike tolerance percentage, maximum consumption limit, or minimum expected value.
Maximum acceptable value for validation rules. Interval data above this limit triggers a validation exception or editing action.
Version number of the VEE rule configuration. Incremented with each modification to support change tracking and rollback capabilities.
User identifier of the person who created this VEE rule record. Supports accountability and audit requirements.

Programmed interval in minutes for resetting the demand register (e.g., 15, 30 minutes). Determines how frequently peak demand is calculated and recorded. Critical for demand billing accuracy.

description: Current position of the remote disconnect switch for meters with disconnect capability. Connected indicates service is on; Disconnected indicates service is off; Armed indicates ready for remote command; Not Applicable for meters without disconnect.

description: Version identifier of the embedded software running on the meter device. Critical for security patching, feature enablement, and compatibility with head-end systems. Tracked for firmware upgrade campaigns.
ANSI form designation describing the physical configuration and wiring arrangement of the meter (e.g., Form 2S, Form 12S, Form 16S). Determines socket compatibility and installation requirements.

description: Date the meter was physically installed at its current service location. Used for age tracking, warranty calculations, and lifecycle management. Distinct from manufacturing date.

Programmed interval duration in minutes for load profile data collection (e.g., 15, 30, 60 minutes). Determines granularity of consumption data for billing, demand response, and grid analytics. Configurable parameter tracked for versioning.
reference: ANSI C12.19 - Utility Industry End Device Data Tables

description: Assigned IP address for meters using IP-based communication protocols (cellular, fiber). Used for direct meter communication, remote diagnostics, and firmware updates. Confidential to prevent unauthorized access.
Timestamp of the most recent update to any field in this meter record. Used for change tracking, data synchronization, and audit compliance. Updated automatically on any record modification.

Current state of the meter in its asset lifecycle. Installed indicates active deployment; In Stock indicates warehouse inventory; In Transit indicates shipment; Retired indicates end-of-life; Failed indicates defective; Under Test indicates lab testing.

Comma-separated list of load profile channels currently enabled for data collection (e.g., kWh Delivered, kWh Received, kVARh, Voltage, Current). Defines which measurement streams are actively recorded in interval data.

description: Hardware MAC address of the communication module network interface. Used for network device identification, AMI head-end provisioning, and communication diagnostics. Confidential to prevent network security risks.
Name of the company that manufactured the meter device (e.g., Landis+Gyr, Itron, Sensus, Elster, Aclara). Used for vendor management, warranty tracking, and firmware compatibility.

Classification of meter technology and capability level. AMI Smart Meter supports two-way communication and remote operations; Interval Meter records time-series consumption; Demand Meter tracks peak demand; Electromechanical is legacy analog; Electronic is digital non-communicating; Prepaid supports prepayment programs.
Manufacturer model designation identifying the specific meter product line and capabilities. Used for configuration management, firmware updates, and technical specifications lookup.
Version identifier of the firmware running on the communication module, tracked separately from meter firmware. Critical for communication security patches and protocol updates.

Current operational status of the communication module. Active indicates normal operation; Inactive indicates disabled but functional; Failed indicates hardware failure; Replaced indicates module swap; Not Installed for non-AMI meters.

Free-text field for operational notes, special handling instructions, field observations, or historical context not captured in structured fields. Used by field technicians and operations staff.
Count of independent metering elements within the device. Single-phase meters have 1 element; polyphase meters have 2 or 3 elements. Determines measurement capability for multi-phase services.

Legal ownership classification of the meter asset. Utility Owned is standard for most deployments; Customer Owned for customer-purchased meters; Leased for rental arrangements; Third Party for meters owned by service providers.
Purchase order number under which this meter was procured. Used for procurement tracking, warranty validation, and vendor management. Links to financial and supply chain systems.
Description of the meter register setup including number of dials, multiplier, and measurement units (kWh, kVARh, kW demand). Defines what consumption data the meter captures and how it is displayed.

Boolean flag indicating whether the meter has remote service disconnect/reconnect capability. True enables remote service control for collections, move-in/move-out, and emergency response. False requires manual field operations.

description: Date the meter was removed from service location. Nullable for currently installed meters. Used for lifecycle tracking, inventory management, and historical service point analysis.
Unique identifier of the tamper-evident seal applied to the meter cover. Used to detect unauthorized meter access, tampering, and theft. Recorded during installation and verified during inspections.

Current condition of the meter seal. Intact indicates no tampering; Broken indicates potential unauthorized access requiring investigation; Missing indicates seal loss; Not Applicable for meters without seals.
Manufacturer-assigned unique serial number physically stamped on the meter device. Used for asset tracking, warranty claims, and field verification. SSOT for device identity.

Date of the most recent accuracy test or calibration performed on the meter. Used to track compliance with regulatory testing intervals and identify meters due for testing.
Nominal voltage rating for which the meter is designed and certified. Determines appropriate deployment location (residential 120/240V, commercial 277/480V, primary voltage for large industrial).
Date when the manufacturer warranty coverage expires. Used for warranty claim eligibility, replacement planning, and total cost of ownership analysis. Nullable if warranty terms are not date-based.

description: AMI communication network segment or cell serving this meter point. Determines data collection routing and network performance monitoring.

description: Contracted or subscribed service capacity in kilowatts for this meter point. Applicable to large commercial and industrial customers.
Indicates whether this meter point is eligible for critical peak pricing programs. Used for demand response event targeting.
Timestamp when this meter point record was first created in the MDM system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

description: Composite data quality score (0-100) reflecting completeness, accuracy, and consistency of meter point attributes. Used for data stewardship prioritization.
Nameplate capacity in kilowatts of distributed generation or storage interconnected at this meter point. Used for hosting capacity analysis.

Geographic latitude coordinate of the meter point in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, outage analysis, and field crew navigation.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the meter point in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, outage analysis, and field crew navigation.
Indicates whether this meter point supports interval data collection (15-minute, 30-minute, or hourly). Required for TOU billing and demand response.

description: Length of each measurement interval in minutes for interval data collection (typically 15, 30, or 60). Determines data granularity for analytics.
Date of the most recent successful meter reading for this service point. Used for billing cycle validation and data quality monitoring.
Timestamp when this meter point record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data synchronization.
reference: SOX Internal Controls - Data Audit Standards

description: Customer segment classification determining consumption patterns, rate structures, and demand response eligibility. Critical for load forecasting and grid planning.
Two-digit billing cycle code determining the scheduled meter reading date. Used for billing run scheduling and route optimization.
Frequency at which meter readings are collected for billing purposes. AMI-enabled points support continuous interval data collection.
Indicates whether net energy metering is enabled for this service point due to behind-the-meter generation (solar, wind, CHP).
Logical node identifier in the electrical network topology model. Used by ADMS and DMS systems for network analysis and switching operations.
Maximum recorded demand in kilowatts at this meter point. Used for capacity planning, rate design, and demand charge billing.
Electrical phase configuration of the service connection. Determines metering channel requirements and load balancing considerations.
Tariff rate schedule code applicable to this meter point. Determines pricing structure, TOU periods, and billing determinants.
Date when service was first activated at this meter point. Marks the beginning of the service point lifecycle.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Service Point Lifecycle

description: Primary street address line for the meter point location. Used for field crew dispatch and outage management.
Secondary address line for apartment, suite, or unit number at the meter point location.
City or municipality where the meter point is located. Used for jurisdictional rate determination and regulatory reporting.
Three-letter ISO country code for the meter point location. Determines applicable national regulatory frameworks.
Date when service was permanently deactivated at this meter point. Null for active service points.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Service Point Lifecycle

description: Externally-known business identifier for the service delivery point. Used in customer communications, billing, and field operations.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Service Point Number

description: Current lifecycle status of the meter point. Active indicates the point is in service and generating consumption data.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Service Point Lifecycle

description: Classification of the commodity delivered at this meter point. Determines applicable rate schedules and measurement requirements.
Postal code for the meter point service address. Used for geographic analysis and service territory validation.
Two-letter state or province code for the meter point location. Determines applicable PUC jurisdiction and regulatory requirements.
Voltage classification at which energy is delivered to this meter point. Determines metering accuracy requirements and applicable tariffs.
Nominal voltage in volts at which service is delivered (e.g., 120V, 240V, 480V, 13.8kV). Used for power quality monitoring and equipment compatibility verification.
Code identifying the authoritative source system for this meter point record. Supports multi-system data integration and master data governance.
Indicates whether time-of-use rate pricing is active for this meter point. Requires interval data collection and TOU-capable metering.

description: Indicates whether meter data from this point undergoes VEE processing for data quality assurance before billing and analytics.

Foreign key linking to billing.adjustment. Business justification: Failed meter tests trigger billing adjustments for inaccurate metering periods (regulatory requirement). This link directly connects test results to financial corrections, supports PUC audit trails, a

Foreign key linking to compliance.audit. Business justification: Meter testing programs audited for compliance with testing frequency, accuracy standards, documentation requirements. Provides audit evidence for measurement accuracy programs, regulatory inspection s

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Meter testing activities are cost-accounted to specific cost centers (meter shop operations). Required for meter shop budgeting, labor cost allocation, and regulatory compliance testing cost tracking
Reference to the customer service request that initiated the meter test, if applicable. Links to the customer service system for complaint tracking and resolution.

Foreign key linking to renewable.der_registry. Business justification: Accuracy testing of bidirectional meters at DER installations for regulatory compliance and revenue assurance. Annual DER meter testing program requires test records linked to DER for compliance repor
Reference to the technician or engineer who performed the meter test. Links to the workforce or employee registry for accountability and certification tracking.

Foreign key linking to compliance.environmental_permit. Business justification: Meter test facilities require environmental permits for calibration equipment, hazardous waste disposal (mercury switches, electronic waste). Enables permit compliance tracking for test labs, regulato

Foreign key linking to asset.asset_inspection. Business justification: Meter testing is a specialized asset inspection activity. Utilities integrate meter test results (accuracy, condition ratings, defects) into asset health monitoring and condition-based maintenance pro
Reference to the meter that was tested. Links to the meter asset registry.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM - Meter Asset Management

description: FK to metering.meter.meter_id — Meter test results must reference the meter device tested. Required for regulatory compliance (PUC meter testing requirements) and accuracy tracking.
Reference to the work order that authorized or triggered the meter test. Links to the work management system for scheduling, labor tracking, and cost allocation.

Measured accuracy of the meter expressed as a percentage error. Positive values indicate the meter is running fast (over-registering); negative values indicate the meter is running slow (under-registering). Calculated as ((measured - actual) / actual) * 100.

Meter register reading captured at the beginning of the test, before any adjustments or repairs. Represents the meter state as found in the field or upon receipt at the test facility. Measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).
Meter register reading captured at the conclusion of the test, after any adjustments, calibrations, or repairs. Represents the meter state after corrective action. Measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).

Calculated billing adjustment amount resulting from the meter test, measured in local currency. Positive values indicate customer credit (meter was over-registering); negative values indicate back-billing (meter was under-registering). Calculated based on accuracy error, consumption history, and regulatory back-billing limits.

Indicates whether the test results require a billing adjustment (back-billing or credit). True if meter was found out of tolerance and billing correction is needed; false otherwise. Triggers downstream billing adjustment workflow.

Standardized code representing the corrective action taken. None indicates meter passed without adjustment; calibrated indicates meter was adjusted to meet accuracy standards; repaired indicates component-level repair; replaced indicates meter was swapped; sealed indicates new tamper seal applied; retired indicates meter removed from service.

Description of any corrective action performed on the meter following the test. May include calibration adjustments, component replacement, seal replacement, or meter replacement. Empty if no action was required (meter passed as-found).
Date and time when this meter test record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.
Date on which the customer was notified of the test results. Required for regulatory compliance when test results trigger billing adjustments or service actions.

Indicates whether the customer was notified of the test results. True if notification was sent; false if not yet notified. Required for customer-requested tests and tests resulting in billing adjustments.

Standardized code categorizing the failure mode. Examples include accuracy-out-of-tolerance, display-failure, communication-failure, mechanical-damage, tampering-detected, seal-broken, internal-component-failure. Empty if meter passed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: accuracy_out_of_tolerance|display_failure|communication_failure|mechanical_damage|tampering_detected|seal_broken|internal_component_failure|environmental_damage|calibration_drift|manufacturing_defect — promote to reference product]

Detailed description of why the meter failed the test, if applicable. May include root cause analysis such as component wear, environmental damage, tampering, manufacturing defect, or calibration drift. Empty if meter passed.

Power factor applied during the test, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. Represents the phase relationship between voltage and current. Unity power factor (1.0) represents purely resistive load; lagging power factor (e.g., 0.5 lag) simulates inductive loads common in industrial settings.

Indicates whether the test results have been included in regulatory reporting to the Public Utility Commission (PUC). True if reported; false if pending. Required for periodic meter testing compliance reports.
reference: State PUC Meter Testing Reporting Requirements

description: The maximum allowable percentage error defined by the applicable regulatory standard. Meters exceeding this tolerance fail the test and require adjustment or replacement. Typical values range from ±2% to ±3% depending on meter class and jurisdiction.
reference: ANSI C12.1, State PUC Meter Accuracy Requirements

description: Total cost incurred to perform the meter test, including labor, equipment usage, and materials. Measured in local currency. Used for cost recovery and regulatory rate case support.

Current level applied during the meter test, measured in amperes. Test standards typically specify light load, full load, and heavy load current levels to validate accuracy across the meter's operating range.
The date on which the meter test was performed. This is the principal business event timestamp for the test.
Total time required to complete the meter test, measured in minutes. Includes setup, test execution, and teardown. Used for labor costing and scheduling optimization.
Reference to the test equipment or meter test bench used to perform the test. Links to the asset registry for calibration tracking and equipment certification.
Serial number of the test equipment used. Captured for traceability and to ensure test equipment is within its calibration period.
Reference to the facility or service center where the test was performed. Links to the facility registry for location tracking and certification management.

The known reference load applied during the test, measured in kilowatt-hours. This is the standard energy quantity used to calculate meter accuracy by comparing the meter's measured value against this reference.

Physical location where the meter test was conducted. Field indicates in-situ testing at the customer premise; shop indicates utility service center; laboratory indicates independent testing facility; customer-premise indicates on-site testing; service-center indicates utility-operated test facility.
Free-form notes captured by the test technician. May include observations about meter condition, environmental factors, customer interactions, or any anomalies encountered during testing.
Business identifier for the meter test, typically assigned by the testing system or laboratory. Used for external reference and tracking.

Overall pass/fail determination for the meter test based on regulatory accuracy thresholds. Pass indicates meter meets accuracy standards; fail indicates meter is out of tolerance; inconclusive means test could not produce a definitive result.

The regulatory or industry standard used to conduct and evaluate the meter test. Typically references ANSI C12.1, ANSI C12.20, or state Public Utility Commission (PUC) meter testing requirements. Defines the accuracy thresholds and test procedures applied.
reference: ANSI C12.1, ANSI C12.20, State PUC Regulations

description: Current lifecycle status of the meter test. Scheduled indicates the test is planned; in-progress means testing is underway; completed indicates test finished successfully; cancelled means test was aborted; failed indicates test could not be completed due to technical issues; pending-review means results await validation.
Full name of the technician who performed the meter test. Captured for audit trail and regulatory reporting purposes.
Precise date and time when the meter test was initiated, including time zone. Provides granular event tracking for audit and scheduling purposes.

Classification of the meter test. In-service tests are conducted in the field without removing the meter; shop tests are performed in a controlled laboratory environment; referee tests are independent third-party tests to resolve disputes; customer-requested tests are initiated by customer complaint; post-complaint tests follow service quality issues; periodic tests meet regulatory schedules; installation tests verify new meter accuracy; removal tests validate meter condition at decommissioning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: in_service|shop|referee|customer_requested|post_complaint|periodic|installation|removal — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: ANSI C12.1 - Code for Electricity Metering

description: Voltage level applied during the meter test, measured in volts. Typically matches the meter's rated voltage (e.g., 120V, 240V, 480V) to simulate field operating conditions.
Date and time when this meter test record was last modified. Audit trail field for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

Foreign key linking to interconnection.der_system. Business justification: Tracks DER-owning customers experiencing outages for NEM credit adjustments (energy not exported during outage), performance guarantee calculations, and regulatory reporting (CPUC Rule 21 requires tra
Identifier of the substation serving this customer service point at the time of the outage. Used for substation-level reliability performance reporting and asset management correlation.
