description: Name or code of the business unit or department (e.g., T&D Engineering, Asset Management, Construction) that initiated the planned outage window request. Used for resource allocation and OPEX/CAPEX tracking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA; Ventyx Asset Suite; internal organizational taxonomy

description: Indicates whether the planned outage must be reported to the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) due to transmission-level impact or market implications under NERC/FERC requirements.

Outage coordination identifier assigned by the RTO or ISO (e.g., MISO, PJM, CAISO) when the planned outage is registered in the transmission outage coordination system. Populated only when rto_iso_notification_required is true.
reference: NERC FAC-002; FERC; RTO/ISO outage coordination procedures

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Contribution (Minutes)
description: Contribution of this planned outage window to the annual System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) in customer-minutes per customer served. Calculated as (actual_duration_minutes × affected_customer_count) / total_customers_served. Used for IEEE 1366 reliability reporting.
reference: IEEE 1366; State PUC reliability reporting; NERC

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Contribution
description: Contribution of this planned outage window to the annual System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), calculated as affected_customer_count / total_customers_served. Used for IEEE 1366 reliability performance reporting to PUC.
reference: IEEE 1366; State PUC reliability reporting; NERC

description: Code identifying the regulated service territory within which the planned outage window occurs. Used for PUC jurisdictional reporting, rate case filings, and geographic performance analysis.
reference: State PUC CPCN; FERC; internal service territory taxonomy

description: Indicates whether this planned outage window is associated with a declared storm or major event, which may qualify for IEEE 1366 major event day (MED) exclusion from SAIDI/SAIFI reliability index calculations.
reference: IEEE 1366 Major Event Day criteria; State PUC reliability rules

description: Reference number of the switching order issued in the ADMS or OMS to execute the de-energization and re-energization sequence for this planned outage window. Links to the operational switching workflow.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS; IEEE C37.96; NERC FAC-002

description: FK to outage.outage_event.outage_event_id — Planned maintenance windows result in planned outage events. This FK links the scheduling/approval workflow to the actual outage event record.
Nominal operating voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the network segment being de-energized. Determines safety protocols, crew qualifications, and regulatory notification thresholds.
reference: IEC 60038; IEEE C57; NERC FAC-002; OSHA 1910.269

description: Free-text description of the maintenance, construction, or upgrade activity to be performed during the planned outage window. Provides context for crew briefings, customer communications, and regulatory filings.
reference: Ventyx Asset Suite; SAP S/4HANA PM; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Reference number of the associated work order in the asset management or ERP system (e.g., SAP S/4HANA PM or Ventyx Asset Suite) that drives the maintenance, construction, or upgrade activity requiring de-energization.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance; Ventyx Asset Suite Work Management

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the outage prediction record. Primary key for this entity in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Outage Management Module

description: Identifier of the primary distribution circuit predicted to be affected by the outage. Sourced from the GIS network model and used for crew routing and switching order preparation.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network — Network Modeling; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Identifier of the substation associated with the predicted outage scope. Used for crew dispatch routing and switching order coordination.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network — Network Modeling; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Identifier of the system operator or dispatcher who created or last modified this prediction record when prediction_source is 'dispatcher_manual'. Provides accountability and audit trail for manually-entered predictions.
reference: NERC CIP-004 — Personnel and Training; SOX Section 404

description: Identifier of the distribution feeder predicted to be affected. A feeder is a primary distribution line segment fed from a substation bus. Used for network topology analysis and switching order preparation.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network — Network Modeling; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Foreign key linking to forecast.load. Business justification: Predictive outage management systems integrate load forecasts to estimate customer impact (count, MW interrupted) and prioritize response. Advanced OMS platforms reference specific load forecast runs

Externally-known identifier assigned by the Outage Management System (OMS) to the predicted outage event. Used to correlate this prediction record with the OMS event lifecycle and downstream actual outage records.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Outage Management Module; NERC CIP-014

description: Identifier of the predictive analytics model version that generated this prediction, when prediction_source is 'predictive_model'. Enables model performance tracking, auditability, and retraining feedback loops.
reference: DOE Grid Modernization Initiative; GE PowerOn ADMS — Predictive Analytics

description: Identifier of the SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) alarm that triggered or corroborated this outage prediction. Provides traceability back to the real-time operational data historian (OSIsoft PI) or ADMS alarm log.
reference: OSIsoft PI — SCADA Integration; GE PowerOn ADMS; NERC CIP-007

description: Reference to the regulated service territory within which the predicted outage falls. Used for regulatory reporting to State Public Utility Commissions (PUCs) and SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI performance tracking.
reference: State PUC Service Territory Regulations; IEEE 1366

description: Reference to the storm or major weather event record associated with this prediction, if applicable. Links the prediction to the storm response management workflow for resource mobilization and regulatory major event day (MED) classification.
reference: IEEE 1366 — Major Event Day (MED) Classification; State PUC Storm Reporting

description: Foreign key linking to forecast.weather_input. Business justification: Outage prediction models consume weather forecast inputs (wind speed, precipitation, temperature) to predict storm-related outage likelihood and severity. Utilities use this linkage for storm prepared

Number of Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meters within the predicted outage scope that contributed last-gasp or ping-failure signals to the prediction. Indicates the AMI signal density supporting the prediction confidence.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — Meter Reading; AMI/MDM Integration

description: Numeric confidence score (0.00–100.00) representing the model's or system's certainty in the predicted outage scope, cause, and affected area. Higher values indicate greater confidence. Used to prioritize crew dispatch and ETR communication decisions.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Predictive Analytics; DOE Grid Modernization Initiative

description: Audit timestamp recording when this outage prediction record was first persisted in the data platform. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Indicates whether field crews have been pre-positioned based on this outage prediction prior to field confirmation of the actual outage. When True, crew dispatch records are linked to this prediction in the workforce management system.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Outage Management; Ventyx Asset Suite — Work Management

description: Indicates whether the predicted outage scope includes one or more critical customers (e.g., hospitals, emergency services, life-support customers, large industrial accounts with SLA obligations). When True, triggers priority restoration protocols and mandatory customer notification.
reference: State PUC Critical Customer Regulations; NERC CIP-014

description: Number of inbound customer outage calls received and clustered to generate or corroborate this prediction. Used to assess the customer-reported signal strength and prioritize crew dispatch.
reference: SAP IS-U — CIS; Oracle Utilities CC&B — Customer Management

description: Indicates whether the predicted outage scope includes Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) such as rooftop solar, battery storage, or microgrids that may be islanded or require isolation procedures. When True, DERMS coordination is required.
reference: IEEE 1547 — DER Interconnection; FERC Order 2222; NERC CIP-014

description: Date and time after which this prediction is considered stale and should no longer be used for crew dispatch or ETR communication without refresh. Typically set to a configurable window (e.g., 2 hours) after prediction_timestamp. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Outage Management Module

business_glossary_term: Fault Location Isolation and Service Restoration (FLISR) Eligible Flag
description: Indicates whether the predicted outage scope is within a network segment eligible for automated Fault Location, Isolation, and Service Restoration (FLISR) execution via the ADMS. When True, automated switching sequences may be initiated without manual dispatcher intervention.

Indicates whether this prediction is associated with a Major Event Day (MED) as defined by IEEE 1366. MED events are excluded from standard SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI calculations and reported separately to state PUCs and NERC.
reference: IEEE 1366 — Major Event Day Classification; State PUC Reliability Reporting; NERC

description: Indicates whether the predicted outage scope includes customers enrolled in a medical baseline or life-support program. When True, triggers mandatory proactive notification and priority restoration per state PUC regulations.
reference: State PUC Medical Baseline / Life Support Customer Regulations

description: Indicates whether an outage notification has been sent to affected customers based on this prediction. When True, the notification timestamp and channel are tracked in the customer notification log. Supports state PUC notification compliance reporting.
reference: State PUC Customer Notification Requirements; NAESB Business Practices

description: Date and time at which the first customer notification was dispatched based on this outage prediction. Used for state PUC compliance reporting on notification timeliness. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Classification of the predicted outage by its nature. 'unplanned' = unexpected equipment or system failure; 'planned' = scheduled maintenance window; 'storm' = weather-driven event; 'momentary' = predicted to be a brief interruption (< 5 minutes per IEEE 1366); 'sustained' = predicted to exceed the momentary threshold.
reference: IEEE 1366 — Guide for Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices

description: Comma-delimited list of distribution circuit segment identifiers predicted to be de-energized. Sourced from the GIS network model topology analysis. Used for switching order preparation and crew routing.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network — Network Modeling; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Standardized cause code representing the predicted root cause of the outage at time of initial assessment (e.g., equipment failure, tree contact, animal contact, weather, vehicle accident, unknown). Aligned with IEEE 1366 cause code taxonomy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equipment_failure|tree_contact|animal_contact|weather|vehicle_accident|planned_maintenance|unknown|overload|lightning|ice_loading — promote to reference product]
reference: IEEE 1366 — Guide for Electric Power Distribution Reliability Indices; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Free-text narrative describing the predicted cause of the outage as assessed at the time of prediction creation. Supplements the structured cause code with dispatcher or model-generated context.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Outage Management Module

description: Estimated number of customers predicted to be without power based on the initial assessment. Used for crew pre-positioning, ETR communication, and SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI impact estimation. Distinct from the confirmed customer count on the actual outage event record.
reference: IEEE 1366 — SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI; State PUC Reliability Reporting

description: Initial estimated date and time by which power is predicted to be restored to affected customers. Communicated to customers and field crews at the time of prediction creation. Distinct from the revised ETR updated during active restoration. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: State PUC Customer Notification Requirements; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: WGS-84 decimal latitude coordinate of the predicted fault location. Used for GIS-based crew dispatch and outage mapping.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; WGS-84 Coordinate Reference System

description: Predicted geographic or network location of the fault, expressed as a GIS asset identifier, address, or coordinate reference. Used to direct first-responder crews to the most probable fault point before field confirmation.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network — Outage Analysis; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: WGS-84 decimal longitude coordinate of the predicted fault location. Used for GIS-based crew dispatch and outage mapping.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; WGS-84 Coordinate Reference System

description: Estimated megawatts (MW) of load predicted to be interrupted based on the affected circuit segments and customer mix. Used for grid operations impact assessment and load restoration prioritization.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Outage Management; NERC TPL Standards

description: Estimated duration of the outage in minutes as assessed at the time of prediction creation. Derived from historical restoration times for similar cause codes and circuit configurations. Used for CAIDI estimation and crew resource planning.
reference: IEEE 1366 — CAIDI; State PUC Reliability Reporting

description: The originating signal or mechanism that triggered the outage prediction. 'ami_ping' = Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) last-gasp or ping failure; 'scada_alarm' = SCADA system alarm from field device; 'customer_call_cluster' = clustering of inbound customer outage calls; 'predictive_model' = ML/analytics model output; 'dispatcher_manual' = manually entered by a system operator or dispatcher; 'smart_meter_outage_notification' = direct outage notification from smart meter.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM — Meter Reading; GE PowerOn ADMS; NERC CIP-014

description: Current lifecycle state of the outage prediction record. 'pending' = generated but not yet dispatched; 'active' = in use for crew pre-positioning and ETR communication; 'confirmed' = field crew has validated the predicted scope; 'superseded' = replaced by a newer prediction; 'cancelled' = prediction voided before confirmation; 'expired' = prediction window elapsed without field confirmation.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Outage Management Module

description: The date and time at which the outage prediction was system-generated or dispatcher-created. Represents the principal real-world event time for this prediction record. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — Outage Management Module; IEEE 1366

description: Version string of the predictive analytics model that generated this prediction. Used alongside predictive_model_id for model governance, auditability, and performance benchmarking.
reference: DOE Grid Modernization Initiative; SOX Section 404

description: The protection zone or relay zone within which the predicted fault is located. Used by switching order coordinators to identify the correct protective device (recloser, fuse, breaker) to operate for isolation and restoration.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS — FLISR; IEEE C37 — Protective Relaying

description: Code identifying the operational system of record that originated this outage prediction record. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and Silver Layer provenance tracking.
reference: SOX Section 404; GE PowerOn ADMS; OSIsoft PI; Oracle Utilities MDM

description: Audit timestamp recording when this outage prediction record was last modified in the data platform. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
Voltage classification of the network segment predicted to be affected. Determines the severity tier, crew qualification requirements, and regulatory reporting category.
reference: IEC 60038 — Standard Voltages; IEEE C57; NERC FAC Standards

description: Standardized code representing the weather conditions at the time of prediction creation (e.g., clear, wind, ice, lightning, flood). Used for cause analysis, storm classification, and reliability reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|wind|ice|lightning|flood|snow|extreme_heat|fog|tornado|hurricane — promote to reference product]
reference: IEEE 1366 — Major Event Day Classification; NOAA Weather Classification

description: Recorded or forecast wind speed in miles per hour at the predicted fault location at the time of prediction creation. Used for storm severity assessment and major event day (MED) classification.
reference: IEEE 1366 — Major Event Day Classification; NOAA

business_glossary_term: Public Utility Commission (PUC) Outage Report ID
description: Unique surrogate identifier for each PUC outage report record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
reference: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reporting Requirements

description: Reference to the underlying outage event that triggered this PUC regulatory report. Links the formal filing to the operational outage record in the Outage Management System (OMS).

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: PUC outage reports are a specific type of regulatory filing with docket numbers, submission tracking, and approval workflows. Compliance teams manage outage reports within the broader regulatory filin

business_glossary_term: Superseded By PUC Outage Report ID
description: Reference to the newer puc_outage_report_id that supersedes this record when a corrected or amended report has been filed. Null if this is the current active version. Enables version chain traversal for audit purposes.

Date and time when this report was actually submitted to the state PUC. Compared against filing_deadline_timestamp to determine on-time compliance. This is the principal business event timestamp for the report transaction.

Comma-separated list of county names within the utility service territory that experienced customer interruptions during this outage event. Required by many state PUCs for geographic impact assessment and emergency management coordination.

Description of the geographic service territory area impacted by the outage, such as county names, city names, or distribution circuit identifiers. Used in PUC reports to communicate the geographic scope of the event to regulators.

Free-text narrative description of the root cause of the outage event as submitted in the PUC report. Provides detailed explanation beyond the cause category code, including contributing factors, sequence of events, and any relevant environmental or equipment conditions.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004

description: Target completion date for the corrective action plan committed to in the final PUC report. Used for regulatory follow-up tracking and compliance monitoring.

Free-text description of the corrective actions taken or planned to prevent recurrence of the outage event. Required in final PUC reports. Includes infrastructure improvements, maintenance program changes, vegetation management, and operational procedure updates.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004

description: Date and time when this PUC outage report record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer. Represents the audit trail creation timestamp for data governance and lineage tracking.

Total number of customer accounts that experienced an interruption during this outage event. Used to determine whether the event meets PUC reportable customer threshold (e.g., >50,000 customers) and for System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) calculations.
reference: IEEE 1366; State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004

description: Number of customer accounts that have been restored to service as of the time this report was filed. For final reports, this should equal customers_affected_count. For initial and update reports, tracks restoration progress.

Estimated date and time by which all affected customers are expected to be restored, as reported in initial and update PUC filings. The Estimated Time of Restoration (ETR) is a key metric for customer communication and regulatory scrutiny during major events.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; OMS Best Practices

description: Regulatory deadline by which this report type (initial, update, or final) must be submitted to the state PUC. Calculated based on outage_start_timestamp and the applicable PUC reporting rules for the jurisdiction. Used for compliance monitoring and SLA tracking.
Indicates whether the report was submitted to the PUC at or before the filing_deadline_timestamp. Used for regulatory compliance tracking, internal audit, and PUC performance reporting.

Indicates whether this outage occurred on a day classified as a Major Event Day (MED) per IEEE 1366 beta method. MED events are typically excluded from SAIDI/SAIFI baseline calculations but must still be reported to the PUC separately.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reportable Flag
description: Indicates whether this outage event also meets NERC EOP-004 reporting thresholds and has been or must be filed with NERC in addition to the state PUC. Enables cross-regulatory compliance tracking.

Indicates whether this outage was caused by or associated with a declared storm event. Storm-related outages may have different PUC reporting requirements, extended restoration time allowances, and separate cost recovery treatment.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004

description: Number of customers registered on the utility's life support or medical baseline program who were affected by this outage. PUC regulations typically require special notification and prioritized restoration for life support customers, and this count is a required field in many state PUC outage reports.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; PUC Life Support Rules

description: Indicates whether mutual aid assistance from other utilities was requested and activated in response to this outage event. Mutual aid activation is a reportable fact in many state PUC major event reports and NERC EOP-004 filings.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004; ESOP

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Event Report Number
description: NERC-assigned event report number for the corresponding NERC EOP-004 filing, when applicable. Enables cross-referencing between the state PUC report and the federal NERC submission for the same outage event.

Reference number of the corresponding incident record in the Outage Management System (OMS), specifically GE PowerOn ADMS. Enables traceability between the regulatory PUC report and the operational OMS incident record.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS; OMS Integration Standards

description: High-level cause category for the outage event as reported to the PUC. Derived from the OMS outage cause classification and mapped to PUC-required cause taxonomy. Distinct from the detailed cause code in the outage_cause reference product.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; IEEE 1366; NERC EOP-004

description: Total duration of the outage event in minutes, measured from outage_start_timestamp to outage_end_timestamp. Used to assess whether the event meets PUC reportable duration thresholds (e.g., >8 hours) and for SAIDI/CAIDI reliability index calculations.
reference: IEEE 1366; State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004

description: Date and time when the last affected customer was restored and the outage event was officially closed. Used to calculate total outage duration for SAIDI/CAIDI reporting and to confirm restoration completion.
reference: NERC EOP-004; State PUC Reporting Requirements; IEEE 1366

description: Date and time when the reportable outage event began, as recorded in the Outage Management System (OMS). This is the principal real-world event time used to calculate outage duration and filing deadline compliance.
reference: NERC EOP-004; State PUC Reporting Requirements; IEEE 1366

description: Classification of the outage by the level of the electric grid affected. Transmission-level events typically have lower PUC reporting thresholds than distribution events. Used to route reports to the appropriate regulatory body and apply correct reporting rules.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004; FERC

description: Full name of the utility employee responsible for preparing and submitting this PUC outage report. Required for regulatory accountability and as the point of contact for PUC inquiries about the filing.
Direct phone number of the utility employee who prepared this PUC outage report. Provided to the PUC as the contact number for follow-up questions regarding the filing.

Job title of the utility employee who prepared this PUC outage report (e.g., 'Manager, Regulatory Affairs', 'Director, Grid Operations'). Required by some PUCs to confirm appropriate organizational authority for the filing.

Status of the PUC's formal acknowledgment or acceptance of this report filing. 'pending' indicates awaiting PUC response; 'acknowledged' indicates receipt confirmed; 'accepted' indicates formally accepted without deficiency; 'rejected' indicates returned with deficiency notice requiring resubmission.
Date and time when the state PUC formally acknowledged or responded to this report filing. Null if acknowledgment has not yet been received.
Official docket or case number assigned by the state PUC upon receipt of the outage report. Used for tracking the regulatory proceeding and all subsequent correspondence with the commission.
reference: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reporting Requirements

description: Two-letter US state code identifying the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) to which this report is filed. Determines applicable reporting thresholds, deadlines, and format requirements.
reference: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reporting Requirements

description: Free-text description of the reason provided by the PUC for rejecting or returning this report filing. Populated only when puc_acknowledgment_status is 'rejected'. Used to guide corrective resubmission.
FK to outage.outage_event.outage_event_id — PUC reports are filed for specific qualifying outage events. Must link to the event(s) being reported for regulatory traceability.

Externally-known, human-readable report identifier assigned by the reporting utility and submitted to the state PUC. Used as the official reference number in all regulatory correspondence and acknowledgment tracking (e.g., PUC-2024-OUT-00123).
reference: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reporting Requirements

description: Current lifecycle status of this regulatory report filing. 'draft' indicates preparation in progress; 'submitted' indicates filed with PUC; 'acknowledged' indicates PUC receipt confirmed; 'accepted' indicates PUC formally accepted; 'rejected' indicates PUC returned for correction; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a subsequent filing.
reference: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reporting Requirements

description: Indicates the filing stage of this report submission: 'initial' (first notification within required timeframe), 'update' (interim progress report), or 'final' (complete post-restoration report with root cause and corrective actions). Multiple report types may exist per outage event.
reference: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004

description: Sequential version number of this report record, incremented each time the report is revised and resubmitted to the PUC. Version 1 represents the original submission; subsequent versions represent amendments or corrections.
Legal name of the electric utility entity filing this PUC outage report. Required on all regulatory submissions to identify the responsible regulated entity.
reference: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reporting Requirements; FERC

business_glossary_term: Reporting Utility North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) ID
description: NERC-assigned registered entity identifier for the reporting utility. Used to cross-reference NERC EOP-004 filings and to uniquely identify the utility across multi-state regulatory submissions.

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Contribution (Minutes)
description: This outage event's contribution to the utility's System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI), calculated as (customer_interruption_minutes / total_customers_served). Reported to the PUC as part of annual reliability performance metrics.

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Contribution
description: This outage event's contribution to the utility's System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), calculated as (customers_affected / total_customers_served). Reported to the PUC as part of annual reliability performance metrics.
FK to outage.outage_event.outage_event_id — PUC reports are filed for specific qualifying outage events. Required for regulatory compliance tracking.
Date and time when this PUC outage report record was last modified in the lakehouse silver layer. Used for incremental data processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance.

Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the highest-voltage facility involved in the outage event. Used to classify the outage as transmission-level (typically ≥69 kV) or distribution-level, which determines applicable PUC and NERC reporting thresholds.
reference: NERC EOP-004; State PUC Reporting Requirements; IEEE

description: Primary key for reliability_index_period

Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reporting is mandated by specific PUC obligations with defined performance thresholds and filing deadlines. Regulatory affairs maps each reporting period to the governing obligation

Free-text description of the reason for amending or recomputing this reliability index period record (e.g., data correction from OMS, reclassification of MED events, customer count correction). Required for version_number greater than 1. Supports regulatory audit trail and PUC amendment filing documentation.
reference: State PUC Amendment Reporting Requirements; SOX Internal Controls

description: Identifier or name of the authorized utility employee (typically a Reliability Engineer or Director of Grid Operations) who approved this reliability index period record for regulatory filing. Supports SOX internal control documentation and regulatory audit requirements.
reference: SOX Section 302 and 906 (Management Certification); State PUC Audit Requirements; NERC Compliance

description: Date and time when this reliability index period record was formally approved for regulatory filing. Supports SOX internal control audit trails and regulatory submission documentation.
reference: SOX Section 302; State PUC Audit Requirements; NERC Compliance Documentation

business_glossary_term: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) in Minutes
description: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index expressed in minutes per interruption. Computed as total_customer_minutes_interrupted divided by total_customer_interruptions (equivalently, SAIDI divided by SAIFI). Represents the average duration of each interruption experienced by affected customers. Used to assess restoration performance.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.3; NERC Reliability Standards; State PUC Reporting Requirements

business_glossary_term: IEEE 1366 Normalized CAIDI (Excluding Major Event Days) in Minutes
description: CAIDI value computed after excluding Major Event Day (MED) interruptions per IEEE 1366 normalization methodology. Derived from normalized SAIDI and SAIFI values. Used for PUC performance standard compliance and restoration performance benchmarking.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.4; State PUC Performance Standards

description: Identifies the specific computational methodology applied to derive the reliability indices in this record. IEEE_1366_STANDARD applies the full IEEE 1366 methodology including MEDs; IEEE_1366_MED_EXCLUDED applies the normalized MED-excluded methodology; PUC_CUSTOM applies a state-specific PUC-mandated variation; NERC_BENCHMARK applies NERC benchmarking methodology.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Date and time when this reliability index period record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and SOX internal control requirements.
reference: SOX Internal Controls; IEEE Std 1366-2012; State PUC Audit Requirements

description: Total number of customers served within the reporting entity boundary during the reporting period. This is the denominator used in SAIDI and SAIFI index calculations per IEEE 1366. Typically represents the average or end-of-period customer count as defined by the applicable PUC methodology.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.1; State PUC Reporting Requirements

description: Number of outage events during the reporting period caused by equipment failure (excluding storm and third-party causes). Supports asset reliability analysis, maintenance planning, and capital investment justification for aging infrastructure programs.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; Ventyx Asset Suite Work Management; State PUC Reliability Reporting

description: Actual date on which this reliability index period record was submitted to the applicable regulatory authority. Null if not yet filed. Used to verify on-time filing compliance and support regulatory audit trails.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards EOP-004; SOX Compliance

description: Deadline date by which this reliability index period record must be submitted to the applicable regulatory authority (PUC or NERC). Used to track filing compliance and trigger workflow notifications. Determined by PUC tariff or NERC standard reporting schedule.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards EOP-004; FERC Reporting Requirements

description: Current lifecycle state of the reliability index period record in the regulatory submission workflow. DRAFT indicates preliminary computation; UNDER_REVIEW indicates internal QA; APPROVED indicates sign-off for submission; FILED indicates submission to PUC or NERC; AMENDED indicates a corrected re-submission; SUPERSEDED indicates replaced by a newer version.
reference: State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards EOP-004; SOX Internal Controls

description: Date and time when this reliability index period record was most recently modified. Tracks amendments, recomputations, and corrections to the reliability indices. Supports audit trail and regulatory amendment documentation.
reference: SOX Internal Controls; State PUC Amendment Reporting Requirements; IEEE Std 1366-2012

description: Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index computed as total momentary customer interruptions divided by customers served. Measures the frequency of brief power interruptions (five minutes or less) per customer. Increasingly required by PUCs as a power quality metric alongside SAIDI and SAIFI.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.5; State PUC Power Quality Reporting Requirements

description: Number of calendar days during the reporting period that qualified as Major Event Days (MEDs) per the IEEE 1366 beta + 2.5 sigma threshold methodology. Used to assess storm and extreme weather impact on reliability performance.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.4; State PUC Reporting Requirements

business_glossary_term: Major Event Day (MED) Excluded Customer Interruptions
description: Total customer interruptions attributable to Major Event Days (MEDs) that are excluded from the normalized IEEE 1366 index calculations. MEDs are days where the daily SAIDI exceeds a statistically derived threshold (beta + 2.5 sigma). Tracking this separately enables both total and MED-excluded reporting as required by most PUCs.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.4 (Major Event Day definition); State PUC Reporting Requirements

business_glossary_term: Major Event Day (MED) Excluded Customer Minutes Interrupted
description: Total customer minutes interrupted attributable to Major Event Days (MEDs) that are excluded from the normalized IEEE 1366 index calculations. Used to compute MED-normalized SAIDI and SAIFI values required for PUC regulatory filings and NERC benchmarking.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.4; State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards

business_glossary_term: Major Event Day (MED) SAIDI Threshold in Minutes
description: The computed daily SAIDI threshold (beta + 2.5 sigma) used to classify a calendar day as a Major Event Day for this reporting period. Derived from the five-year historical daily SAIDI distribution per IEEE 1366 methodology. Documents the MED classification boundary applied to this period.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.4; State PUC Reporting Requirements

description: Total number of momentary interruptions (duration five minutes or less per IEEE 1366 definition) experienced by customers during the reporting period. Used to compute MAIFI (Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index) and assess power quality performance.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.5 (MAIFI definition); State PUC Power Quality Reporting Requirements

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Registered Entity ID
description: NERC Compliance Registry identifier for the utility entity responsible for this reliability report. Required for NERC reliability standard compliance submissions and benchmarking participation. Aligns with the NERC Transmission Planner, Distribution Provider, or Load-Serving Entity registration.
reference: NERC Compliance Registry; NERC Reliability Standards EOP-004; FERC Order 693

business_glossary_term: Outage Management System (OMS) Source System Code
description: Identifier of the Outage Management System (OMS) instance from which the underlying outage event data was sourced for this reliability index computation. Supports data lineage tracing back to GE PowerOn ADMS or equivalent OMS. Critical for audit and regulatory filing validation.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS OMS Integration; SOX Data Lineage Requirements; State PUC Audit Requirements

description: Calendar date marking the inclusive end of the reliability reporting period. Combined with period_start_date to define the exact window over which SAIDI, SAIFI, and CAIDI indices are computed.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; FERC Form 1; State PUC Annual Reliability Report

description: Calendar date marking the inclusive start of the reliability reporting period. Combined with period_end_date to define the exact window over which SAIDI, SAIFI, and CAIDI indices are computed.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; FERC Form 1; State PUC Annual Reliability Report

description: Classification of the reporting period granularity. Determines the aggregation window for SAIDI, SAIFI, and CAIDI index calculations. MONTHLY is used for operational monitoring; QUARTERLY and ANNUAL are used for PUC regulatory filings; ROLLING_12_MONTH is used for NERC benchmarking.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4; NERC Reliability Standards EOP-004; State PUC Reporting Requirements

description: Customer minutes interrupted attributable to planned (scheduled maintenance) outage events during the reporting period. Some PUC jurisdictions require separate reporting of planned vs. unplanned interruptions. Enables decomposition of total CMI into planned and unplanned components.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 3.2 (planned interruption definition); State PUC Reporting Requirements

description: SAIDI value from the immediately preceding equivalent reporting period (e.g., prior month, prior quarter, prior year) for the same reporting entity. Stored on the record to support period-over-period variance analysis in regulatory filings without requiring a self-join.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; State PUC Annual Reliability Report; NERC Reliability Benchmarking

description: SAIFI value from the immediately preceding equivalent reporting period for the same reporting entity. Stored on the record to support period-over-period variance analysis in regulatory filings without requiring a self-join.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; State PUC Annual Reliability Report; NERC Reliability Benchmarking

description: Two-letter state code plus PUC suffix identifying the state Public Utility Commission jurisdiction under which this reliability index period record is filed (e.g., CA-PUC, NY-PUC, TX-PUC). Determines applicable performance standards, reporting formats, and filing deadlines.
reference: State Public Utility Commission Regulations; NERC Compliance Registry; FERC Jurisdictional Boundaries

business_glossary_term: Public Utility Commission (PUC) SAIDI Performance Target in Minutes
description: Regulatory SAIDI performance target (in minutes) established by the applicable state PUC for the reporting period and reporting entity. Used to assess compliance with performance-based rate mechanisms and potential penalty or incentive triggers. Null if no PUC target applies to this reporting level.
reference: State PUC Performance-Based Ratemaking Orders; State PUC Reliability Standards

business_glossary_term: Public Utility Commission (PUC) SAIFI Performance Target
description: Regulatory SAIFI performance target established by the applicable state PUC for the reporting period and reporting entity. Used to assess compliance with performance-based rate mechanisms and potential penalty or incentive triggers. Null if no PUC target applies to this reporting level.
reference: State PUC Performance-Based Ratemaking Orders; State PUC Reliability Standards

business_glossary_term: Public Utility Commission (PUC) Performance Target Met Indicator
description: Indicates whether the utility met all applicable PUC reliability performance targets (SAIDI and SAIFI) for this reporting period and reporting entity. True if all applicable targets were met; False if one or more targets were missed. Null if no PUC targets apply. Drives performance-based rate adjustment calculations.
reference: State PUC Performance-Based Ratemaking Orders; State PUC Reliability Standards

description: Business identifier for the specific entity (circuit ID, substation code, PUC territory code, operating area code, or system-level identifier) at which the reliability indices are reported. Corresponds to the reporting_level classification. For SYSTEM level, this is the utility NERC registered entity identifier.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; NERC Compliance Registry; State PUC Service Territory Definitions

description: Human-readable name of the reporting entity (e.g., circuit name, substation name, PUC territory name, operating area name). Used for display in regulatory filings and reliability performance dashboards.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; State PUC Reporting Requirements

description: Organizational or geographic granularity at which the reliability indices are computed and reported. SYSTEM represents the full utility service territory; CIRCUIT and SUBSTATION represent distribution-level granularity; PUC_TERRITORY aligns with regulatory jurisdiction boundaries; OPERATING_AREA represents internal operational divisions.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 5; State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Externally-known business identifier for the reporting period, encoding the period type and calendar reference (e.g., MONTHLY-2024-03, QUARTERLY-2024-Q1, ANNUAL-2024). Used as the primary business key for regulatory filings and cross-system reconciliation.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; NERC Reliability Standards; State PUC Reporting Requirements

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) in Minutes
description: System Average Interruption Duration Index expressed in minutes per customer. Computed as total_customer_minutes_interrupted divided by customers_served. Represents the average total duration of interruptions experienced per customer during the reporting period. Primary reliability metric for PUC regulatory filings and NERC benchmarking.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.1; NERC Reliability Standards; State PUC Reporting Requirements

business_glossary_term: IEEE 1366 Normalized SAIDI (Excluding Major Event Days) in Minutes
description: SAIDI value computed after excluding Major Event Day (MED) interruptions per IEEE 1366 normalization methodology. Computed as (total_customer_minutes_interrupted minus med_excluded_customer_minutes) divided by customers_served. This is the primary metric used for year-over-year performance benchmarking and PUC performance standard compliance.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.4; State PUC Performance Standards; NERC Reliability Benchmarking

description: System Average Interruption Frequency Index expressed as interruptions per customer. Computed as total_customer_interruptions divided by customers_served. Represents the average number of interruptions experienced per customer during the reporting period. Key reliability metric for PUC regulatory filings.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.2; NERC Reliability Standards; State PUC Reporting Requirements

business_glossary_term: IEEE 1366 Normalized SAIFI (Excluding Major Event Days)
description: SAIFI value computed after excluding Major Event Day (MED) interruptions per IEEE 1366 normalization methodology. Computed as (total_customer_interruptions minus med_excluded_customer_interruptions) divided by customers_served. Used for PUC performance standard compliance and NERC benchmarking.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.4; State PUC Performance Standards; NERC Reliability Benchmarking

description: Number of outage events during the reporting period that were classified as storm-related (weather-caused). Supports storm impact analysis, MED classification validation, and regulatory storm reporting requirements. Sourced from OMS event cause codes.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.4; State PUC Storm Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004

description: Number of outage events during the reporting period caused by third parties (e.g., vehicle accidents, dig-ins, animal contacts, vegetation encroachment by non-utility parties). Some PUC jurisdictions allow exclusion of third-party caused outages from performance standard calculations.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC EOP-004

description: Total number of customer interruptions (sum of customers affected across all outage events) during the reporting period. This is the numerator for SAIFI calculation. Each customer affected by each distinct outage event counts as one interruption.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.2 (SAIFI definition); State PUC Reporting Requirements

description: Sum of the product of customers affected multiplied by outage duration in minutes across all outage events in the reporting period. This is the numerator for SAIDI calculation, expressed in customer-minutes. Also referred to as Customer Minutes of Interruption (CMI) in regulatory filings.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 4.1 (SAIDI definition); State PUC Reporting Requirements; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Total number of distinct outage events (interruption incidents) that occurred within the reporting entity boundary during the reporting period. Provides context for interpreting SAIDI and SAIFI values and supports frequency-based reliability analysis.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012; GE PowerOn ADMS OMS Event Records; State PUC Reporting Requirements

description: Customer minutes interrupted attributable to unplanned (forced/fault) outage events during the reporting period. Unplanned interruptions are the primary driver of reliability index degradation and are the focus of most PUC performance standards.
reference: IEEE Std 1366-2012 Section 3.2; State PUC Performance Standards; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Sequential version number incremented each time this reliability index period record is amended or recomputed. Version 1 represents the initial filing; subsequent versions represent amendments. Supports regulatory amendment tracking and audit trail requirements.
reference: State PUC Amendment Reporting Requirements; SOX Internal Controls; IEEE Std 1366-2012

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the safety clearance record in the lakehouse. Primary key for the safety_clearance data product. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — a discrete, lifecycle-managed safety authorization event issued to protect field crews working on de-energized equipment.

Reference to the supervisor, lead dispatcher, or safety officer who approved the issuance of this safety clearance, where a dual-authorization workflow is required. May be the same as the issuing dispatcher in single-authority configurations.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; NERC FAC-001; NERC CIP-006

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.sox_control. Business justification: Safety clearance processes for critical infrastructure work may be subject to SOX internal controls over operational safety and asset protection. Internal audit tests safety clearance controls as part
Reference to the substation where the de-energized equipment covered by this clearance is located. Used for geographic scoping of the clearance and for SAIDI/SAIFI reliability reporting.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; GE PowerOn ADMS; NERC FAC-001

description: Reference to the outage event during which this safety clearance was issued. Links the clearance to the associated unplanned interruption or planned maintenance outage driving the switching and restoration work.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS OMS Incident; NERC FAC-001

description: Reference to the distribution feeder or circuit segment on which the safety clearance applies. Enables feeder-level aggregation of active clearances for dispatcher situational awareness and restoration sequencing.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; NERC FAC-001

description: Foreign key linking to grid.grid_switching_order. Business justification: Safety clearances are issued for grid switching orders to protect field crews. Linking enables safety compliance tracking, OSHA documentation, and lockout/tagout procedure enforcement.

Reference to the control room dispatcher or system operator who formally issued this safety clearance. The issuing authority is accountable for verifying equipment de-energization and isolation before granting clearance. Satisfies PARTY_REFERENCE category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269(d); NERC FAC-001; NERC CIP-006

description: Reference to the primary electrical equipment asset (transformer, circuit breaker, switch, line segment, cable, bus section) covered by this safety clearance. Sourced from the asset registry in Ventyx Asset Suite or Esri ArcGIS Utility Network.
reference: Ventyx Asset Suite; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; NERC FAC-001

description: Reference to the dispatcher or supervisor who authorized the release of this safety clearance after confirming all crew members are clear of the work zone and equipment is ready for re-energization. May differ from the original issuing dispatcher.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269(d); NERC FAC-001; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Reference to the maintenance or restoration work order in the asset management system (Ventyx Asset Suite / SAP S/4HANA PM) that this safety clearance supports. Enables traceability between safety clearances and planned work activities.
reference: Ventyx Asset Suite Work Management; SAP S/4HANA Plant Maintenance; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269

business_glossary_term: Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS) Switching Reference
description: Reference identifier from the GE PowerOn Advanced Distribution Management System (ADMS) linking this safety clearance to the associated switching sequence or network model state. Enables traceability to the ADMS network topology at the time of clearance issuance.

Free-text description of the reason this safety clearance was cancelled before use or suspended mid-work. Populated only when clearance_status is 'cancelled' or 'suspended'. Required for safety audit trail and incident investigation.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; NERC FAC-001; SOX Section 404

description: Externally-known, human-readable alphanumeric identifier for the safety clearance, as assigned by the OMS or switching management system (e.g., GE PowerOn ADMS). Used by dispatchers, field crews, and control room operators to reference the clearance in verbal and written communications. Satisfies BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS; NERC FAC-001; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269

description: Business purpose for which the safety clearance was issued. Outage Restoration: unplanned outage repair. Planned Maintenance: scheduled preventive or corrective maintenance. Emergency Repair: urgent unplanned repair outside normal outage workflow. Inspection: equipment inspection requiring de-energization. Construction: new construction or capital project work. Storm Response: clearance issued during declared storm event.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; NERC FAC-001; Ventyx Asset Suite

description: Current lifecycle state of the safety clearance. Requested: clearance has been requested but not yet issued. Issued: clearance has been formally issued to the holding crew member. Active: crew is actively working under the clearance. Suspended: clearance temporarily suspended (e.g., weather hold). Released: clearance has been formally released and equipment may be re-energized. Cancelled: clearance voided before use. Expired: clearance lapsed without formal release. Satisfies LIFECYCLE_STATUS category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: requested|issued|active|suspended|released|cancelled|expired — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; NERC FAC-001

description: FK to outage.switching_order.switching_order_id — Safety clearances are issued in context of switching orders to protect crews. Must link for safety compliance and clearance release workflow.

Classification of the safety clearance instrument issued to protect field crew. Hold Tag: prevents re-energization while crew is on equipment. Clearance Tag: formal authorization to work on de-energized equipment. Ground Placement: physical grounding of conductors for crew protection. Danger Tag: prohibits operation of tagged device. Caution Tag: advisory restriction. Equipment Tag: equipment-specific isolation marker. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hold_tag|clearance_tag|ground_placement|danger_tag|caution_tag|equipment_tag — promote to reference product]
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269(d); IEEE Std 1584; NERC FAC-001

description: Date and time when this safety clearance record was first created in the OMS or switching management system. Satisfies RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX Section 404; NERC CIP-007; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Number of field crew members working under this safety clearance. Used for crew accountability tracking and to ensure all crew members are clear of the work zone before the clearance is released and equipment is re-energized.

Classification of the field crew holding this safety clearance. Line Crew: distribution line workers. Substation Crew: substation maintenance technicians. Transmission Crew: high-voltage transmission workers. Contractor Crew: third-party contracted crew. Mutual Aid Crew: crew deployed under a mutual aid agreement from another utility.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; NERC FAC-001; NERC MOU mutual aid

description: Number of customers de-energized as a result of the switching and isolation actions associated with this safety clearance. Used for SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability index calculation and customer notification prioritization.
reference: IEEE Std 1366; PUC Reliability Reporting; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Human-readable description of the electrical equipment covered by this safety clearance, including equipment name, type, and location identifier as recorded in the OMS or GIS. Supplements the equipment_id for dispatcher and crew reference.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; NERC FAC-001

description: Indicates whether physical protective grounds have been applied to the de-energized conductors or equipment covered by this clearance. True = grounds applied; False = no grounds applied. Grounding is mandatory for certain voltage levels and work types per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269(n); IEEE Std 1584; NERC FAC-001

description: Textual description of the specific locations where protective grounds have been applied (e.g., 'North side of pole 47A, phase A-B-C'). Required when grounds_applied is True. Used for crew safety verification and clearance release sequencing.

Free-text field capturing specific hazard conditions, safety warnings, or special precautions associated with this clearance (e.g., proximity to energized conductors, confined space entry, asbestos presence, wildlife hazards). Communicated to field crew at time of clearance issuance.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 (Confined Space); NERC FAC-001

description: Textual description of the electrical isolation boundary for this safety clearance, identifying all open points, switches, and disconnects that define the de-energized zone. Critical for crew safety verification and dispatcher situational awareness.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269(d); NERC FAC-001; IEEE Std 1584

description: Date and time when the safety clearance was formally issued to the holding crew member by the issuing dispatcher. This is the principal real-world business event time for the clearance lifecycle. Satisfies BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category for TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; NERC FAC-001; GE PowerOn ADMS

description: Indicates whether any customers dependent on life support equipment (medical baseline, life support registry) are within the de-energized zone covered by this safety clearance. True = life support customers affected. Triggers priority restoration and mandatory customer notification per PUC rules.
reference: State PUC Life Support Rules; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; Oracle CC&B CIS

description: Reference number for the associated Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedure document or energy control program record, as required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 for control of hazardous energy. Links the safety clearance to the formal LOTO documentation package.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; NERC FAC-001

description: Indicates whether the switching and clearance activity associated with this safety clearance is subject to NERC reliability standard reporting requirements (e.g., FAC-001, FAC-002, or CIP-related switching). True = NERC reportable.
reference: NERC FAC-001; NERC FAC-002; NERC CIP-006; FERC Order 693

description: Description of the electrical network segment (feeder section, bus section, transmission line segment) covered by this safety clearance, including circuit identifiers and geographic boundaries. Used for dispatcher situational awareness and restoration sequencing.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; NERC FAC-001

description: Native clearance or safety tag identifier as recorded in the source Outage Management System (GE PowerOn ADMS). Used for cross-system traceability between the lakehouse silver layer record and the operational OMS source record.

Indicates whether all applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269 electrical safety requirements have been verified and documented prior to issuing this clearance, including minimum approach distances, PPE requirements, and lockout/tagout procedures. True = OSHA compliance verified.

Indicates whether this safety clearance was issued in support of a planned (scheduled) outage rather than an unplanned interruption. True = planned outage; False = unplanned/emergency outage. Used for SAIDI/SAIFI planned vs. unplanned reliability index segregation.
reference: IEEE Std 1366; PUC Reliability Reporting; NERC FAC-001

description: Priority classification for this safety clearance, reflecting the urgency of the associated restoration or maintenance work. Critical: life safety or critical infrastructure. High: large customer impact or time-sensitive restoration. Normal: standard planned or unplanned work. Low: minor maintenance with minimal customer impact.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS; NERC FAC-001; PUC Service Reliability Standards

description: Free-text field for regulatory compliance notes associated with this safety clearance, including NERC FAC, OSHA, or PUC-specific documentation requirements, special reporting obligations, or compliance exceptions noted at time of issuance.
reference: NERC FAC-001; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; State PUC Reporting Requirements; FERC

description: Date and time when the safety clearance was formally released by the holding crew member and acknowledged by the issuing dispatcher, signaling that the equipment may be re-energized. Null if the clearance has not yet been released. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

description: Maximum power export limit in kilowatts (kW) allowed by the interconnection agreement. May be less than nameplate capacity due to grid constraints, NEM program rules, or hosting capacity limitations. Null if no export limit applies.

Name of the third-party or internal system providing generation forecasts for this DER. Used for solar and wind resources requiring day-ahead and real-time production forecasting. Null for non-variable resources.

Code identifying the utility or state incentive program under which the DER was installed. Examples include solar rebate programs, storage incentives, or federal Investment Tax Credit (ITC) tracking. Null if no incentive was claimed.
reference: State and Federal Renewable Energy Incentive Programs

description: Total installed cost of the DER in US dollars including equipment, labor, permitting, and interconnection fees. Business-confidential. Used for incentive program cost-effectiveness analysis and LCOE calculations.

Unique identifier for the executed interconnection agreement governing the DERs connection to the utility grid. References the legal contract specifying technical requirements, liability, and operational protocols.
Date of the most recent utility or third-party inspection of the DER installation. Used for compliance verification, safety audit tracking, and periodic re-certification requirements.
reference: OSHA and State Electrical Inspection Requirements

description: Timestamp when this DER registry record was most recently updated. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and audit trail purposes.
reference: SOX Internal Controls - Audit Trail Requirements

description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the DER installation in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, solar irradiance modeling, weather correlation, and grid topology analysis.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the DER installation in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, solar irradiance modeling, weather correlation, and grid topology analysis.

Utility meter identifier associated with the DER interconnection point. References the revenue meter or production meter used for NEM credit calculation, billing, and generation tracking. May reference a dedicated production meter or the premise service meter.

Maximum rated power output or storage capacity of the DER in kilowatts (kW). For generation resources, this is the AC output rating. For battery storage, this is the maximum discharge rate. Critical for grid planning, interconnection studies, and program eligibility determination.

Indicates whether the DER is eligible for Net Energy Metering (NEM) programs. True if the resource meets size, technology, and jurisdictional requirements for NEM credit generation. False if ineligible or enrolled in alternative compensation mechanisms.
Scheduled date for the next required inspection or compliance verification. Null if no periodic inspection is required. Used for proactive maintenance scheduling and regulatory compliance tracking.

Free-text field for additional comments, special conditions, or operational notes related to the DER registration. May include interconnection study findings, operational restrictions, or program-specific requirements.

Current operational state of the DER. Commissioned indicates the resource has completed interconnection and is authorized to operate. Operational indicates active generation or storage capability. Offline indicates temporary non-operation due to maintenance or technical issues. Decommissioned indicates permanent removal from service. Suspended indicates administrative hold. Testing indicates pre-commissioning validation phase.
Legal name of the entity that owns the DER asset. May be a residential customer, commercial entity, or third-party developer. Business-confidential for competitive and privacy reasons.

Legal ownership model of the DER. Customer-owned indicates the premise owner owns the asset. Third-party-owned indicates a solar lease, PPA, or other third-party financing arrangement. Utility-owned indicates utility-scale BTM assets. Community-shared indicates community solar or shared renewable programs.

Unique identifier for the physical point where the DER connects to the utility distribution system. References the specific transformer, service panel, or substation bus where interconnection occurs. Critical for grid modeling, outage management, and voltage regulation analysis.
reference: IEEE 1547 - Point of Common Coupling Requirements

description: Indicates whether the DER is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs). True if the resource is a qualifying renewable technology under state RPS rules. False if ineligible due to technology type, vintage, or jurisdictional requirements.

Date when the DER was first registered in the utility DER registry. Represents the initial record creation date, which may precede commissioning. Used for audit trail and registration workflow tracking.

RPS tier classification for the DER under state renewable portfolio standards. Tiers typically differentiate by technology type, vintage, or geographic location. Examples include Tier 1 (new renewables), Tier 2 (existing renewables), Solar Carve-Out, or Distributed Generation tier. Null if not RPS-eligible.
Utility service territory or operating company jurisdiction where the DER is located. Used for regulatory reporting, RPS compliance tracking, and jurisdictional analysis.

Indicates whether the DER is equipped with IEEE 1547-2018 compliant smart inverter functionality. True if the inverter supports advanced grid support functions including volt-VAR, frequency-watt, and dynamic reactive power control. False for legacy inverters without advanced functions.

Total energy storage capacity in kilowatt-hours (kWh) for battery storage and other energy storage systems. Null for non-storage DER types. Used for Virtual Power Plant (VPP) aggregation and demand response program sizing.
reference: FERC Order 841 - Electric Storage Participation in Markets

description: Detailed technology classification including manufacturer model, inverter type, panel efficiency class, or battery chemistry. Provides granular technical categorization beyond the primary DER type.
reference: IEC 61850 - Communication Networks and Systems for Power Utility Automation

Calculated score (0-100) indicating how well the crew's certifications and equipment match the DER technology requirements. Solar PV crews score higher for solar sites, storage-certified crews for battery systems. Used for optimal crew assignment.
Date when the crew most recently completed service at this DER site. Used to calculate next service due date and track service history. Identified in detection data.

Classification of the service activity performed. Preventive maintenance includes scheduled inspections and routine servicing. Corrective maintenance addresses identified issues. Emergency repair for unplanned outages. Storm restoration for weather-related damage. Identified in detection data.
Planned date for the next service visit by this crew to this DER site. Used for maintenance schedule optimization and crew dispatch planning. Identified in detection data.
Total cost for this service assignment including labor, equipment, materials, and travel. Used for DER maintenance cost tracking and budget management.
Actual or estimated duration in hours for the service activity. Used for crew utilization tracking and labor cost allocation.
Planned interval in days between service visits for this DER-crew pairing. Used for preventive maintenance scheduling optimization. Identified in detection data.
Current status of the service assignment. Tracks lifecycle from scheduling through completion.

Anniversary date when cumulative NEM credits are reconciled. Any remaining credit balance may be paid out, rolled over, or forfeited based on program rules.
Total energy storage capacity of paired battery system in kilowatt-hours. Null if no battery is installed. Used for SGIP (Self-Generation Incentive Program) eligibility and VPP dispatch.
End date of the current NEM billing period. Marks the cutoff for credit calculation and ledger posting.

Type of distributed energy resource installed behind the customer meter. Identifies the generation technology for capacity planning and forecasting.
reference: DERMS (Distributed Energy Resource Management System) Standard

description: Timestamp when the NEM account record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

Running total of NEM credits available to offset future charges. Accumulates across billing periods until the annual true-up date.
Date the customer was officially enrolled in the NEM program and began receiving export credits. Marks the start of the NEM billing cycle.
Dollar value of NEM credits earned during the billing period, calculated as net_export_kwh multiplied by export_rate_per_kwh. Posted to the cumulative credit balance.
Maximum instantaneous power export allowed to the grid in kilowatts. May be lower than installed capacity due to interconnection constraints or grid hosting capacity limits.
Compensation rate in dollars per kWh for energy exported to the grid. Rate varies by NEM program type and may differ from retail rate. Used to calculate export credit value.
Total energy consumed by the customer from the grid during the billing period, measured in kilowatt-hours. Does not net out BTM generation.
Total energy generated by the BTM system during the billing period, measured in kilowatt-hours. Includes both self-consumed and exported energy.
Date the BTM generation system was physically installed and commissioned. Used for warranty tracking and depreciation calculations.
Nameplate capacity of the BTM generation system in kilowatts. Used for interconnection limits, export calculations, and grid impact analysis.
reference: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation) Standard

description: Name of the contractor or company that installed the BTM generation system. Used for quality assurance and warranty claims.
State-issued contractor license number for the installer. Verifies that installation was performed by a certified professional.
Unique application number assigned during the DER interconnection approval process. Tracks the regulatory approval for BTM generation interconnection to the utility grid.
Name of the company that manufactured the inverter. Used for equipment certification verification and technical support.
Model number of the inverter installed. Used to verify compliance with interconnection standards and grid support functions.
Manufacturer serial number of the primary inverter converting DC generation to AC for grid export. Used for equipment tracking, warranty claims, and performance monitoring.
Date of the most recent utility or third-party inspection of the BTM system. Used to verify ongoing compliance with safety and interconnection standards.
reference: OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration) Standard

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the NEM account record. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.
User ID or system identifier of the person or process that last modified the record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

Specific NEM tariff program under which the customer is enrolled. Determines export credit rates, true-up rules, and credit expiration policies. NEM 1.0 offers full retail rate credits; NEM 2.0 includes non-bypassable charges; NEM 3.0/NEM-A uses export compensation rates below retail.
Net energy exported to the grid during the billing period after self-consumption. Positive value indicates surplus generation sent to the grid. Basis for export credit calculation.
Net energy imported from the grid during the billing period after accounting for BTM generation. Positive value indicates net consumption from the grid.
Scheduled date for the next required inspection of the BTM system. Used for compliance tracking and maintenance planning.
Free-text field for operational notes, special conditions, or exceptions related to the NEM account. Used by customer service and billing operations.
Date the utility granted permission for the BTM system to operate and export to the grid. Marks the official start of interconnection and may differ from enrollment date.
Current lifecycle status of the NEM account. Active accounts receive export credits; suspended accounts are temporarily paused; terminated accounts are closed.
Indicates whether generation from this NEM account is eligible for REC issuance. True if the system meets RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) eligibility criteria.
Date the NEM account was closed or terminated. Null for active accounts. Marks the end of credit accrual and triggers final true-up processing.
Reason code for NEM account termination. Used for program analytics and customer retention analysis.
Dollar amount of credit adjustment applied during the annual true-up reconciliation. May represent payout, rollover, or forfeiture of remaining credits based on program rules.
Indicates whether this NEM account is enrolled in a VPP aggregation program for demand response or grid services. True if the customer has opted into VPP dispatch.
reference: DERMS (Distributed Energy Resource Management System) Standard

Daily time-of-day (HH:MM format) when the VPP becomes eligible for dispatch. Supports time-of-use constraints and operational availability windows.

Classification of the VPP aggregation strategy: demand response (load reduction), storage dispatch (battery discharge/charge), solar curtailment (PV output reduction), wind curtailment, load shifting, or mixed DER (combination of multiple resource types).
Rolling average performance score (0-100 scale) across all dispatch events, calculated as the ratio of actual delivered capacity to requested capacity. Used for aggregator performance evaluation.
Methodology used to establish the counterfactual baseline for measuring VPP dispatch performance: customer baseline load (CBL), day-ahead forecast, historical average, or control group comparison.

description: Monthly capacity payment rate in dollars per MW for maintaining the VPP in a dispatchable state, independent of actual dispatch events.

Maximum acceptable communication latency in milliseconds between the DERMS platform and participating DER assets for dispatch signal transmission and acknowledgment. Critical for fast-response ancillary services.
Date on which the VPP configuration received compliance certification from the applicable ISO/RTO or Public Utility Commission (PUC) for market participation.
Expiration or termination date of the VPP aggregation contract or program enrollment period. Null for open-ended contracts.
Effective start date of the VPP aggregation contract or program enrollment period.
Timestamp when this VPP configuration record was first created in the system.

Method by which dispatch commands are issued to the VPP: automated (DERMS-driven without human intervention), manual (operator-initiated), semi-automated (operator approval required), or api_driven (external system integration).
ISO/RTO pricing zone, load zone, or distribution service territory in which the VPP operates. Used for locational marginal pricing (LMP) and congestion management.
Financial incentive rate in dollars per MWh paid to the VPP for successful dispatch performance and energy delivery.

business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Market ID
description: Unique market participant identifier assigned by the ISO/RTO for this VPP in wholesale energy, capacity, or ancillary services markets.
