description: Registration status of the VPP with the applicable ISO or RTO for wholesale market participation: registered (approved and active), pending (application submitted), not registered (no application), expired (registration lapsed), or rejected (application denied).
Timestamp of the most recent dispatch event issued to this VPP. Used for operational monitoring and performance tracking.
Maximum duration in minutes that a single dispatch event can be sustained before requiring a rest period or recharge cycle (relevant for battery storage VPPs).
Minimum duration in minutes that a dispatch event must be sustained once activated. Ensures operational stability and prevents rapid cycling of DER assets.
Minimum percentage of requested dispatch capacity that must be delivered for the event to qualify for settlement payment. Typical values range from 70% to 90%.
Timestamp when this VPP configuration record was last modified or updated.
Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or configuration comments related to this VPP aggregation.
Number of individual DER assets (solar arrays, battery storage units, demand response participants, etc.) currently enrolled and participating in this VPP aggregation.
Financial penalty rate in dollars per MWh applied when the VPP fails to meet minimum performance thresholds during a dispatch event.
Time interval in minutes over which VPP dispatch performance is measured and aggregated for settlement purposes (e.g., 5-minute, 15-minute, or hourly intervals).
Rate at which the VPP can increase or decrease its aggregated output in megawatts per minute. Critical for frequency regulation and ramping services.
Name of the state or federal regulatory program under which the VPP operates (e.g., California DRAM, NYISO DER Participation Model, PJM DER Aggregation).
Frequency in seconds at which telemetry data is transmitted from participating DERs to the DERMS platform during active dispatch events.
Indicates whether real-time telemetry data (voltage, frequency, power output) from participating DERs is transmitted to the ISO/RTO or utility control center during dispatch events.
Total nameplate capacity in megawatts (MW) of all Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) aggregated within this VPP portfolio. Represents the maximum dispatchable capacity under ideal conditions.
Cumulative count of all dispatch events issued to this VPP since configuration inception. Used for performance analytics and settlement auditing.
Nominal voltage class in kilovolts (kV) of the distribution system at which the VPP DERs are interconnected (e.g., 12.47 kV, 34.5 kV).
Unique business identifier or registration code for the VPP used in ISO/RTO market systems and DERMS platforms.
Business name or designation of the Virtual Power Plant aggregation portfolio.

Current operational lifecycle status of the VPP configuration: active (operational and dispatchable), inactive (configured but not operational), suspended (temporarily disabled), pending approval (awaiting ISO/RTO or regulatory approval), decommissioned (retired), or testing (pilot phase).

Indicates whether this PPA contract contributes to the utility's Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance obligations (True) or not (False).

Dollar amount of credit support (letter of credit, cash collateral, parent guarantee) required from or provided to this vendor for their role in this specific PPA contract. Counterparties typically provide credit support to the utility; transmission providers may require credit support from the utility. Amount is specific to this PPA contract and vendor role combination.

Description of credit support mechanisms required from the counterparty, such as letters of credit, parent guarantees, or performance bonds, to mitigate counterparty credit risk. [Moved from ppa_contract: Credit support requirements vary by vendor and role within a PPA. The counterparty provides credit support to the utility, but the utility may need to provide credit support to the transmission provider. The amount and form of credit support is vendor-role-specific, not a single contract-level attribute. Should be modeled as credit_support_amount in the association.]

Date when this vendor ceased performing their role in this PPA contract. NULL if vendor is currently active in this role. Populated when vendors are replaced or when the PPA terminates. Supports historical tracking of vendor role changes.

Date when this vendor began performing their role in this PPA contract. May differ from the PPA effective_start_date if vendors are added or replaced during the contract term. Supports vendor role transition tracking and historical vendor participation analysis.

Current status of this vendor's participation in their PPA contract role. Active = currently performing role, suspended = temporarily not performing (e.g., during dispute resolution), terminated = role ended, replaced = vendor was substituted by another vendor in the same role. Supports operational tracking of multi-party PPA administration.

Vendor-specific payment terms for this PPA contract role. Defines payment schedule, invoice requirements, and settlement timing specific to this vendor's role. May differ from the vendor's standard payment terms in their master record because PPA contracts often have specialized payment structures (e.g., monthly energy payments to counterparty, quarterly REC transfer payments to administrator).

Vendor-specific performance guarantee obligations for this PPA contract role. Defines availability targets, response time requirements, service level agreements, and penalty/liquidated damages provisions specific to this vendor's role. Counterparties have energy delivery guarantees, scheduling coordinators have scheduling accuracy requirements, REC administrators have transfer timing requirements.

Frequency at which payments and obligations are settled with this specific vendor for their role in the PPA. Energy counterparties typically settle monthly, REC administrators quarterly, transmission providers monthly. This is contract-role-specific and may differ from standard vendor terms.

Detailed pricing or fee structure for this vendor's services in their PPA contract role. Scheduling coordinators charge per-MWh scheduling fees, REC administrators charge per-REC-transferred fees, transmission providers charge per-MW-month reservation fees. These are contract-specific and may differ from standard vendor pricing.

The business area classification for this revenue (e.g., generation, transmission, distribution, retail). Supports segment reporting under GAAP.
The kilowatt-hours of energy consumption for which revenue is being recognized. Sourced from meter data management system.
The organizational cost center responsible for this revenue stream. Supports internal management accounting and profitability analysis.
The date and time when this revenue recognition entry record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for record lifecycle.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this revenue recognition entry. Typically USD for US utilities.
The portion of billed revenue that has been collected but not yet earned. Represents liability for future service delivery under ASC 606.
The peak kilowatt demand for which demand charges are being recognized. Applicable to commercial and industrial rate schedules.
The general ledger account code to which this revenue recognition entry is posted in SAP S/4HANA FI. Maps to FERC account structure.
The user ID or name of the person or system process that last modified this revenue recognition entry record.
The date and time when this revenue recognition entry record was last modified. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.
The date of the meter reading that forms the basis for billed revenue in this entry. Null for unbilled accruals or non-metered charges.
Free-text notes providing additional context for this revenue recognition entry, including explanations for adjustments or special circumstances.
Description of the performance obligation satisfied by this revenue recognition entry under ASC 606 (e.g., electricity delivery, capacity reservation).
The date this revenue recognition entry was posted to the general ledger in SAP S/4HANA FI. May differ from recognition_date due to period-end adjustments.
The profit center to which this revenue is allocated for segment reporting and profitability analysis.
The specific date on which revenue was recognized in the general ledger. Represents the business event timestamp for this revenue recognition transaction.
The accounting method used to recognize this revenue under ASC 606. Indicates whether revenue is recognized at a point in time or over time.
The total revenue amount recognized in this accounting period for this service agreement and revenue category. Represents earned revenue under ASC 606.
The regulatory accounting code as defined by FERC or state PUC for revenue classification and reporting. Supports regulatory financial statements.
Classification of the revenue type being recognized. Distinguishes between energy consumption charges, demand charges, fixed customer charges, regulatory riders, and ancillary services.
Customer class for which revenue is being recognized. Aligns with rate class segmentation and regulatory reporting requirements.
FK to billing.invoice.invoice_id — Revenue recognition entries may reference specific invoices for billed revenue. Supports GL reconciliation.
Indicates whether this revenue recognition entry is a reversal of a previous entry. True for reversals, False for original entries.
The business reason for reversing this revenue recognition entry (e.g., billing error, customer dispute, regulatory adjustment). Populated only when reversal_flag is True.
FK to billing.service_agreement.service_agreement_id — Revenue recognition entries are derived from billed/unbilled revenue for a specific service agreement and accounting period.
The regulatory rider or surcharge code applied to this revenue recognition entry (e.g., fuel adjustment clause, renewable energy surcharge).
FK to billing.service_agreement.service_agreement_id — Revenue recognition entries are derived from billed/unbilled revenue for a specific service agreement. Required for ASC 606 compliance.
The end date of the service period for which revenue is being recognized. Defines the end of the consumption or service delivery window.
The start date of the service period for which revenue is being recognized. Defines the beginning of the consumption or service delivery window.
The document number in the source system that originated this revenue recognition entry (e.g., SAP IS-U billing document number, FI document number).
The operational system from which this revenue recognition entry was sourced (SAP IS-U FICA, Oracle CC&B, SAP S/4HANA FI, or manual entry).
The version of the tariff rate schedule applied for this revenue recognition entry. Ensures auditability of rate changes.
The total tax amount included in recognized revenue (sales tax, utility tax, franchise fees). Excluded from net revenue for regulatory reporting.
The portion of recognized revenue that has been earned but not yet invoiced. Represents accrued revenue for consumption between last meter read and period end.
The user ID or name of the person or system process that created this revenue recognition entry record.
Unique identifier for this enrollment record. Primary key for the association.
Foreign key to the billing service agreement participating in this enrollment.

description: Foreign key linking to the renewable incentive program in which the service agreement is enrolled

business_glossary_term: Service Agreement Incentive Enrollment - Billing Service Agreement Id

External reference number from the program application or approval process for this enrollment.
Total incentive amount approved for this service agreement under this specific program in USD. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Current compliance status of this enrollment indicating whether the service agreement meets ongoing program requirements. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Timestamp when this enrollment record was created in the system.

Current lifecycle status of this enrollment indicating whether it is actively receiving incentive payments.
Date of the most recent compliance verification for this enrollment.
Scheduled date for the next incentive payment for this enrollment. Null for one-time payments already disbursed.
Type of payment schedule for this enrollment: one_time, monthly, quarterly, annual, or per_kwh_generated. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Cumulative amount paid to date for this specific enrollment in USD. Tracks actual payments made under this program-agreement combination. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Timestamp when this enrollment record was last modified.
Unique surrogate identifier for the utility customer account record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for all downstream joins across billing, metering, and demand response domains.
reference: SAP IS-U Business Partner / Account Object; Oracle CC&B Account Entity

reference: SAP IS-U Business Partner (BUT000); Oracle CC&B Person/Account Relationship

Foreign key linking to grid.control_area. Business justification: Customer accounts are assigned to control areas for energy settlement, interchange accounting, regulatory reporting, and balancing authority cost allocation. Required for billing and compliance operat

Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Utility accounts are assigned to cost centers for internal cost allocation, segment profitability analysis, and management accounting. Essential for customer segment P&L reporting and regulatory cost-

Reference to the parent account_id for consolidated billing hierarchies and corporate account structures. Null for top-level or standalone accounts. Enables traversal of multi-level corporate hierarchies for enterprise billing and reporting.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Account Hierarchy; Oracle CC&B Account Hierarchy; FERC Form 1

description: Reference to the primary service premise (physical location) associated with this account. A premise represents the physical address where electricity is delivered. Accounts may span multiple premises in consolidated billing scenarios.
reference: SAP IS-U Premise (EANL); Oracle CC&B Premise; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network Service Location

business_glossary_term: Primary Service Asset Registry Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_registry. Business justification: Accounts track primary service delivery asset (transformer, service vault) for billing context, capacity planning, and outage impact analysis. Critical for customer-asset operational linkage in utilit

Grouping classification that determines billing consolidation and hierarchy rules. Consolidated billing groups multiple premises under one bill; corporate parent denotes the apex of a corporate hierarchy; municipal aggregation and Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) denote aggregated load programs; franchise denotes accounts under a specific franchise territory agreement.
reference: SAP IS-U Account Group (VKONT-VKGRP); Oracle CC&B Account Management Group; FERC OATT; State PUC Tariff

description: Externally-known utility account number as assigned by the Customer Information System (CIS). This is the number printed on customer bills and used in all customer-facing communications. Sourced from SAP IS-U FKKVK or Oracle CC&B ACCOUNT table.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Account (FKKVK); Oracle CC&B Account; NAESB WEQ-001

description: Current lifecycle state of the utility account. Governs service eligibility, billing generation, and collections processing. Transitions include: pending_activation (new account awaiting energization), active (energized and billed), suspended (temporarily halted per tariff or non-payment), disconnected (service terminated), written_off (uncollectable balance), reactivated (restored after disconnection).
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Account Status (VKONT-VKOSTATUS); Oracle CC&B Account Status; PUC Service Disconnection Rules

description: Classification of the utility account by customer segment. Drives rate eligibility, billing rules, and regulatory reporting. Residential covers single-family and multi-family dwellings; commercial covers businesses; industrial covers large-load manufacturing and processing facilities. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: residential|commercial|industrial|municipal|agricultural|street_lighting|transportation|government — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP IS-U Account Determination (VKTYP); Oracle CC&B Account Type; FERC Form 1 Customer Classification; EIA-861

description: Date and time when the account was first activated and service was energized. Represents the precise business event time of account creation and service commencement. Used for SLA tracking of new service connections.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Account Creation; Oracle CC&B Account Activation; State PUC New Connect SLA

description: Indicates whether this account has an Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meter installed, enabling automated interval reads, remote connect/disconnect, and real-time usage data. Drives eligibility for TOU rates, demand response programs, and enhanced billing analytics.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM; SAP IS-U Device Management; FERC Order 888; State PUC AMI Deployment Plans; IEEE C12.19

description: Indicates whether this account is enrolled in automatic payment (AutoPay), where the bill amount is automatically debited from the customer's bank account or charged to a payment card on the due date. Reduces collections risk and improves cash flow.
reference: SAP IS-U FI-CA Payment Method; Oracle CC&B Auto Pay; NAESB WEQ; PCI DSS

description: Code identifying the billing cycle (meter reading and bill generation schedule) assigned to this account. Determines the monthly read date and bill due date. Managed in SAP IS-U Billing Order or Oracle CC&B Bill Cycle. Examples: BC01 (1st of month), BC15 (15th of month).
reference: SAP IS-U Billing Order (ABRSPERR); Oracle CC&B Bill Cycle; State PUC Billing Rules

description: Indicates whether this account has Behind-the-Meter (BTM) generation or storage assets installed at the premise. BTM assets include solar PV, battery storage, and combined heat and power (CHP) systems that are not directly visible to the grid operator. Drives load disaggregation and DER management workflows.
reference: FERC Order 2222; State PUC DER Rules; DERMS Integration; IEEE 1547

description: Indicates whether this account is enrolled in a budget billing (levelized payment plan) program, where monthly bills are averaged over a 12-month period to smooth seasonal fluctuations. Affects bill calculation and settlement processes in SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B.
reference: SAP IS-U Budget Billing (ABSCHLAG); Oracle CC&B Budget Billing; State PUC Tariff

description: The native primary key or account identifier as stored in the source CIS (SAP IS-U contract account number VKONT, or Oracle CC&B account ID). Enables traceability back to the operational system of record for reconciliation, audit, and issue resolution.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Account (VKONT); Oracle CC&B Account ID; SOX Data Lineage; Enterprise MDM Policy

description: Identifies the operational Customer Information System (CIS) from which this account record originates. Critical for data lineage, deduplication, and cross-system reconciliation in multi-CIS utility environments. Values: SAP_IS_U (SAP Industry Solution for Utilities), ORACLE_CCB (Oracle Customer Care and Billing), LEGACY_CIS (decommissioned legacy system).
reference: SAP IS-U; Oracle CC&B; Enterprise Data Governance Policy; SOX Data Lineage

description: Date on which the service agreement or contract associated with this account is scheduled to expire or terminate. Null for open-ended tariff service. For fixed-term commercial or industrial contracts and PPAs, this date triggers renewal or renegotiation workflows.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract (VERTRAG); Oracle CC&B Service Agreement; FERC PPA; State PUC Tariff

description: Date on which the service agreement or contract associated with this account became effective. For residential accounts this typically aligns with move_in_date; for commercial and industrial accounts this may reflect a separately negotiated contract effective date, Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), or special contract term.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract (VERTRAG); Oracle CC&B Service Agreement; FERC PPA; State PUC Tariff

description: Timestamp when this account record was first created in the source CIS system. Represents the audit creation time for data lineage and SOX compliance. Distinct from activation_timestamp which represents the business event of service energization.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Account Creation Timestamp; Oracle CC&B Account Created Date; SOX Internal Controls; GDPR Article 30

description: Credit risk classification assigned to the account based on payment history, credit bureau data, and internal scoring. Governs deposit requirements, payment plan eligibility, and collections treatment. Managed within SAP IS-U FICA or Oracle CC&B Collections module.
reference: SAP IS-U FI-CA Credit Management (FKKCR); Oracle CC&B Credit Review; State PUC Credit and Deposit Rules; SOX Internal Controls

description: Dollar amount of security deposit held by the utility for this account, as required by credit class or PUC tariff rules. Refundable upon account closure in good standing. Tracked in SAP IS-U FI-CA or Oracle CC&B.
reference: SAP IS-U FI-CA Security Deposit (FKKDEP); Oracle CC&B Deposit; State PUC Deposit Rules; SOX

business_glossary_term: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Rate Enrollment Flag
description: Indicates whether this account is enrolled in a special Electric Vehicle (EV) charging rate or managed charging program. Drives eligibility for off-peak EV charging incentives and supports grid load forecasting for EV adoption planning.
reference: State PUC EV Tariff; FERC Order 2222; DOE EV Infrastructure Programs; IEEE 2030.5

description: Date of the most recent bill generated for this account. Used to identify unbilled accounts, support billing cycle management, and calculate days since last bill for collections and customer service workflows.
reference: SAP IS-U Billing Document (ERDK); Oracle CC&B Bill; State PUC Billing Rules

description: Date of the most recent payment posted to this account. Used in collections scoring, credit class review, and customer service inquiries. Sourced from SAP IS-U FI-CA payment history or Oracle CC&B payment records.
reference: SAP IS-U FI-CA Payment (DFKKZP); Oracle CC&B Payment; State PUC Collections Rules

description: Timestamp of the most recent change to account_status. Enables tracking of the current status duration and supports collections and reconnection SLA monitoring. Complements the account status history table for current-state queries.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Account Status History; Oracle CC&B Account Status History; State PUC Disconnection/Reconnection Rules

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this account record in the source CIS or Silver Layer. Supports incremental data loading, change data capture (CDC), and audit trail requirements for SOX and regulatory compliance.
reference: SAP IS-U Change Document; Oracle CC&B Audit Log; SOX Internal Controls; GDPR Article 30

description: Indicates whether a customer at this account relies on electrically-powered life support equipment (e.g., home dialysis, ventilator, oxygen concentrator). Triggers mandatory advance disconnection notice requirements and priority restoration during outages per PUC regulations.
reference: State PUC Life Support Rules; NERC EOP-011; State Emergency Management Regulations

description: Date on which the customer initiated service at the associated premise, triggering account activation and the start of billing. Corresponds to the service start date in CIS. Critical for proration of first bill and regulatory reporting of new connects.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In (EINZUG); Oracle CC&B Start Service; State PUC Service Rules

description: Date on which the customer terminated service at the associated premise, triggering final bill generation and account closure. Null for currently active accounts. Corresponds to the service end date in CIS.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-Out (AUSZUG); Oracle CC&B Stop Service; State PUC Service Rules

description: Current outstanding balance on the account as of the last billing or payment posting. Represents the net amount owed by the customer (positive) or credit due to the customer (negative). Sourced from SAP IS-U FI-CA or Oracle CC&B AR sub-ledger. Used for collections prioritization and credit risk management.
reference: SAP IS-U FI-CA (DFKKOP); Oracle CC&B Financial Transaction; SOX AR Controls; State PUC Collections Rules

description: Indicates whether this account is enrolled in paperless (electronic) billing, receiving bills via email or online portal rather than postal mail. Supports sustainability reporting and customer engagement analytics.
reference: Oracle CC&B Bill Delivery; SAP IS-U Bill Print Suppression; State PUC E-Bill Rules

description: Customer's preferred channel for receiving utility communications including bills, outage notifications, and program offers. Drives multi-channel engagement routing in CRM and outage notification systems (OMS). Aligns with customer consent preferences.
reference: Oracle CC&B Contact Preference; SAP CRM Interaction Channel; TCPA; GDPR Article 7

description: ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) representing the customer's preferred language for all communications. Drives bill language selection, IVR routing, and outage notification language. Examples: en, es, zh-TW, vi, ko.
reference: ISO 639-1; ISO 3166-1; State PUC Language Access Rules; Title VI Civil Rights Act

description: The tariff rate schedule or rate class assigned to this account, determining how energy consumption is priced. Examples include residential flat rate, Time-of-Use (TOU), Critical Peak Pricing (CPP), industrial demand rate, and agricultural pumping rate. Drives bill calculation in SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: residential_flat|tou_residential|tou_commercial|cpp|industrial_demand|agricultural|street_lighting|ev_charging — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP IS-U Rate Type (TARIFTYP); Oracle CC&B Rate Schedule; State PUC Tariff; FERC Rate Filing

description: Two-letter US state code (ISO 3166-2 subdivision) identifying the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) with regulatory authority over this account. Determines applicable tariff, consumer protection rules, and reporting obligations. Critical for multi-state utility operations.
reference: ISO 3166-2; State PUC Jurisdiction; FERC; NERC

description: Code identifying the voluntary renewable energy plan or green tariff program in which this account is enrolled. Examples include 100% renewable, green power option, or Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) purchase programs. Supports Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|green_100pct|green_50pct|rec_purchase|community_solar|wind_option — promote to reference product]
reference: State PUC RPS Rules; EPA Green Power Partnership; REC (Renewable Energy Certificate) Standards; NERC

description: Code identifying the regulated service territory within which this account receives electric service. Determines applicable tariff schedules, regulatory jurisdiction, and franchise area. Aligns with PUC-approved service territory boundaries.
reference: SAP IS-U Division (SPARTE); Oracle CC&B Service Territory; State PUC Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN); FERC

description: Reason code explaining the most recent account status transition. Examples include non_payment, customer_request, move_out, returned_check, medical_baseline, regulatory_order. Supports collections analytics and regulatory compliance reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: non_payment|customer_request|move_out|returned_check|medical_baseline|regulatory_order|fraud|deceased — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP IS-U Disconnection Reason (ABGRU); Oracle CC&B Stop Reason; State PUC Disconnection Rules; NERC CIP

description: Indicates whether this account is enrolled on a Time-of-Use (TOU) rate schedule, where energy prices vary by time of day and season to reflect grid conditions. Requires AMI metering. Supports demand flexibility analytics and rate design evaluation.
reference: State PUC TOU Tariff; SAP IS-U Rate Type; Oracle CC&B Rate Schedule; FERC Order 2222

description: Unique identifier for the account-premise relationship record. Primary key for the account_premise_link entity.
Reference to the service premise associated with this account. Links to the premise entity representing the physical service location.
reference: SAP IS-U Installation, Oracle CC&B Service Point

description: Reference to the formal service agreement governing this account-premise relationship. Links to the contract or service agreement entity.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Account, Oracle CC&B Service Agreement

description: Reference to the forwarding address for final bill delivery and correspondence after account-premise relationship termination. Used in move-out processing.
Reference to the customer account associated with this premise. Links to the account entity in the Customer Information System (CIS).
reference: SAP IS-U Business Partner, Oracle CC&B Account

description: Reference to the service order that initiated this account-premise relationship. Links to the move-in or service connection order.
reference: SAP IS-U Service Order, Oracle CC&B Field Activity

description: Reference to the tenant account when this link represents a landlord-of-record relationship. Used to track tenant accounts associated with a landlord premise. Null for non-landlord relationships.
FK to customer.premise.premise_id — The association entity must reference the premise it links. account_premise_link.premise_id → premise.premise_id.

Indicates whether this account has billing responsibility for the premise. In master-metered or landlord scenarios, multiple accounts may be linked to a premise but only one has billing responsibility.
Preferred communication channel for outage notifications and service alerts for this account-premise relationship. Used by OMS and customer engagement systems.
Security deposit amount collected for this account-premise relationship. Null if no deposit was required. Expressed in local currency.
Indicates whether a security deposit was required for this account-premise relationship based on credit classification and service territory regulations.
Indicates whether this account-premise relationship is enrolled in a Distributed Energy Resource (DER) program such as demand response, virtual power plant, or distributed generation program.
reference: FERC Order 2222, State PUC DER Programs

description: Indicates whether a final bill has been issued for this account-premise relationship upon termination. Used in move-out and service disconnection workflows.
Timestamp when this account-premise link record was first created in the Customer Information System (CIS). Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Date when the account-premise relationship was terminated. Represents move-out date or service disconnection date. Null for active relationships.
Timestamp when this account-premise link record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking in customer relationship management.
Free-text notes and comments regarding this account-premise relationship. Used by customer service representatives to document special circumstances, arrangements, or historical context.
Date when the account-premise relationship became effective. Represents move-in date or service initiation date for the account at this premise.
Current lifecycle status of the account-premise relationship. Indicates whether the link is currently in effect or has been terminated.
Reason code for termination of the account-premise relationship. Provides business context for why the link was ended. Null for active relationships.
Classification of the relationship between the account and premise. Defines the role and responsibility of the account holder at the service location.
Indicates whether this relationship involves a master-metered configuration where a single meter serves multiple tenant accounts. Common in multi-family residential and commercial properties.

Indicates whether this account-premise relationship involves a Net Energy Metering (NEM) participant with Behind the Meter (BTM) generation. Used to identify customers with distributed energy resources.
reference: FERC Net Metering Policy, State PUC NEM Tariffs

description: Indicates whether the account holder has authorized receipt of outage notifications and service alerts for this premise. Used by Outage Management System (OMS) for customer communication.
Classification of the occupancy status for this account-premise relationship. Indicates whether the account holder is an owner, tenant, or if the premise is vacant.
Numeric ranking of this account-premise link when multiple accounts are associated with a single premise. Used to determine primary contact for outage notifications and field operations.
Reference to the property management company responsible for this premise when the link type is property manager. Used in commercial and multi-family property management scenarios.
Identifier of the operational system of record that originated this account-premise link. Used for data lineage and integration troubleshooting.
Original primary key or unique identifier from the source system. Used for data reconciliation and bidirectional synchronization with operational systems.
Indicates whether vacancy billing is active for this account-premise relationship. When true, the landlord or property manager is billed for usage during tenant vacancy periods.
Unique identifier for the address record. Primary key.

FK to customer.premise.premise_id — Service addresses are associated with premises. address.premise_id → premise.premise_id (for service address type). Critical for GIS integration and field operations.

Current lifecycle status of the address: active (in use), inactive (not currently used), pending_validation (awaiting verification), retired (no longer valid), or seasonal (used only during specific periods).

Classification of address usage: service (physical service delivery location), mailing (correspondence destination), billing (invoice destination), third_party_notification (authorized third-party contact), premise (metered location), or correspondence (general communication).
reference: SAP IS-U Business Partner Address Types

description: USPS carrier route code identifying the mail delivery route for this address.
US Census Bureau block group identifier for granular demographic and socioeconomic analysis.
US Census Bureau tract identifier for demographic analysis, regulatory reporting, and low-income program eligibility (e.g., LIHEAP, energy assistance programs).
City or municipality name for the address.
Three-letter ISO country code (e.g., USA, CAN, MEX).
County or parish name for regulatory jurisdiction, tax district assignment, and Public Utility Commission (PUC) reporting.
Timestamp when this address record was first created in the system.
USPS Delivery Point Barcode (DPBC) for automated mail sorting and delivery accuracy.
Distribution system planning zone or district for load forecasting, capacity planning, and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) analysis.
Date when this address ceased to be effective. Null for currently active addresses.
Date when this address became effective and available for use in customer service agreements and billing.
Precision level of geocoding: rooftop (exact building), parcel (property boundary), street (street segment), zip_centroid (postal code center), city_centroid (city center), or unknown (not geocoded).
Geographic latitude coordinate in decimal degrees for GIS integration and outage management. Supports spatial analysis and proximity calculations.
Geographic longitude coordinate in decimal degrees for GIS integration and outage management. Supports spatial analysis and proximity calculations.
Geographic Information System (GIS) feature identifier linking this address to the utility network model in Esri ArcGIS or equivalent GIS platform.
Indicates whether this is the primary address for the associated customer or premise. True if primary, False otherwise.
Indicates whether this address is used seasonally (e.g., vacation homes, seasonal businesses). True if seasonal, False otherwise.
Timestamp when this address record was last updated or modified.
Primary street address line including street number, street name, and street type (e.g., 123 Main Street).
Secondary address line for apartment, suite, unit, building, floor, or other location identifiers.
Incorporated city, town, or municipal district name for franchise agreement tracking and local regulatory compliance.
Outage Management System (OMS) zone identifier for outage tracking, crew dispatch, and SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability metric calculation.
Postal or ZIP code for the address. Supports 5-digit, ZIP+4, and international postal code formats.
Month number (1-12) when seasonal occupancy typically ends. Null for non-seasonal addresses.
Month number (1-12) when seasonal occupancy typically begins. Null for non-seasonal addresses.
Utility service territory identifier indicating the geographic area and regulatory jurisdiction for service delivery. Used for Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) compliance.
Source system or application that created or maintains this address record (e.g., SAP IS-U, Oracle CC&B, GIS, MDM).
Unique identifier for this address in the source system of record. Used for data lineage and reconciliation.
Two-letter state or province code (e.g., CA for California, ON for Ontario).
IANA time zone identifier for the address location (e.g., America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles). Used for Time of Use (TOU) rate scheduling and Demand Response (DR) event timing.

business_glossary_term: United States Postal Service (USPS) Standardized Address
description: USPS-standardized full address string in CASS-certified format for delivery accuracy.

business_glossary_term: United States Postal Service (USPS) Validation Status
description: Status of USPS address validation: validated (confirmed by USPS), invalid (rejected by USPS), not_validated (not yet checked), corrected (USPS suggested correction applied), or ambiguous (multiple matches found).
Date when the address was last verified or validated through USPS, field inspection, or customer confirmation.

Method used to verify the address: usps_api (USPS web service), field_inspection (physical site visit), customer_confirmation (customer-provided), gis_validation (GIS system match), or third_party_service (external validation service).
Unique identifier for the contact record. Primary key.
Reference to the specific service account associated with this contact. Supports account-level contact management for multi-account customers.
Reference to the customer profile or account to which this contact belongs. Links contact to customer master entity in CIS (SAP IS-U, Oracle CC&B).

Foreign key linking to customer.address. Business justification: Contact has embedded postal address fields that should be normalized to reference the address table. The contact table has postal_address_line1, postal_address_line2, postal_city, postal_state_provinc
FK to customer.account.account_id — Some contacts are account-level (billing contact, emergency contact) rather than profile-level. Required for account-specific notification routing.
FK to customer.profile.profile_id — Contact points belong to a customer profile. contact.profile_id → profile.profile_id. Essential for multi-channel engagement.
Number of failed delivery attempts (email bounces, SMS failures, undeliverable mail) for this contact. High bounce counts trigger contact verification workflows.
Primary communication channel or medium for this contact point. Determines delivery method for notifications and alerts.
Specific role or relationship of the contact to the account holder. Defines authorization level for account actions and information access.
Current lifecycle status of the contact record. Determines whether the contact is eligible for notifications and communications.
Classification of the contact role within the customer relationship. Determines contact authority and notification eligibility.
The actual contact information value (phone number, email address, postal address, device token). Format varies by contact_channel. Classified as restricted PII.
Timestamp when this contact record was first created in the CIS system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.
Date when this contact record expires or is no longer valid for communications. Null indicates an open-ended contact.
Date when this contact record becomes active and eligible for use in communications.
Primary email address for electronic communication. Used for billing statements, outage alerts, DR (Demand Response) event notifications, and regulatory communications.
Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code indicating the customers preferred language for communications through this contact channel.
Date of the most recent failed delivery attempt for this contact channel.
Date when this contact channel was last successfully used for customer communication. Supports contact hygiene and data quality monitoring.
Timestamp when this contact record was last updated. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.
Preferred frequency for non-critical notifications through this contact channel. Critical alerts (outages, safety) are always sent in real-time.
Indicates whether the customer wants to receive billing alerts and payment reminders through this contact channel.
Indicates whether the customer wants to receive DR event dispatch notifications through this contact channel. Supports demand response program participation.
reference: CIS (Customer Information System) Business Rules, FERC Order 2222

description: Indicates whether the customer wants to receive marketing communications, promotional offers, and energy efficiency program information through this contact channel.

description: Indicates whether the customer's need was fully resolved within the IVR self-service system without requiring transfer to a live agent. True = IVR-contained; False = transferred to agent or unresolved. Key metric for IVR optimization and cost-to-serve analysis.
reference: Oracle CC&B IVR Integration; SAP IS-U CRM

description: Sequence of IVR menu selections made by the customer during the interaction (e.g., '1>3>2' representing the menu tree traversal). Used for IVR design optimization and self-service analytics.

ISO 639-1 language code for the language used during the interaction (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'zh-TW'). Supports multilingual service analytics and compliance with state language access requirements for utility customers.
reference: ISO 639-1; State PUC Language Access Requirements

description: Indicates whether this interaction involved a Net Energy Metering (NEM) inquiry, application, or billing question related to a customer's behind-the-meter (BTM) distributed energy resource (DER) such as rooftop solar. Supports NEM program analytics.
reference: FERC PURPA; State PUC NEM Tariff Rules; DOE DER Integration Standards

description: Free-text notes entered by the agent summarizing the interaction, customer concerns, actions taken, and follow-up commitments. Confidential as may contain sensitive account or personal context. Stored in Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U CRM activity log.
reference: Oracle CC&B Interaction History; SAP IS-U CRM Activity; GDPR Article 5 (data minimization)

description: The result or disposition of the interaction at its conclusion. 'follow_up_required' triggers a subsequent outbound contact. 'callback_scheduled' indicates a scheduled return call was arranged. Used for first-contact resolution (FCR) measurement.
reference: Oracle CC&B Interaction History; SAP IS-U CRM; PUC Service Quality Standards

description: Indicates whether a payment arrangement or deferred payment plan was established during this interaction. True = payment arrangement created. Supports collections analytics and FICA (Financial Customer Accounting) integration in SAP IS-U.
reference: SAP IS-U FICA; Oracle CC&B Collections Management; PUC Low-Income Customer Protection Rules

description: Externally visible alphanumeric reference number assigned to this interaction, communicated to the customer as a confirmation or tracking number (e.g., from Oracle CC&B or SAP IS-U interaction log).
reference: Oracle CC&B Interaction History; SAP IS-U CRM Activity

description: Customer sentiment assessed during or after the interaction, derived from speech analytics, text analysis, or agent classification. Supports CRM analytics, churn risk modeling, and regulatory complaint identification. 'highly_negative' may trigger proactive follow-up.
reference: Oracle CC&B CRM Analytics; SAP IS-U CRM

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this interaction record originated (e.g., SAP IS-U CRM, Oracle CC&B, Genesys telephony platform). Supports data lineage and Silver layer reconciliation.
reference: SAP IS-U CRM; Oracle CC&B; NAESB Data Exchange Standards

description: The native interaction identifier from the originating source system (e.g., Oracle CC&B interaction log ID, SAP IS-U activity number, Genesys call GUID). Enables traceability back to the system of record for audit and reconciliation.
reference: SAP IS-U CRM; Oracle CC&B Interaction History; SOX Section 404

description: Date and time when the customer interaction began (call connected, chat session opened, email received, in-person visit commenced). Principal business event timestamp per TRANSACTION_HEADER role. Stored in ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: Oracle CC&B Interaction History; NAESB Business Practice Standards

description: Granular sub-classification of the interaction within its category (e.g., 'high_bill_dispute' under billing_inquiry, 'payment_arrangement' under payment, 'tree_contact' under outage_report). Supports root-cause analytics and agent training.
reference: Oracle CC&B Interaction History; SAP IS-U CRM Activity

description: Indicates whether the customer completed a post-interaction satisfaction survey. True = survey completed. Used to calculate survey response rates and validate CSAT score population.
reference: PUC Service Quality Standards; Oracle CC&B CRM Analytics

description: Indicates whether the interaction involved a Time-of-Use (TOU) or Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate plan inquiry, enrollment, or change request. Supports rate analytics and AMI-enabled pricing program adoption tracking.
reference: State PUC Rate Tariff; Oracle CC&B Rates Management; SAP IS-U Billing

description: Number of times the interaction was transferred between agents, queues, or departments during a single session. High transfer counts indicate routing inefficiency and negatively impact customer satisfaction scores.
reference: Oracle CC&B Interaction History; SAP IS-U CRM

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this interaction record in the source system. Used for incremental data pipeline processing and audit trail compliance.
Unique identifier for the customer service agreement. Primary key for this entity.

FK to customer.account.account_id — Every service agreement is held by an account. This is a core CIS relationship — service_agreement.account_id → account.account_id. Without this, service agreements are orphaned.
Reference to the physical premise where service is delivered under this agreement.
reference: SAP IS-U Installation / Oracle CC&B Service Point

description: Interconnection agreement identifier for customers with DER (Distributed Energy Resource) such as solar, wind, or battery storage. Links to detailed interconnection application and technical specifications. Null for customers without DER.

Foreign key linking to renewable.ppa_contract. Business justification: Behind-the-meter PPA agreements are service agreements requiring direct linkage for billing integration, rate schedule coordination, and customer account management. Critical for community solar and t

FK to customer.premise.premise_id — Every service agreement delivers service at a specific premise. service_agreement.premise_id → premise.premise_id. This is the core CIS triad: account ↔ service agreement ↔ premise.
Reference to the customer account that holds this service agreement.

business_glossary_term: Service Delivery Asset Registry Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to asset.asset_registry. Business justification: Service agreements reference specific service delivery assets (transformer, switchgear) for capacity allocation, load management, and contract demand enforcement. Required for distribution capacity pl

Foreign key linking to customer.service_level_agreement. Business justification: Each customer service agreement is governed by a Service Level Agreement; adding FK captures this relationship and provides inbound link to service_level_agreement.

Reference to the competitive energy supplier or Community Choice Aggregator (CCA) providing generation service in deregulated markets. Null for bundled service where utility provides both delivery and generation.
reference: FERC Open Access Rules / State Retail Choice Programs

description: Externally visible business identifier for the service agreement, used in customer communications and billing statements.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Number / Oracle CC&B Service Agreement ID

description: Current lifecycle state of the service agreement. Draft indicates agreement is being prepared; pending approval awaiting credit or regulatory review; active means service is being delivered; suspended for temporary service interruption; terminated for completed agreements; cancelled for agreements that never went active.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Status / Oracle CC&B Service Agreement Status

description: Classification of the service agreement. Standard represents typical utility service; NEM (Net Energy Metering) for customers with behind-the-meter generation; DER interconnection for Distributed Energy Resource participants; community solar for shared renewable programs; green tariff for voluntary renewable energy purchase; special contract for negotiated large customer agreements.
reference: PURPA / State PUC Net Metering Rules

description: Indicates whether automatic payment is enabled for this service agreement, allowing bills to be paid automatically from customer bank account or credit card.
Billing cycle assignment determining when meter reads occur and bills are generated. Typically represents a monthly cycle number (e.g., cycle 01 reads on 1st of month, cycle 15 reads on 15th).
reference: SAP IS-U Billing Schedule / Oracle CC&B Bill Cycle

description: Indicates whether the customer is enrolled in budget billing program, which averages annual usage to provide consistent monthly payment amounts.

business_glossary_term: California Alternate Rates for Energy (CARE) Program Flag
description: Indicates enrollment in CARE or similar low-income assistance program providing discounted rates. CARE is California-specific; other states have equivalent programs (e.g., LIHEAP).

Contracted maximum demand in kilowatts (kW) for large commercial and industrial customers with demand-based rate schedules. Customer pays for this capacity regardless of actual usage. Null for non-demand customers.
Timestamp when this service agreement record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and compliance.
Dollar amount of security deposit held for this service agreement, typically required for customers with poor credit or no credit history. Null if no deposit required.

Reason why security deposit was waived if deposit amount is zero. Good credit for customers meeting credit score threshold; senior citizen, low income, or military for protected classes; prior customer for returning customers with good payment history; none if deposit was not waived.
Date when service agreement terminates and service delivery ends. Null for open-ended agreements. Populated when customer requests disconnection or agreement reaches contracted term end.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract End Date / Oracle CC&B Stop Date

description: Indicates whether premise has registered life support or medical equipment requiring continuous electric service. Provides special protections against disconnection and priority restoration during outages.

Statistical load profile classification used for non-interval metered customers to estimate hourly usage patterns for settlement and forecasting. Based on customer class and historical usage patterns.

Indicates whether this agreement covers master-metered service where a single meter serves multiple dwelling units (e.g., apartment building) and the property owner sub-meters or allocates costs to tenants.
Timestamp when this service agreement record was last modified. Audit field for change tracking and compliance.

Specific NEM (Net Energy Metering) program version if customer has behind-the-meter generation. NEM 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 represent California program generations; VNEM for virtual net metering; NEMBAT for NEM with battery storage. Not applicable for customers without generation.
reference: CPUC NEM Tariff / State Net Metering Rules

description: Indicates whether customer has opted for electronic bill delivery instead of paper statements.
Indicates whether customer currently has an active payment arrangement or installment plan for past due balances.

Minimum power factor (ratio of real to apparent power) required for large industrial customers. Typically 0.90 or higher. Customers below threshold may incur penalties. Null for customers without power factor requirements.

Tariff rate schedule code assigned to this agreement, determining pricing structure and billing rules. Examples include residential flat rate, commercial TOU (Time of Use), industrial demand-based, or CPP (Critical Peak Pricing) schedules.
reference: State PUC Approved Tariff / FERC Rate Schedule

description: Indicates whether this is a seasonal service agreement (e.g., vacation home, agricultural operation) with predictable periods of no usage and special billing rules.

Customer segment classification for regulatory reporting and rate design. Residential for households; commercial for businesses; industrial for manufacturing; agricultural for farms; municipal for government facilities; street lighting for public infrastructure.
reference: FERC Form 1 / State PUC Customer Class Definitions

description: Type of utility commodity delivered under this agreement. Electric for electricity service; gas for natural gas; water for potable water; steam and chilled water for district energy systems.

Voltage level at which electric service is delivered. Secondary for residential/small commercial (120/240V); primary for larger commercial (4-35kV); subtransmission (35-138kV); transmission for industrial customers (>138kV). Null for non-electric services.

Operational system of record from which this service agreement was sourced. SAP IS-U for SAP Industry Solution for Utilities; Oracle CC&B for Oracle Customer Care and Billing; legacy CIS for older customer information systems being migrated.
Native identifier of this service agreement in the source operational system. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and troubleshooting integration issues.
Date when service agreement becomes effective and service delivery begins. Corresponds to service turn-on date for new customers or agreement renewal date for existing customers.
reference: SAP IS-U Contract Start Date / Oracle CC&B Start Date

description: Reason for service agreement termination. Customer request for voluntary disconnection; move out when customer relocates; non-payment for involuntary disconnection; death of account holder; foreclosure for property repossession; service transfer when service moves to new account; contract expiration for fixed-term agreements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: customer_request|move_out|non_payment|death|foreclosure|service_transfer|contract_expiration — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Indicates whether customer has designated a third party (family member, social worker, advocate) to receive copies of disconnection notices and other critical communications.
Specific TOU (Time of Use) pricing plan code if the rate schedule includes time-differentiated pricing. Defines peak, off-peak, and shoulder period pricing structures.

Unique surrogate identifier for the move order record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service

description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_service_agreement. Business justification: Move order (move-in, move-out, transfer) should reference the service agreement being initiated or terminated. Currently move_order has account_id and premise_id but no service_agreement_id. This FK e

Reference to the field work order created in the asset/workforce management system (Ventyx Asset Suite) to execute the physical service connection, disconnection, or meter read associated with this move order. Links the CIS move order to the field operations domain.
reference: Ventyx Asset Suite Work Management; SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out

description: Reference to the meter device installed at the service point at the time of the move order. Used to schedule move-in/move-out meter reads and link final read values to the correct device record in the Metering domain.
reference: SAP IS-U Device Management; Oracle Utilities MDM; AMI infrastructure standards

description: Reference to the specific service point (metering point / point of delivery) at the premise where service is being initiated or terminated. A premise may have multiple service points (e.g., electric and gas).
reference: SAP IS-U Connection Object; Oracle CC&B Service Point; NAESB Retail Electric Provider standards

description: FK to customer.account.account_id — Move orders initiate/terminate service for an account. move_order.account_id → account.account_id.
Reference to the service premise (physical location) at which the move order is being executed. Central linkage to the premise master record for address, meter, and distribution asset context.
reference: SAP IS-U Premise Management; Oracle CC&B Premise; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network

description: Reference to the existing service account being closed or vacated as part of this move order. Populated for move-out and transfer order types. Used to trigger final bill generation and deposit disposition in the billing domain.
reference: SAP IS-U EVER; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service

description: Reference to the customer party initiating the move order. Links to the customer master record in the Customer domain. For a transfer, this is the incoming customer (move-in party).
reference: SAP IS-U Business Partner; Oracle CC&B Customer Management

description: Reference to the account of the previous occupant at the premise, if known at the time of the move-in order. Used to coordinate final bill issuance for the departing customer and to identify any outstanding balance or deposit transfer obligations.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service

description: FK to customer.premise.premise_id — Move orders reference the premise where service starts/stops. move_order.premise_id → premise.premise_id.

Indicates whether the customer is enrolled in a budget billing (levelized payment) plan at the time of the move order. When true, the final bill calculation must account for any budget billing true-up balance upon move-out.
reference: SAP IS-U Billing; Oracle CC&B Billing; State PUC budget billing tariff rules

description: Free-text or coded reason explaining why the move order was cancelled or rejected. Populated only when order_status is 'cancelled' or 'rejected'. Used for operational quality analysis and customer service improvement.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service

description: The customer engagement channel through which the move order was submitted. Supports multi-channel analytics and CRM reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: web_portal|mobile_app|call_center|walk_in|field_crew|ivr|third_party — promote to reference product]
reference: Oracle CC&B Customer Management; SAP IS-U CIS; CRM channel analytics standards

description: The date and time when the move order was fully completed and all downstream actions (meter read, billing, account activation/deactivation) were confirmed. Distinct from effective_date (the business date of service change) and submitted_timestamp (when the order was placed).
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service; State PUC SLA requirements

description: Audit timestamp recording when this move order record was first created in the Silver layer data store. Distinct from submitted_timestamp which reflects the business event time.
reference: SOX Section 404; NERC CIP-007 audit logging requirements

description: Indicates whether a credit check was required for this move-in or transfer order based on the customer's credit classification or account history. When true, the move order may be held pending credit review and deposit determination per SAP IS-U FICA or Oracle CC&B Collections rules.
reference: SAP IS-U FICA; Oracle CC&B Collections; State PUC credit and deposit regulations

description: The outcome of the credit check performed for this move order. Not_required: credit check was not triggered. Passed: customer met credit criteria. Failed: customer did not meet criteria (deposit required). Pending: check in progress. Waived: credit check bypassed per business rules (e.g., existing customer in good standing).
reference: SAP IS-U FICA; Oracle CC&B Collections; State PUC credit regulations

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code applicable to all monetary amounts on this move order (deposit_amount, final_bill_amount). Typically USD for North American utilities. Supports multi-currency operations for utilities with international operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FERC financial reporting standards; SOX

description: Indicates whether the customer or premise is enrolled in a Demand Response (DR) program at the time of the move order. When true, the DR program administrator must be notified to update enrollment records and avoid erroneous dispatch signals.
reference: FERC Order 745; State PUC DR program rules; DOE demand response guidelines

description: The monetary value of the security deposit associated with the prior or new account at the time of the move order. Used to determine deposit disposition (refund, transfer, or application to final bill balance) upon move-out or transfer.
reference: SAP IS-U FICA; Oracle CC&B Collections; State PUC deposit regulations

description: The outcome or planned treatment of the security deposit upon move-out or transfer. Refund: returned to customer. Applied_to_balance: offset against outstanding final bill. Transferred: moved to new account. Forfeited: retained by utility per tariff terms. Pending: disposition not yet determined.
reference: SAP IS-U FICA; Oracle CC&B Collections; State PUC deposit regulations

description: Indicates whether the premise associated with this move order has an active Distributed Energy Resource (DER) enrollment (e.g., battery storage, EV charger, demand response program). When true, triggers DERMS notification and DER agreement review upon move-out or transfer.
reference: FERC Order 2222; State PUC DER interconnection rules; DERMS integration standards

description: The actual date on which the service change (move-in, move-out, or transfer) became effective at the premise. Used as the billing boundary date for final bill generation and new account activation. May differ from requested_date due to scheduling constraints or field execution timing.
reference: SAP IS-U EVER; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service; FERC billing standards; State PUC tariff requirements

description: The total monetary amount of the final bill generated as a result of the move-out or transfer order. Represents the net amount owed by or to the customer after applying the final meter read, applicable tariff rates, taxes, and deposit disposition.
reference: SAP IS-U Billing; Oracle CC&B Billing; State PUC tariff requirements; SOX financial reporting

description: The meter register reading (in kWh or applicable unit) captured at the time of the move order. For move-out, this is the closing read used to calculate the final bill. For move-in, this is the opening read establishing the new billing baseline.
reference: SAP IS-U Device Management; Oracle Utilities MDM; ANSI C12.20 metering accuracy standards

description: Indicates whether the property owner or landlord must be notified of the service change per tariff rules or regulatory requirements. Relevant for rental properties where the landlord has a standing notification agreement with the utility.
reference: State PUC landlord notification tariff rules; Oracle CC&B Customer Management

description: The date on which the landlord or property owner was notified of the service change associated with this move order. Populated only when landlord_notification_required is true. Used for regulatory compliance documentation.
reference: State PUC landlord notification tariff rules; Oracle CC&B Customer Management

description: Indicates whether the customer has an approved medical baseline allowance (life support or medical necessity designation) that requires special handling during service disconnection or move-out. When true, additional notification and regulatory compliance steps are required before service termination.
reference: State PUC medical baseline tariff rules; CPUC Rule 14; DOE energy assistance guidelines

description: The date on which the meter was physically or remotely read in connection with this move order. Used as the billing cut-off date for the final bill (move-out) or the start-of-service read date (move-in). Sourced from Oracle Utilities MDM or SAP IS-U Device Management.
reference: SAP IS-U Device Management; Oracle Utilities MDM; State PUC metering standards

description: Indicates whether the customer associated with this move order is enrolled in a Net Energy Metering (NEM) program, typically due to rooftop solar or other behind-the-meter (BTM) generation. When true, triggers specialized NEM billing and interconnection review processes upon move-in or move-out.
reference: FERC PURPA; State PUC NEM tariff rules; CPUC NEM 2.0/3.0 regulations

description: Externally-known business identifier for the move order, assigned by the source system (SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B). Used for customer-facing correspondence and cross-system reconciliation.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service

description: Current lifecycle state of the move order workflow. Pending: submitted but not yet processed. In_progress: actively being executed (meter read scheduled, field crew dispatched). Completed: service change fully effected. Cancelled: withdrawn before execution. Rejected: failed validation or business rules.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service

description: Classifies the nature of the service order: move_in (new service activation at a premise), move_out (service termination at a premise), transfer (simultaneous move-out and move-in for a change of occupant), reconnect (restoration of previously disconnected service), or disconnect (non-payment or voluntary disconnection). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: move_in|move_out|transfer|reconnect|disconnect — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
reference: SAP IS-U EVER; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service; NAESB Retail Electric Provider standards

description: The tariff rate schedule code assigned to the new service account upon move-in or transfer. Determines the billing rate class (e.g., residential, small commercial, large industrial, TOU, CPP). Sourced from the applicable PUC-approved tariff.
reference: SAP IS-U Rate Management; Oracle CC&B Rates; State PUC tariff filings; FERC OATT

description: Indicates how the move-order meter read was obtained: actual (field technician physical read), estimated (calculated based on usage history when actual read is unavailable), AMI_remote (automated read via Advanced Metering Infrastructure), or customer_self_read (customer-reported reading).
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM VEE rules; SAP IS-U Device Management; State PUC metering standards

description: The unit of measure for the final_read_value. Typically kWh for electric meters, but may be therms, CCF, or MCF for gas service points. Ensures correct interpretation of the meter read value across commodity types.
reference: SAP IS-U Device Management; Oracle Utilities MDM; ANSI C12.20; NAESB standards

description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or exceptions associated with this move order. May include field crew instructions, customer-specific handling notes, or escalation details entered by customer service representatives.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service

description: The date the customer requested the service change to take effect. This is the customer-stated desired effective date, which may differ from the actual effective date after scheduling and field execution.
reference: SAP IS-U EVER; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service; State PUC service connection standards

description: The date on which the meter read associated with this move order is scheduled to be performed. May differ from meter_read_date (actual read date) if the read is rescheduled or delayed. Used for field crew scheduling and MDM read request management.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM; SAP IS-U Device Management; State PUC metering standards

description: Customer service classification at the time of the move order, determining applicable tariff, billing rules, and regulatory reporting category. Residential, small commercial, large commercial, industrial, agricultural, or lighting.
reference: SAP IS-U Rate Management; Oracle CC&B Customer Class; State PUC tariff classifications; FERC Form 1

description: Code identifying the utility's regulated service territory within which the premise is located. Used for regulatory reporting to State PUCs, FERC Form 1 filings, and NERC reliability reporting. Determines applicable tariff jurisdiction.
reference: FERC Form 1; State PUC service territory maps; NERC reliability reporting

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this move order record was sourced. SAP_IS-U: SAP Industry Solution for Utilities. Oracle_CCB: Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing. Manual: entered directly into the data platform. Used for data lineage and reconciliation.
reference: SAP IS-U; Oracle CC&B; Enterprise Data Governance standards

description: The native primary key or order identifier from the originating operational system (SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B). Enables traceability back to the source system record for audit, reconciliation, and issue resolution.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service; SOX audit trail requirements

description: The date and time when the move order was first submitted into the CIS system (SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B). Represents the principal business event timestamp for order creation. Used for SLA tracking and order aging analysis.
reference: SAP IS-U Move-In/Move-Out; Oracle CC&B Start/Stop Service

description: Audit timestamp recording when this move order record was most recently modified in the Silver layer data store. Used for change data capture and incremental processing.
reference: SOX Section 404; NERC CIP-007 audit logging requirements

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the physical service location (premise) within the utility's Customer Information System (CIS). Primary key for all premise-level metering, billing, and outage management references. Role: MASTER_RESOURCE.
reference: SAP IS-U Premise Object; Oracle CC&B Premise Entity

description: Identifier of the distribution transformer bank serving the premise, as recorded in the utility's asset management system (Ventyx Asset Suite) and GIS. Used for transformer loading analysis, outage impact assessment, and asset maintenance planning.
reference: Ventyx Asset Suite; Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; IEEE C57 Transformer Standards

Identifier of the meter reading route to which the premise is assigned for field meter reading operations. Used for route optimization, meter reader scheduling, and AMI walk-by/drive-by reading coordination in Oracle Utilities MDM.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Meter Reading Route; SAP IS-U Meter Reading Order

Indicates whether the premise is eligible for Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meter deployment based on infrastructure readiness, service voltage, and utility AMI rollout program criteria. Drives meter deployment prioritization in Oracle Utilities MDM.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM AMI Deployment; DOE Smart Grid Investment Grant Standards; State PUC AMI Deployment Orders

description: Code identifying the billing cycle to which the premise is assigned, determining meter reading schedule and bill generation frequency. Sourced from SAP IS-U Billing Cycle or Oracle CC&B Bill Cycle configuration.
reference: SAP IS-U Billing Cycle; Oracle CC&B Bill Cycle; State PUC Billing Frequency Rules

description: Detailed structural classification of the premise beyond the high-level premise type. Used for load profile modeling, infrastructure planning, and demand response program eligibility.
