reference: Oracle CC&B Premise Classification; SAP IS-U Premise Category Detail

description: Climate zone designation assigned to the premise based on geographic location and DOE/ASHRAE climate classification. Used for energy efficiency program targeting, demand response (DR) program design, Integrated Resource Planning (IRP), and Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) compliance analysis.
reference: DOE Building Energy Codes; ASHRAE 90.1 Climate Zone Map; State PUC Energy Efficiency Program Rules

description: Year the premise structure was originally constructed. Used for energy efficiency program eligibility assessment, weatherization program targeting, load profile modeling, and infrastructure age analysis. Sourced from county assessor records or customer-provided data.
reference: DOE Weatherization Assistance Program; State PUC Energy Efficiency Program Standards

description: Timestamp when the premise record was first created in the source CIS system (SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B). Provides audit trail for data governance, regulatory compliance, and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; NERC CIP-007 System Security Management; SAP IS-U Audit Log

description: Indicates whether the premise is designated as a critical facility (e.g., hospital, emergency services, water treatment plant, telecommunications hub) requiring priority restoration during outages. Drives outage management system (OMS) prioritization and mutual aid planning.
reference: GE PowerOn ADMS OMS Critical Customer; NERC CIP Critical Infrastructure Protection; State PUC Critical Facility Designation Rules

description: Indicates whether the premise has an active Distributed Energy Resource (DER) enrollment, including rooftop solar, battery storage, or other behind-the-meter (BTM) generation assets registered in the utility's Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS). Supports Virtual Power Plant (VPP) aggregation and demand response programs.
reference: FERC Order 2222 DER Aggregation; State PUC DER Interconnection Rules; IEEE 1547; DERMS Integration Standards

description: Indicates whether the premise has a registered electric vehicle (EV) charging installation. Used for distribution load forecasting, EV rate schedule eligibility, demand response program targeting, and grid modernization planning.
reference: State PUC EV Rate Tariffs; DOE EV Infrastructure Standards; IEEE 2030.1.1 EV Charging Standards

description: Total conditioned floor area of the premise structure in square feet. Used for energy intensity benchmarking (kWh per square foot), energy efficiency program eligibility, demand response capacity estimation, and load profile normalization.
reference: DOE Commercial Buildings Energy Consumption Survey (CBECS); EPA ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager

description: Assessor's parcel number or GIS parcel identifier linking the premise to the county tax assessor's spatial parcel layer in Esri ArcGIS Utility Network. Enables land-use analysis, property boundary correlation, and infrastructure planning.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; County Assessor Parcel Standards

description: Date of the most recent utility field inspection of the premise's service entrance, metering equipment, or electrical infrastructure. Used for compliance tracking, safety program management, and asset maintenance scheduling in Ventyx Asset Suite.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Electrical Safety Standards; State PUC Safety Inspection Requirements; Ventyx Asset Suite Inspection Records

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the premise record in the source CIS system. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change data capture (CDC), and audit trail maintenance per SOX and NERC CIP requirements.
reference: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; NERC CIP-007; SAP IS-U Change Document; Oracle CC&B Audit Log

description: Geographic latitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the physical service location as recorded in the utility's Geographic Information System (GIS). Used for outage management spatial analysis, field crew routing, and distribution network modeling in Esri ArcGIS Utility Network.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; IEEE 1547 Interconnection Standards

description: Indicates whether a registered life-support equipment user resides at the premise. Triggers disconnection protection, priority outage notification, and special field crew protocols per state PUC regulations. Distinct from medical_baseline_flag which governs billing treatment.
reference: State PUC Life Support Equipment Rules; CPUC General Order 111-G; Oracle CC&B Life Support Configuration

description: Current operational state of the premise within the utility's service portfolio. Drives eligibility for new service connections, billing activation, and outage management inclusion. Active premises are energized and receiving service; decommissioned premises have been permanently removed from service.
reference: SAP IS-U Premise Status; Oracle CC&B Premise Status

description: Utility-assigned load profile class code used to model the premise's expected energy consumption pattern for billing, forecasting, and settlement purposes. Applied to non-interval-metered customers for load research and wholesale market settlement. Sourced from Oracle Utilities MDM or SAP IS-U.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM Load Profile; NERC Load Forecasting Standards; FERC Settlement Procedures

description: Geographic longitude coordinate (WGS84 decimal degrees) of the physical service location as recorded in the utility's Geographic Information System (GIS). Used in conjunction with latitude for spatial analysis, outage polygon mapping, and DER interconnection planning.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Utility Network; WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; IEEE 1547 Interconnection Standards

description: Indicates whether the premise has a registered medical baseline allowance due to a life-support or medical necessity condition. Triggers special billing treatment, outage notification priority, and disconnection protection protocols per state PUC regulations.
reference: State PUC Medical Baseline Tariff Rules; CPUC Rule 11 (California); Oracle CC&B Medical Baseline Configuration

description: Number of meter sockets (meter points) installed at the premise. Multi-socket premises include multi-family dwellings, commercial complexes, and industrial facilities with multiple service points. Drives meter deployment planning in Oracle Utilities MDM and SAP IS-U Device Management.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM; SAP IS-U Device Management; ANSI C12.1 Electric Meters Standards

description: Indicates whether the premise is eligible for Net Energy Metering (NEM) based on service territory rules, interconnection capacity, and applicable state PUC tariff provisions. Supports Distributed Energy Resource (DER) enrollment and behind-the-meter (BTM) generation tracking.
reference: State PUC NEM Tariff Rules; FERC PURPA; IEEE 1547 Interconnection Standard; SAP IS-U NEM Configuration

description: Number of individual dwelling or tenant units within the premise. Applicable to multi-family, high-rise, and mixed-use premises. Used for per-unit load analysis, master-metered billing allocation, and demand response program enrollment capacity.
reference: Oracle CC&B Multi-Unit Premise Configuration; SAP IS-U Premise Unit Count

description: Recorded or estimated peak electrical demand in kilowatts (kW) for the premise. Used for transformer sizing, distribution capacity planning, demand charge billing, and demand response (DR) program baseline establishment. Sourced from Oracle Utilities MDM interval data or SAP IS-U demand registers.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM; SAP IS-U Demand Register; NERC Load Forecasting; State PUC Demand Charge Tariffs

description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the premise as assigned by the utility's CIS (SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B). Used in field operations, customer correspondence, and cross-system integration. Corresponds to SAP IS-U Premise Number or Oracle CC&B Premise ID.
reference: SAP IS-U Premise Number; Oracle Utilities CC&B Premise Identifier

description: High-level classification of the premise by customer segment and land use. Drives rate schedule eligibility, load profile assignment, and regulatory reporting segmentation. reference: FERC Form 1; EIA-861 Customer Class Definitions; SAP IS-U Premise Category

description: Utility tariff rate schedule code applicable to the premise, as defined in the state PUC-approved tariff and configured in SAP IS-U or Oracle CC&B. Determines energy charge structure, demand charges, TOU periods, and applicable riders.
reference: State PUC Approved Tariff Schedules; SAP IS-U Rate Category; Oracle CC&B Rate Schedule

reference: SAP IS-U Connection Object; Oracle CC&B Premise Deactivation; State PUC Service Termination Rules

description: Date on which utility service was first activated at the premise. Establishes the premise's service history baseline for billing, regulatory reporting, and infrastructure age analysis.
reference: SAP IS-U Connection Object; Oracle CC&B Premise Service Start; State PUC Service Commencement Rules

description: Utility-defined code identifying the franchised service territory zone in which the premise is located. Determines applicable tariff schedules, regulatory jurisdiction (PUC), and operational responsibility. Sourced from SAP IS-U Division or Oracle CC&B Service Territory.
reference: State PUC Franchise Territory Certificates (CPCN); FERC Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT); SAP IS-U Division

Critical for rate design and OATT compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: secondary_120v|secondary_240v|primary_4kv|primary_12kv|primary_25kv|transmission — promote to reference product]
reference: FERC OATT; State PUC Rate Schedules; IEEE C84.1 Voltage Standards; ANSI C12.1

description: Indicates whether the premise qualifies for Time of Use (TOU) or Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate schedules based on metering capability (AMI), service class, and applicable PUC tariff provisions. Drives rate schedule assignment and customer enrollment workflows.
reference: State PUC TOU/CPP Tariff Schedules; Oracle CC&B Rate Schedule Eligibility; SAP IS-U Rate Determination

Unique identifier for this aggregation contract record. Primary key.
Foreign key linking to the demand response aggregator party in this aggregation contract
Foreign key linking to the distributed energy resource system being aggregated under this contract
Financial account or sub-account identifier used for revenue settlements specific to this aggregation contract. Enables tracking of payments and reconciliation at the individual DER system level.

Current operational status of this specific aggregation contract. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. Indicates whether the DER system is actively participating, pending approval, temporarily suspended, or no longer aggregated.

Specific baseline calculation methodology agreed upon for this aggregation contract to measure demand response performance. May differ from the aggregators default methodology based on DER system characteristics or program requirements.
Reference identifier or URI to the legal contract document governing this specific aggregation relationship, stored in the document management system.

The specific capacity in kilowatts that this DER system has committed to provide under this aggregation contract. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. This is distinct from the DER systems total nameplate capacity, as a system may allocate different capacities to different aggregators or reserve capacity for on-site use.
System timestamp when this aggregation contract record was created in the data platform.

Numeric priority ranking for dispatch instructions when the DER system is aggregated by multiple aggregators. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Ensures conflict resolution when multiple aggregators attempt to dispatch the same resource simultaneously.
Scheduled or actual end date when the DER system exits the aggregators portfolio, either due to contract expiration, customer withdrawal, or system decommissioning.

Classification of the DER systems performance obligations and incentive structure under this aggregation contract. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. Higher tiers may require faster response times, higher availability, or more frequent dispatch capability in exchange for higher compensation.

Percentage of demand response revenues or incentive payments that the DER system owner receives from this aggregation contract. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. The remainder goes to the aggregator as compensation for market participation services.
Effective start date when the DER system was enrolled into the aggregators portfolio under this specific contract. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

Required frequency in seconds at which the DER system must report real-time operational data (power output, state of charge, availability status) to the aggregators platform for this contract. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. Different aggregators or programs may require different telemetry frequencies (e.g., 15 seconds for ISO/RTO markets, 5 minutes for utility programs).
User or system identifier that last modified this aggregation contract record.
System timestamp when this aggregation contract record was last modified.
User or system identifier that created this aggregation contract record.
Unique identifier for the demand response enrollment record. Primary key for the DR enrollment entity.
Reference to the customer account enrolled in the demand response program. Links to the customer account master record in the Customer Information System (CIS).

Reference to the third-party demand response aggregator managing this customer enrollment on behalf of the utility. Null for direct utility-managed enrollments. Links to the aggregator master record defining aggregator contracts, settlement terms, and performance obligations.

Reference to the specific demand response program in which the customer is enrolled. Links to the DR program master record defining program rules, incentives, and dispatch protocols.

Foreign key linking to interconnection.application. Business justification: Customer DR enrollment requires completed interconnection for behind-the-meter DER. Enrollment verification validates interconnection approval status and export capacity limits. ISO/RTO registration a

Reference to the interruptible tariff agreement contract that governs the terms, conditions, and compensation for load curtailment. Links to the tariff agreement master record defining rate discounts, curtailment obligations, and penalty provisions.

Foreign key linking to supply.material_master. Business justification: Enrollments track specific equipment installed at customer premises (thermostats, control switches). Business process: asset tracking, warranty management, spare parts planning, equipment lifecycle ma

Reference to the Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) meter device used to measure interval load data for baseline calculation and measurement and verification (M&V). Links to the meter device master record in Meter Data Management (MDM).
Reference to the physical service delivery point where demand response load curtailment will be measured. Links to the service point master record in the Customer Information System (CIS).

The average actual load curtailment in kilowatts (kW) achieved by the customer across all participated DR events during the current enrollment period. Used for program performance analysis and capacity planning.

Indicates whether day-of or morning-of baseline adjustments are enabled for this enrollment to account for real-time load variations. True: adjustments are applied. False: unadjusted baseline is used for M&V.

The methodology used to calculate the customer baseline load (CBL) for measurement and verification (M&V) of load curtailment performance. High X of Y: average of highest X days in prior Y days. Mid X of Y: average of middle X days in prior Y days. Regression: statistical regression model. Control Group: comparison to similar non-participating customers. Meter Before Meter After: direct comparison of meter readings.

Indicates whether this enrollment is registered to participate in the ISO/RTO capacity market and is eligible to receive capacity payments for committed load reduction. True: participating in capacity market. False: energy-only or retail program participation.
The date and time when this enrollment record was first created in the data platform. System-generated audit timestamp for data lineage and compliance.

Indicates whether the utility has direct load control capability to remotely curtail customer load via smart thermostats, water heaters, or other controllable devices. True: DLC enabled. False: behavioral or manual curtailment only.

The committed load reduction capacity in kilowatts (kW) that the customer has enrolled to curtail during demand response events. This is the System of Record (SSOT) for enrolled capacity reported to ISO/RTO for capacity market settlements and to PUC for program performance audits.

The channel or method through which the customer enrolled in the demand response program. Web Portal: customer self-service online. Mobile App: enrollment via utility mobile application. Call Center: enrollment via customer service representative. Field Enrollment: enrollment by field agent or installer. Aggregator: enrollment through third-party demand response aggregator. Auto Enrollment: automatic enrollment based on rate class or program rules. Utility Initiated: proactive enrollment by utility for targeted customers. The date on which the demand response enrollment becomes active and the customer becomes eligible to participate in DR events and receive incentive payments. Must align with program enrollment windows and ISO/RTO capacity commitment deadlines.

The date on which the demand response enrollment expires and the customer is no longer eligible for DR event dispatch or incentive payments. Null for open-ended enrollments subject to annual renewal or customer opt-out.

Business-facing unique enrollment number assigned to the customer for this DR program participation. Used in customer communications, billing statements, and regulatory reporting. Format: DR-XXXXXXXXXX.
The name of the operational system of record from which this enrollment record originated. Examples: SAP IS-U, Oracle CC&B, proprietary DR management system, aggregator platform.
The unique identifier of this enrollment record in the source operational system. Used for data lineage traceability and reconciliation with upstream systems.

Current lifecycle status of the demand response enrollment. Pending: enrollment submitted but not yet active. Active: enrollment is in effect and customer is eligible for DR events. Suspended: temporarily inactive due to non-compliance or customer request. Terminated: enrollment ended by utility or customer. Expired: enrollment period ended. Opted Out: customer exercised opt-out right.
The date and time when the customer enrollment was submitted and recorded in the system. Represents the business event time of enrollment initiation, distinct from audit timestamps.

business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Registration Identifier
description: The unique registration identifier assigned by the ISO or RTO for this demand response resource enrollment. Used for wholesale market participation, capacity market bidding, and settlement reconciliation with the ISO/RTO.
The date of the most recent opt-out event when the customer declined to participate in a dispatched DR event. Null if the customer has never opted out during the current enrollment period.
The date and time when this enrollment record was most recently modified in the data platform. System-generated audit timestamp for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

The minimum advance notice time in minutes required to notify the customer before a demand response event dispatch. Defined by program rules and customer agreement. Typical values range from 15 minutes to 24 hours.

The customer preferred method for receiving demand response event notifications and dispatch alerts. Email: email notification. SMS: text message. Phone: automated phone call. Mobile App: push notification via utility mobile app. None: no notification requested.

The cumulative number of times the customer has exercised their opt-out right to decline participation in a dispatched DR event during the current enrollment period. Used to track customer engagement and enforce program opt-out limits.

The percentage of dispatched DR events in which the customer successfully participated and achieved the required load curtailment during the current enrollment period. Calculated as (successful events / total dispatched events) * 100. Used for program performance reporting and customer incentive tier determination.

Indicates whether this enrollment must be included in Public Utility Commission (PUC) demand response program participation and performance reports. True: include in PUC reporting. False: exclude from regulatory reporting.

Indicates whether real-time telemetry data from the customer meter or behind-the-meter (BTM) devices is enabled for this enrollment to support real-time dispatch verification and settlement. True: telemetry enabled. False: interval data only.
The date on which the enrollment was terminated. Null for active, pending, or suspended enrollments. Populated when enrollment status transitions to terminated.

The reason code for enrollment termination when enrollment status is terminated. Customer Request: customer voluntarily withdrew. Non-Compliance: customer failed to meet program requirements. Program Ended: DR program was discontinued. Account Closed: customer account was closed. Moved: customer moved out of service territory. Aggregator Change: customer switched to different aggregator. Other: other termination reason. The cumulative total of all incentive payments in United States Dollars (USD) paid to the customer for demand response participation during the current enrollment period. Includes capacity payments, energy payments, and performance bonuses.

Indicates whether this enrollment is part of a Virtual Power Plant (VPP) aggregation that dispatches distributed energy resources (DER) as a single coordinated resource. True: enrolled in VPP. False: standalone DR enrollment.

Current lifecycle status of this specific enrollment. Active indicates the DER is eligible for dispatch. Suspended indicates temporary ineligibility. Withdrawn indicates permanent termination. Pending indicates enrollment application under review. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

Numeric priority ranking (1=highest) determining the order in which this DER system is dispatched during DR events for this program. Priority may be based on response reliability, capacity size, location, or contractual terms. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Date when this enrollment is scheduled to terminate. Null for open-ended enrollments. Supports tracking of enrollment history and program participation lifecycle.
Date when this enrollment becomes operationally effective and the DER system can be dispatched under this program. May differ from enrollment_date if there is a waiting period or future start date.

Calculated performance score (0-100) measuring this DER system's historical response reliability and load reduction accuracy for this specific DR program. Used for dispatch priority optimization and incentive adjustments.

The baseline calculation methodology applied to this specific DER system for this specific DR program. May override or refine the program's default baseline_calculation_method based on DER technology type or customer agreement. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

Technical configuration specifying how real-time telemetry data from this DER system is collected, transmitted, and processed for this DR program. Includes polling frequency, communication protocol, data points monitored, and aggregation rules. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.
Cumulative hours this DER system has been dispatched under this program since enrollment. Supports compliance tracking against max_event_hours_per_year program limits.
Cumulative count of DR events in which this DER system has been dispatched under this program since enrollment. Supports compliance tracking against max_events_per_year program limits.
System timestamp when this enrollment record was last modified.

Unique identifier for the demand response event participant record. Primary key for this transactional entity linking a customer, aggregated resource, or Direct Load Control (DLC) device to a specific DR event.
Reference to the customer account participating in the DR event. Used for billing, incentive payment processing, and customer-level performance aggregation.
Reference to the third-party aggregator managing this participant resource. Used for wholesale market DR programs and aggregated DER portfolios. Null for utility-direct programs.

Reference to the customer enrollment record that authorized participation in this DR event. Links to the active enrollment in the DR program at the time of event dispatch.

Reference to the specific Direct Load Control (DLC) device or Distributed Energy Resource (DER) that was dispatched during the event. Applicable for DLC programs, smart thermostats, battery storage, and VPP resources. Null for behavioral DR programs.
FK to demand.dr_event.dr_event_id — Core header-line relationship. Every participant record must reference the event it responds to. Required for event-level curtailment aggregation.

Reference to the physical premise location where the DR event participation occurred. Used for geographic analysis, load zone aggregation, and distribution system impact assessment.

Reference to the parent DR event that this participant record is associated with. Links to the specific dispatch event across all DR program types (DLC, behavioral, interruptible, VPP, wholesale market).
FK to demand.dr_event.dr_event_id — Every participant response record must reference the event it responds to. This is the core header-to-line relationship for DR event performance tracking.

Date and time when the participant device or system acknowledged receipt of the dispatch command. Used to measure communication latency and confirm successful command delivery for DLC and VPP resources.

Measured actual load in kilowatts consumed by the participant during the DR event window. Sourced from Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) interval data or SCADA telemetry for real-time measurement.

Methodology used to calculate the baseline load for this participant. Common methods include high X of Y days, regression-based, or control group comparison. Must align with program rules and regulatory requirements for Measurement and Verification (M&V).

Calculated baseline load in kilowatts representing what the participant would have consumed absent the DR event. Used as the reference point for measuring actual curtailment performance. Calculated using the baseline methodology specified in the program rules.

Load reduction in kilowatts that the participant committed to provide during the DR event. Used for interruptible tariff, VPP, and wholesale market programs where participants bid or contract specific curtailment amounts.
Date and time when this participant event record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and record lifecycle tracking.
Total duration in minutes that the participant actively curtailed load during the DR event. Used for calculating energy reduction (kWh) and validating minimum participation requirements.
Indicator of the quality and reliability of the meter data used for performance measurement. Flags estimated or missing interval data that may affect settlement accuracy and require manual review.
Type of control command issued to the DLC device or DER during the event. Applicable for direct load control programs. Null for behavioral and interruptible tariff programs.
Date and time when the DR event dispatch command was issued to this participant. Represents the moment the utility or aggregator initiated the curtailment request or device control signal.

Total energy reduction in kilowatt-hours achieved by the participant during the DR event, calculated as measured curtailment (kW) multiplied by duration (hours). Used for program impact reporting and wholesale market settlement.

Calculated engagement score for behavioral DR participants based on notification interaction (open, click, response). Used for segmentation, targeted messaging, and gamification strategies to improve participation rates.
Categorized reason for participant non-response or under-performance during the DR event. Used for root cause analysis, device maintenance prioritization, and program improvement initiatives.

Calculated incentive payment amount in local currency earned by the participant for this DR event based on measured curtailment, program rate structure, and performance ratio. Subject to final settlement and adjustment.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the incentive payment amount. Supports multi-currency operations for utilities operating across international jurisdictions.

Boolean indicator of whether this participant performance qualifies for incentive payment based on program rules, minimum performance thresholds, and compliance requirements. False indicates disqualification due to non-performance or rule violation.

Actual measured load reduction in kilowatts achieved by the participant during the DR event, calculated as baseline load minus actual load. This is the verified performance used for incentive payment calculation and program reporting.

Measurement and Verification method applied to validate the participant curtailment performance. Determines the data sources and calculation approach used for performance settlement and regulatory reporting.

Boolean indicator of whether a penalty applies to this participant for failing to meet committed curtailment obligations. Applicable for interruptible tariff and wholesale market programs with contractual performance requirements.

Communication channel used to notify or dispatch this participant. For behavioral DR: notification method. For DLC: control protocol. Used for engagement analysis and communication effectiveness tracking.
Status of the event notification delivery to the participant for behavioral DR programs. Tracks email, SMS, or mobile app notification delivery confirmation and engagement.

Primary key for workforce_crew_dispatch
Unique surrogate identifier for each crew dispatch record. Primary key for the association.

Foreign key linking to the crew master record. Supports queries like 'show all outages this crew responded to' and enables crew performance analysis including average response time and restoration effectiveness.

Foreign key linking to the outage event record for which this crew was dispatched. Supports queries like 'show all crews assigned to this outage' and enables aggregation of crew resources per event for major storm analysis.

Calculated field: actual response time in minutes from dispatch to arrival (arrival_timestamp - dispatch_timestamp). Used for crew performance benchmarking, OMS dispatch optimization, and regulatory reporting of emergency response effectiveness.

Calculated field: actual work duration in minutes from work start to completion (work_completed_timestamp - work_start_timestamp). Used for labor cost allocation, crew productivity analysis, and validation of OMS restoration time estimates.

Timestamp when the crew arrived at the outage site, typically recorded via mobile device GPS check-in or crew foreman confirmation. Used to calculate actual response time (arrival - dispatch) for OMS performance metrics and IEEE 1366 reporting.
Timestamp when the crew dispatch record was first created in the OMS or data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

Classification of crew type dispatched to this outage. Captured at dispatch time to support analysis of crew type effectiveness by outage cause and to validate that appropriate crew skills were assigned. Values align with workforce.crew.crew_type enumeration.

Numeric priority ranking assigned to this dispatch at time of assignment. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Determined by outage severity, customer count, critical infrastructure impact, and restoration sequence optimization. Used by OMS to manage crew reassignment during major storm events when new high-priority outages emerge.
Source or actor that initiated this crew dispatch. Supports analysis of automated vs. manual dispatch effectiveness and audit trail for crew assignment decisions during major events.

Current lifecycle status of the crew dispatch assignment. Transitions tracked in OMS for real-time crew location awareness and restoration progress monitoring. Values: DISPATCHED (crew notified), EN_ROUTE (crew traveling), ON_SITE (crew arrived), WORKING (active restoration), COMPLETED (work finished), CANCELLED (dispatch cancelled before arrival), REASSIGNED (crew redirected to higher priority event).
Timestamp when the crew was officially dispatched to the outage event by the OMS dispatcher or automated dispatch system. Start of the dispatch lifecycle and baseline for response time calculation.

Estimated travel time in minutes from crew location to outage site at time of dispatch. Calculated by OMS using GPS location and routing algorithms. Used to set initial ETR communicated to customers and to optimize crew assignment decisions.

Free-text notes entered by crew foreman or field supervisor documenting site conditions, work performed, materials used, safety incidents, or reasons for delays. Critical for post-storm after-action review, cause validation, and continuous improvement of OMS predictive models.
Free-text explanation if crew was reassigned or dispatch was cancelled before completion. Documents operational decisions during dynamic storm restoration when priorities shift rapidly.
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the crew dispatch record. Supports change data capture and real-time OMS dashboard refresh.

Identifier of the vehicle used by the crew for this dispatch. Captured for GPS tracking integration, equipment utilization analysis, and mutual aid reimbursement documentation. May reference workforce vehicle master or be free-text for contractor/mutual aid vehicles.
Timestamp when the crew completed their assigned restoration work and cleared the site. Used to calculate crew work duration, support ETR accuracy analysis, and close the dispatch record in OMS.

Timestamp when the crew began active restoration work on the outage. May differ from arrival time due to site assessment, safety briefing, or waiting for switching orders. Used for labor cost allocation and work duration analysis.
